title: build-deck.js: slide backgrounds lost crossorigin, breaking cross-origin PNG export
description: REGRESSION, pre-dates the Moonshot work — found while running quality gates on 2026-08-02, not caused by that branch. SYMPTOM: agent/tests/test_publish.py::test_render_invokes_real_build_deck fails. It asserts crossorigin="anonymous" appears in the rendered HTML; it no longer does. CAUSE: 5b27501 ('renderer: fill 16:9 frame on export') changed backgrounds from an to a div with a CSS background-image. The diff drops the bgAttrs/crossOrigin logic entirely (build-deck.js, removed lines around the old :91 and :108). WHY IT MATTERS, and why this is not just a stale assertion: bs-517 added that attribute so html2canvas would not throw SecurityError on a tainted canvas when exporting a deck whose assets are served from another origin — which is the published-deck case (assets under the S3 asset-base). A CSS background-image taints the canvas the same way an does, and crossorigin cannot be expressed on it at all. So the export path that bs-517 fixed may be broken again for published decks. DO NOT just delete the assertion. Decide first whether export still works cross-origin: 1. Publish a deck, open it from the S3 URL, run the PNG export, watch for SecurityError. 2. If broken: either go back to for backgrounds, or keep the div and make html2canvas use useCORS/allowTaint with proper CORS headers on the bucket. 3. Only then update or remove the test to match the mechanism that actually ships. Local preview is same-origin and will NOT reproduce this — it must be tested against the published URL.

title: build-deck.js report leaks lyrics back into frontier context
description:
Redacting the email is NOT sufficient. scripts/build-deck.js writes
service-report.json, and that report quotes lyric lines back at the frontier model.

MEASURED 2026-08-01, on the real six 7/26 songs extracted by the offsets pipeline:
service-report.json contains 53 of the 127 distinct copyrighted lyric lines, VERBATIM.
(service-preview.html contains 112/127, though the model is not asked to read it.)

Two paths put them there:
  - report.typography lists, per song, the actual lines that will not fit;
  - report.warnings quotes the worst offender in prose, e.g.
    'One Day: 5 line(s) will WRAP MID-PHRASE ... Worst: "One day when heaven was
    filled with His praises,"'

This matters because the model is TOLD to read it. .claude/commands/gen_service.md
step 5: "Summarize from the report". And line 44 tells it to act on those warnings by
adding a caesura to songs/<slug>.md — i.e. to open a file of copyrighted lyrics and
rewrite a lyric line.

So specs/lyric-ingestion.md has a hole. Section 4.3 checks the DECK JSON and correctly
finds no lyric text in it; the REPORT is a different file and was never checked. The
redaction chokepoint at extract_body only closes the email->model direction. This one
runs tool->model and is wide open, which is why a perfectly redacted thread (verified:
0 of 128 lyric lines survive, by exact-line or substring) can still put ~50 lines of
copyrighted lyric into frontier context.

WHAT TO DO (not yet decided, needs Thomas):
  1. build-deck.js reports typography by LINE NUMBER / section + index, never by text.
     Deterministic renderer already owns the text; the model never needs it.
  2. The caesura loop is the harder half - it currently requires the model to edit
     lyric lines. Either move caesura insertion into build-deck.js (it knows the
     metrics and the sense-breaks are guessable from punctuation), or express it as
     an offset edit the way lyric ingestion already expresses extraction.
  3. Until then, "never route verbatim lyric text through a cloud model" is not true
     of this pipeline even with ingest_thread built exactly as specified.
notes:
## 2026-08-02 — exact attribution, and the design tension underneath

Measured on service-report.json for the real six 7/26 songs (53 of 127 distinct
copyrighted lines present verbatim). Which field puts them there:

  typography[].unmarked   (kind=shrunk)   53 lines   build-deck.js:602
  warnings[]  "Worst: ..."                 4 lines   build-deck.js:616  (subset of the above)
  typography[].lines      (kind=caesura)   0 lines   build-deck.js:586  <- LATENT
  anything else in the report              0 lines

So today it is essentially ONE call site: line 602, `unmarked: needMarking.map(lineText)`.
Line 616 quotes one line in prose. Line 586 scored zero only because freshly extracted
songs carry no caesura markers yet; it emits both `line` and `as` (the split parts), so
it starts leaking as soon as any caesura is marked — which is exactly what the fix for
602 tells the model to go and do. Fix all three together or the win is temporary.

THE PART THAT IS NOT A SIMPLE BUG. build-deck.js:191-195 states the division of labour
deliberately: "the SCRIPT measures (it can, exactly), the MODEL judges where the
caesura falls (it can; a mechanical 'break at the widest gap' rule breaks lines
somewhere musically wrong)... the break is a PROJECTION decision, not a lyric edit."

That is a considered decision and it predates specs/lyric-ingestion.md. It is also in
direct conflict with it: to judge a caesura the model must be shown the line. So this
is not an oversight to patch quietly — it is a choice between two designs for
copyrighted songs, and it belongs to Thomas:

  (a) Keep model-judged caesuras, and accept that ~50 lyric lines reach frontier
      context for a six-song service regardless of how clean the email is. The
      2026-08-01 gate run did exactly this and was NOT filtered — but another run on
      the same input WAS, so this is a probability, not a guarantee.
  (b) Report by section name + line index only, and move caesura placement into
      build-deck.js. Punctuation is a decent proxy for the sense-break, and the script
      already has exact glyph metrics. Cheaper than it sounds, and it makes the "never
      route lyric text through a cloud model" claim actually true.
  (c) Hybrid: report by index for songs whose frontmatter says public_domain: false,
      by text otherwise. Keeps the good judgement where it is legally free, and the
      frontmatter to drive it already exists.

Whichever is chosen, tests/build-deck.test.js pins the report shape, so the change is
a visible contract change and not a silent one.

title: Eval: process the real 7/26 email end to end with no content-filter block
description:
THE NEXT SESSION'S GOAL. One sentence: process the real 2026-07-26 email end to end,
in an eval, and get a correct deck plus a reply — with no content-filter block.

That is the first time this failure mode would have been beaten rather than argued
about. Everything in specs/lyric-ingestion.md exists to make this run pass.

THE FIXTURE EXISTS: examples/flowcharts.md, "Example: 7/26/2026" — the minister's
initial request, the agent's reply, the minister's reply pasting all six songs'
lyrics, and the bs-9ed apology. Committed 2026-08-01. Six songs: The Lord Will
Provide (Passion), One Day, How Firm a Foundation, All Hail King Jesus, Goodness of
God (Bethel), Jesus Keep Me Near the Cross. The copyrighted ones are what blocked;
the public-domain hymns wrote fine on the day.

THE TEST VEHICLE IS SAFE: agent/tests/eval/eval_harness.py gives each eval a fresh
workspace with a seeded library (seed_library(ws, keep={...})), copies scripts/
schemas/ .claude/ examples/ and symlinks templates/, and — critically — send_reply is
a STAND-IN that only records the body. NO MAIL REACHES THE MINISTER. Options are
built at eval_harness.py:224. Run with `uv run pytest -m eval -s` from agent/.

SEQUENCING — do NOT start at the bottom.

1. *** GATE FIRST (spec §7.1). Cheap, and it can invalidate the whole design. ***
   Run the pipeline over the 7/26 text to produce a REDACTED thread, then put that
   redacted thread in front of cloud Sonnet as a full agent run and confirm it
   completes. The redacted output still carries song TITLES and [LYRICS: ...]
   reference lines, and the model still has to reason about a service full of
   copyrighted songs. If the trigger is broader than verbatim lyric lines, zero
   leaked lines does not buy safety. UNTESTED. Everything else is downstream.
   Run the raw arm alongside (spec §7.2) — nearly free, and if it 400s you finally
   have a regression test. Note it may NOT reproduce; the synthetic cloud arm passed.

2. Tune the consensus against the REAL text (spec §7.3), not the synthetic one.
   `uv run python -u tests/probes/probe_consensus.py --sweep` currently runs against
   the synthetic fixture; point it at the 7/26 text. Six songs and ~200 lyric lines
   is a much bigger input than the two-song synthetic — check the spec stays valid
   and watch for range overlap between adjacent songs, which is the validator's most
   common rejection.

3. Promote the deterministic half. agent/tests/probes/lyric_offsets.py and
   lyric_consensus.py are pure, network-free and self-tested; move them into
   src/email_agent/ and pin them with golden tests the way build-deck.js is pinned by
   tests/build-deck.test.js.

4. Build the ingest tool and the redaction chokepoint (spec §5, items 2/4/5). The
   ordering constraint is what makes this real: the tool takes a THREAD_ID, never
   text, and is called INSTEAD OF get_thread. Redact at extract_body (tools.py:148)
   so get_message (tools.py:181) cannot bypass it.

5. Write the eval and make it pass.

ASSERT ON, in the eval:
  - no content-filter 400 anywhere in the run;
  - songs/*.md exists for all six, with lyrics VERBATIM from the email — check word
    by word, not by eyeball. Wrong words on a sanctuary screen is the worst outcome
    this system can produce and no amount of green elsewhere excuses it;
  - stanza headings not duplicated (the failure mode from model-authored shell);
  - caesura `|` markers preserved where present, and none invented;
  - deck JSON valid against schemas/deck.schema.json, build-deck.js clean;
  - the run ends in exactly one of send_reply / skip_reply;
  - the reply names the songs and does NOT quote lyrics;
  - any prose lines the consensus over-claimed are surfaced in the reply.

KNOWN TRAPS
  - Call llama.cpp DIRECT, never through UniClaudeProxy. The proxy drops
    chat_template_kwargs (so reasoning cannot be disabled) and drops
    reasoning_content (so a truncated call looks like an empty answer). Spec §3.2.
  - enable_thinking:false is the ONLY knob that works. Without it the task takes
    159s instead of 6.3s.
  - finish_reason == "length" is an ERROR, never "no lyrics found". Failing open
    there silently disables the entire protection.
  - The endpoint address is volatile and the 192.168.x one does not route from
    outside the house. Use LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL.
  - `uv run pytest` is RED on one pre-existing failure (bs-tr6, test_publish
    crossorigin). Expect exactly 1; do not read it as your own.
  - bd silently reverts edits to pre-existing issues (bs-om5). After any bd update,
    run `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` IMMEDIATELY and verify with bd show.
acceptance_criteria: An eval run over the real 7/26 thread completes with no content-filter 400: all six songs written to songs/*.md with lyrics verbatim from the email (verified word by word), stanza headings not duplicated, caesuras preserved and none invented, deck JSON valid, build-deck.js clean, the run ending in exactly one terminal tool, and a reply that names the songs without quoting lyrics. Any over-claimed prose lines are surfaced in the reply.
notes:
## 2026-08-02 — gate run + consensus tuned against the real email

SEQUENCING NOTE: the gate was run first, as this issue said. It did not return a
yes/no. See specs/lyric-ingestion.md 7.1 and the new 4.5 — both updated with the
measurements, and both should be read before planning further work.

WHAT IS DONE
- fixture_0726.py slices the 7/26 thread out of examples/flowcharts.md (not copied,
  so the committed record stays the source of truth).
- probe_consensus.py --fixture 0726, plus --save-specs/--load-specs so consensus can
  be re-scored offline without spending ~4 minutes of model calls per iteration.
- probe_gate.py — the 7.1/7.2 arms, with --repeat, transcript dumps, and a
  redacted-noseed arm.
- tests/test_lyric_repair.py — pins the repair invariant, runs in the default suite.
- Consensus now works on the real email: K>=1..K>=3 leak 0, 212/212 verbatim, six
  songs, correct titles and stanza structure. Was 0 of 7 specs valid before.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, in the order it matters

1. bs-vhp blocks this issue. service-report.json hands the model 53 of 127 distinct
   copyrighted lyric lines. Redacting the email does not stop it. Until that is
   closed, a green eval would be green for the wrong reason.

2. GATE RATE, measured: the redacted arm cleared the filter in 6 of 7 runs and built
   a deck in all 6. The single 400 was the FIRST run, and it used the old redaction
   (fused sections, one song's lyrics inside another's file, duplicate headings);
   every run on the improved redaction cleared — 6/6. That is encouraging but it is
   n=1 on the old version, so the two explanations (base rate ~15%, vs the improved
   redaction fixing it) are not separated. 6/6 is also consistent with a true failure
   rate up to ~20%; it does NOT establish zero. Re-run probe_gate.py --repeat before
   trusting a green eval.

3. Over-claimed labels land inside song files. Five "<Song> lyrics:" lines were
   swallowed; because blank lines are no longer claimed they surface as isolated
   single-line sections (four of them in one-day.md). They are claimed by 1 spec out
   of 5 while real stanzas are claimed by 5, so the vote data already separates them.
   Options, none chosen: raise K (K>=2 drops 2 of 5, K>=3 drops 3, but K>=4 starts
   leaking); drop isolated single-line runs (simple, but a one-line lyric like "(2x)"
   could be a real stanza and dropping un-claims it, which is the leak direction);
   or accept them and surface them in the reply, which is what 4.2 already says to do.
   THIS IS A JUDGEMENT CALL FOR THOMAS — it trades a wrong line on the wall against
   a leak, and 2.2 warns off exactly this kind of heuristic.

4. The model narrates the redaction as a fault to the minister ("your reply's email
   body didn't actually contain any lyrics ... which is an unusual way for that to
   happen"). The reference line needs to explain itself or the system prompt does.

5. DONE since: the deterministic half is now src/email_agent/lyrics/, pinned by
   tests/test_lyric_repair.py and tests/test_lyric_pipeline.py (a golden run over the
   real email, with five real model specs frozen into tests/fixtures/specs_0726.json —
   which contains zero lyric characters, and there is a test asserting that).
   Also fixed after the fact: single-line islands, where a real lyric was filed under
   the wrong song. Found by READING a passing run's reply, not by a test.

   Still not started: the llama.cpp client, config keys, ingest_thread, the
   extract_body chokepoint, the sanitized-thread cache, the fail-closed path, the
   healthcheck, and the eval itself.

TRAPS CONFIRMED THIS SESSION
- ~40s per local call on the real 262-line email, not the 6.3s measured on the
  synthetic. N=7 is ~4 minutes.
- uv run pytest: exactly 1 pre-existing failure (bs-tr6), 85 passed, plus 5 new.

title: Keep lyrics out of the model entirely: redact in get_thread, copy with a pinned tool
description:
THE REPLACEMENT FOR bs-dox APPROACH A. Filed 2026-07-30 on the strength of bs-e4m,
which falsified the provider-fallback premise: gpt-5.6-terra REFUSES to reproduce
copyrighted lyrics (deterministically, 2/2), while cloud Sonnet does not.
Copyright-reproduction guardrails are an industry norm, so there is no provider to
escape to. Swapping providers only trades an Anthropic 400 for an OpenAI refusal.

THE INSIGHT: copying text is not a language task, and we keep asking a language
model to do it. Every failure mode we have — the content-filter 400, the OpenAI
refusal, and the hallucinated-lyrics risk that SYSTEM_PROMPT step 4 exists to
prevent — comes from routing verbatim lyric text through a model. Stop doing that
and all three go away at once.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (bs-e4m, scratchpad/probe_copy.py): given the same job but
FORBIDDEN from emitting lyric text and told to move bytes with shell instead, both
providers succeed, with no refusal and no lyric text in the model's own output:
  gpt-5.6-terra  : 1 Bash call,  6.4s, correct file
  claude-sonnet-5: 2 Bash calls, 12.9s, correct file

TWO HALVES, BOTH REQUIRED. Building only one leaves the 7/26 failure intact.

  HALF 1 — OUTPUT. A pinned extraction tool does the copying.
  HALF 2 — CONTEXT. get_thread must redact lyric-shaped blocks before the model
    ever sees them, stashing them under a handle. This half is NOT optional: per
    bs-a1f, attempt 3 (session 8cebe443) blocked on the FIRST assistant turn after
    mcp__gmail__get_thread having written nothing at all. Lyrics merely being in
    context was enough that time. A design that only cleans the output path would
    not have survived that run.

The model's job becomes: identify WHICH stashed block is WHICH song, and where each
song's stanzas begin and end. It never sees or emits the lyric lines themselves —
it works in handles and offsets. That is a classification/segmentation task, which
is well within reach and carries no copyright-reproduction surface.

*** DO NOT LET THE MODEL WRITE THE SHELL. *** This is the sharpest lesson from
bs-e4m and it is easy to get wrong. gpt-5.6-terra's shell one-liner produced
byte-exact lyrics but DUPLICATED stanza headings — 16 headings where there should
have been 10 (## Chorus, ## Verse 2 and ## Bridge each twice). A mangled stanza
structure is a broken deck. Sonnet got it right only because it ran an inspection
pass (grep -n for frontmatter and heading offsets) before composing its command; it
earned correctness rather than being guaranteed it.

So the copy belongs in a fixed, tested script or MCP tool — pinned by golden tests,
exactly as build-deck.js is pinned by tests/build-deck.test.js. This is already this
repo's stated rule (CLAUDE.md: "the model emits data, not slide markup — if a slide
is wrong, fix build-deck.js, not the HTML"). Apply it to lyrics verbatim: the model
emits a SPEC (which handle, which offsets, which song file), and a deterministic
tool writes songs/*.md from it.

CONSEQUENCES IF THIS WORKS:
  - The whole multi-provider fallback (bs-dox) becomes unnecessary. So does the
    UniClaudeProxy dependency, the homelab availability risk (bs-7sb), the backend
    pinning (bs-1x4), and arguably the Pi migration question (bs-752).
  - Everything stays on subscription-billed Sonnet with the existing SDK — no
    economics change, no framework migration, no second runtime on the deploy box.
  - bs-fsx (caesura placement) becomes reachable for copyrighted songs, since
    placing a '|' is an OFFSET operation, not a reproduction one.

RISKS TO DESIGN AGAINST
  1. Redaction fidelity. Identifying lyric blocks in a mixed prose/lyric email is
     heuristic. Over-redact and the model loses the minister's instructions;
     under-redact and lyrics reach context anyway. Ministers' emails are
     semi-structured (flowchart, then a reply pasting lyrics), which helps. If a
     classifier is wanted, THIS is the right job for the local 27B — one bounded
     task, no multi-turn tool use, no session resume, indifferent to proxy
     translation fidelity. That is a far better use of Bonsai than bs-fxj's
     "drive the whole agent loop", which bs-e4m's evidence makes unattractive.
  2. Verification. We still have NO faithful reproduction of the original 7/26
     filter trip — the minimal repro passes on cloud. Build a fixture from the real
     thread before claiming this fixes anything.
  3. The agent must still be able to REPORT what it could not find, without quoting
     lyrics, so the reply stays useful to the minister.

FIRST STEP, cheap: prove the redaction half. Take the real 7/26 thread, run
get_thread with redaction on, and confirm (a) the model can still tell which songs
are wanted and in what order, and (b) no lyric text appears anywhere in the
transcript.
acceptance_criteria: A service with copyrighted songs is processed end to end on subscription-billed Sonnet with NO provider fallback: get_thread redacts lyric blocks so no lyric text appears in the transcript, the model emits only handles/offsets, and a pinned tool (golden-tested like build-deck.js) writes songs/*.md with correct stanza structure. Demonstrated against a fixture built from the real 7/26 thread, with stanza headings verified NOT duplicated.
notes:
================================================================
2026-07-31 — PICKING THIS UP COLD. Anchors, decisions, and one design
hole found while writing this section.
================================================================

DECISION (Thomas, 2026-07-31): attempt the REDACTION half. It is not gated on first
building a 7/26 reproduction. The reproduction is still worth building for
VERIFICATION (see risk 2 above) but it does not block starting.

*** DESIGN HOLE — REDACTING get_thread ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH. ***
Found while pinning anchors. `get_message` returns a message body too, so a model
that has been handed a redacted thread can simply call get_message on the same id
and receive the lyrics unredacted. Both tools must go through the same redaction,
and the natural chokepoint is `extract_body` (tools.py:148), which is the single
function both paths use to turn a Gmail payload into body text. Redact there, or at
minimum in both callers, and add a test that asserts get_message cannot be used to
bypass the thread redaction. This is exactly the kind of hole that would look fine
in testing and leak on a Sunday.

CODE ANCHORS (verified 2026-07-31, agent/src/email_agent/)
  tools.py:148   extract_body()            <- the shared chokepoint; redact HERE
  tools.py:181   fetch one message         <- builds the get_message payload
  tools.py:354   get_thread() internal     <- builds the thread payload
  tools.py:459   @tool "get_message"       <- MCP surface
  tools.py:547   @tool "get_thread"        <- MCP surface
  tools.py:606   @tool "send_reply"        <- must never carry lyric text either
  harness.py:37  GET_THREAD_TOOL constant
  harness.py:143 mcp_servers={"gmail":..., "deck":...}
  harness.py:151 built-in tool allow-list (Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash/...)

NOTE harness.py:151 grants Read and Bash. Once songs/*.md exist on disk the model
can read the lyrics back at will, so redaction protects the INGEST path, not the
whole session. That is fine — the 7/26 block happened on ingest — but do not
oversell the guarantee, and do not be surprised if a later turn reads a song file.

THE songs/*.md CONTRACT the extraction tool must produce (parsed by
scripts/build-deck.js:103-164; a malformed file fails the build, which is the
good outcome):
  - YAML-ish flat frontmatter between --- lines. Fields in use: title, type, source,
    author, copyright, public_domain, verified. gen_service treats `verified` as
    meaningful (see bs-9fe / the gen_service skill) — do not invent a value for it.
  - `## Section` headings (Verse 1, Chorus, Bridge, ...), order preserved.
  - build-deck.js distinguishes `sections` (every heading, including placeholders)
    from `usable` (those carrying real projectable lyrics). A stub section is a
    legitimate state meaning "we do not have these words yet".
  - A `|` in a lyric line is a CAESURA — a projection hint, never shown on a slide.
    The extraction tool must preserve any that exist and must not invent them.

TEST VEHICLE — use it, it is safe:
  agent/tests/eval/eval_harness.py gives each eval a FRESH WORKSPACE with a SEEDED
  song library (seed_library(ws, keep={...})), copies scripts/ schemas/ .claude/
  examples/ and symlinks templates/. Crucially `send_reply` is a STAND-IN that only
  records the body, so NO MAIL REACHES THE MINISTER. ClaudeAgentOptions is built at
  eval_harness.py:224. Evals are excluded from the default suite; run them with
  `uv run pytest -m eval -s` from agent/.

THE REAL 7/26 THREAD, for building the verification fixture (from bs-a1f):
  thread 19f95387567d275e, msg 19f9e252615fabcb   — 3 attempts, gave up
  thread 19f9e5592103ca17                          — 3 attempts, gave up
  Songs: The Lord Will Provide / Goodness of God / All Hail King Jesus (copyrighted,
  blocked) alongside one-day and how-firm-a-foundation (public domain, WROTE FINE).
  None of the copyrighted three are in songs/ — that run died before saving them.
  Check the mailbox still has the thread before planning around it; lookback_days
  defaults to 7 but the mail itself should persist.

EVIDENCE IS NOW IN THE REPO, not in a scratchpad. The probes this issue cites moved
to agent/tests/probes/ (probe_filter.py, probe_copy.py, README.md) with portable
paths and an --out-dir flag. README.md carries the full result tables. Earlier notes
on this issue and on bs-e4m refer to "scratchpad/probe_copy.py" — that path is dead;
read agent/tests/probes/ instead.

BEFORE YOU START: `uv run pytest` in agent/ is currently RED — one pre-existing
failure in tests/test_publish.py over the crossorigin assertion, tracked as bs-tr6.
It is unrelated to this work. Do not let it confuse a green/red judgement on your
own changes; check that the failure count stays at exactly 1.

ALSO: bd silently reverts edits to pre-existing issues (bs-om5). After any
`bd update`, run `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` IMMEDIATELY and verify with
`bd show`, or your notes will vanish. See the stored `bd remember` entry.

================================================================
2026-07-31 — BONSAI-AS-INTERMEDIARY TESTED. Concept survives, the
agentic implementation does NOT. Probe: agent/tests/probes/probe_intermediary.py
================================================================

DESIGN TESTED (Thomas's): Bonsai reads the incoming mail, extracts lyrics into
songs/*.md, and hands the frontier model the email with lyric blocks replaced by
library references. Frontier model therefore never has lyric text in context.

TWO PRIOR MEASUREMENTS, both green (agent/tests/probes/README.md):
  - Bonsai does NOT refuse copyrighted lyrics and is NOT filtered: 7 tool calls,
    81.9s, file written and self-verified. gpt-5.6-terra refuses the same task 2/2.
  - Transcription is FAITHFUL: 42/42 lyric lines verbatim, zero hallucination, all
    3 caesura `|` markers preserved in place.

THEN THE REAL TEST — a deliberately hostile email (lyrics butted onto a sentence
with no blank line, an instruction buried BETWEEN stanzas, two songs separated only
by a bare title, a title-only song that must not be fabricated, short prose decoys).

VERDICT: FAIL.

WHAT WORKED — the JUDGEMENT half, which is the part I expected to be weakest:
  - CHECK 2 over-redaction: 0 prose lines lost. Every instruction survived,
    including "Please put the second one AFTER the offering" which was buried
    mid-stanza, and it stayed in its original position.
  - CHECK 4: "Days of Elijah", mentioned by name only, correctly NOT fabricated.
  - Song 2 WAS correctly redacted — lyrics removed, reference substituted.
  - Library transcription faithful. (CHECK 3 flagged 1 line as non-verbatim; that is
    a CHECKER ARTIFACT, not a model error — the probe concatenates a lyric onto a
    prose sentence, so the split line legitimately is not a standalone source line.
    Bonsai split it correctly.)

WHAT FAILED:
  1. *** 18 LYRIC LINES LEAKED. *** For song 1 it APPENDED the [LYRICS: ...]
     reference but never DELETED the lyric block. It did the additive half of the
     edit and skipped the deletive half. This is precisely the one thing the design
     exists to prevent, and it failed open — the frontier model would have received
     the lyrics.
  2. *** 3209s = 53.5 MINUTES, 66 tool calls *** on a TWO-song email. The transcript
     shows thrashing: repeated Write/Read/verify loops and "I apologize for the
     confusion" / "I apologize for the repeated confusion". agent_timeout_seconds is
     1800 for an ENTIRE run; this one preprocessing stage took nearly twice that.
     The 7/26 service had six songs.
  3. Titles derived from first lyric lines, not song titles:
     you-are-here-moving-in-our-midst.md, worthy-is-the-lamb-who-was-slain.md.
     For song 1 no title was present in the email (fair), but for song 2 the bare
     line "Revelation Song" WAS present and it still used the first lyric line.
     A wrong slug means the reference handed to the frontier model is wrong and
     gen_service cannot find the song.

DIAGNOSIS — DO NOT READ THIS AS "BONSAI CANNOT DO IT". Read it as: THIS FORMULATION
cannot. Every failure above is a failure of TEXT REGENERATION and AGENTIC
SELF-CORRECTION, not of lyric/prose judgement:
  - the leak happened while rewriting the email by hand;
  - the 53 minutes is dominated by emitting and re-verifying text it did not need
    to emit (at ~31 tok/s decode, measured by Thomas);
  - the thrashing is a small model in a multi-step correct-yourself loop.

NEXT FORMULATION TO TEST — and this is the last rescue this design gets:
  * ONE CALL. NO TOOLS. NO AGENTIC LOOP. *
  Input : the email with LINE NUMBERS PREFIXED (0012| ...), so the model reads an
          index off the page instead of counting, which small models are bad at.
  Output: one JSON spec and nothing else —
          {"song":"way-maker","title":"Way Maker",
           "sections":[{"name":"Verse 1","start":12,"end":19}, ...]}
  A DETERMINISTIC SCRIPT then does BOTH jobs: slices those ranges into songs/*.md,
  and deletes those same ranges from the email, substituting the reference line.

  Why this addresses each observed failure:
    - The leak becomes IMPOSSIBLE: deletion is the script's job, and it removes
      exactly the ranges it extracted. There is no "forgot to delete" path.
    - Hallucination becomes impossible BY CONSTRUCTION rather than merely checkable:
      the model emits no lyric characters at all; the script copies bytes, which
      also preserves caesuras and whitespace for free.
    - ~300 output tokens instead of ~2800+, i.e. ~10s of decode instead of tens of
      minutes, and no tool-call thrashing because there are no tools.
  Validate the spec before applying: ranges in bounds, non-overlapping, start<end,
  slices non-empty, and every email line accounted for as either a lyric range or
  preserved prose.

  The TITLE problem is NOT fixed by this and needs its own assertion: given a bare
  title line adjacent to a lyric block, does it pick the title? Test it explicitly.

FALSIFICATION CONDITION — state it now so we do not keep rescuing this: if the
single-call offsets version ALSO leaks lyrics or mis-titles a song whose title is
present in the email, Bonsai is not reliable enough for the gatekeeper role and the
design should be abandoned rather than patched a third time.

STANDING RISK regardless of formulation: this puts Bonsai on the critical path for
EVERY email, not just copyrighted ones. It must fail CLOSED (legible error into the
bs-9ed apology path), never pass through unredacted. bs-7sb (healthcheck probing the
endpoint AND the model alias) becomes more important, not less.

ALSO leaks lyrics or mis-titles a song whose title is present in the email, Bonsai
is not reliable enough and the design should be abandoned rather than patched a
third time." It leaks 2 lines. BY THE LETTER, IT FAILS.

reasoning would show up. Stating the tension plainly instead: the bar treated

Thomas decides whether to continue.

  b) FAIL CLOSED ON SUSPICION for leak 2: after validation, if an unclaimed line sits
     BETWEEN two claimed ranges OF THE SAME SONG, treat the spec as unsafe and refuse

     already uses (harness.py:237 terminal guard, bs-tiz.4's "deciding NOTHING is the

Neither asks the model to be better; both make the deterministic layer stricter.

THE OTHER NEW OPERATIONAL FACT — BONSAI'S HIDDEN REASONING BUDGET:
At max_tokens=4000 the call returned stop_reason=max_tokens with an EMPTY text block.

reaches an answer. At max_tokens=16000 it succeeded: 5969 output tokens for a

  - every call needs a five-figure max_tokens or it silently returns nothing;
  - an empty text block is indistinguishable from "no lyrics found" unless you check
    stop_reason — CHECK stop_reason, and treat max_tokens as an ERROR, not an answer;
  - the "cheap bounded preprocessing step" costs ~2.5 min of mostly unobservable
    decode per email, before the frontier agent starts.

================================================================
2026-08-01 — BONSAI AS A TOOL, NOT AN AGENT. Thomas's framing, and it is
the right one. Plus two negative results and a corrected address.
================================================================

THE FRAMING: stop treating Bonsai as something that reasons about tool calls.
Expose it as a TOOL the frontier model invokes with a one-shot prompt. Agentic
local execution is only ever wanted here as a response to a hard cloud refusal —
it is not a capability worth building for its own sake.

This is right, and probe_offsets.py already validates the mechanism: ONE http call,
no SDK, no tools, no loop, and the judgement was good (both titles correct,
mid-stanza instruction excluded, bare title line excluded, title-only song skipped,
zero non-verbatim output). What is new is not the mechanism but the PACKAGING and
the TRIGGER.

*** THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES OR BREAKS THIS DESIGN ***
If the FRONTIER model decides when to call the tool, it must first know there are
lyrics — which means it has read the email — which is the exact exposure we are
removing. bs-a1f attempt 3 blocked on the FIRST assistant turn after
mcp__gmail__get_thread, having written nothing at all.

So the tool MUST take a thread_id, NEVER lyric text. It fetches the thread itself,
calls Bonsai one-shot, writes songs/*.md, and returns ONLY metadata — slugs, titles,
section names — plus the redacted body. The frontier model calls it INSTEAD OF
get_thread, not after it. Get that ordering wrong and the whole design is decorative.

  mcp__songs__ingest_thread(thread_id) ->
    {"songs":[{"slug":"way-maker","title":"Way Maker",
               "sections":["Verse 1","Chorus"]}],
     "thread": "<redacted body with [LYRICS: ...] reference lines>"}

Note this returns exactly what deck JSON needs anyway — slug plus section names
(verified: passages/2026-07-19/service.deck.json carries no lyric text at all) — so
the frontier model is not losing information it needs. It is losing only the words.

ON "ONLY WHEN A CLOUD MODEL HARD-BLOCKS": tempting but unworkable as stated — you
cannot know a block is coming without looking, and by then you have looked. If the
goal is to keep Bonsai off the path for ordinary prose-only emails, use a CHEAP
DETERMINISTIC TRIGGER instead: invoke it only when the body contains a run of N+
consecutive short lines lacking terminal punctuation. Over-triggering costs latency
only; under-triggering leaks, so tune it conservatively. That keeps the common case
fast without asking a model to predict a refusal.

*** NEGATIVE RESULT 1 — REASONING CANNOT BE TURNED OFF FROM THE CLIENT. ***
Tested against the proxy, ten variants, "Reply with exactly: OK":
  baseline 183 | reasoning_effort none/low/minimal 104/176/161 | thinking:disabled 158
  chat_template_kwargs 174 | extra_body.enable_thinking 121 | /no_think 224
  /nothink 248 | system-prompt "no reasoning" 218
The apparent win for reasoning_effort=none is NOISE. Repeated 4x each:
  baseline               [167,135,139,107] mean 137
  reasoning_effort=none  [108,214,167,113] mean 150
No knob has an effect. Either the proxy drops these fields or the serving stack
ignores them. DISABLING REASONING REQUIRES A SERVER-SIDE CHANGE on whatever serves
Bonsai; it is not reachable per-request. Until then every call carries the hidden
budget: ~140 output tokens to say "OK", ~5900 for a 273-character JSON spec, and
max_tokens must stay five-figure or the call returns an EMPTY text block with
stop_reason=max_tokens.

*** NEGATIVE RESULT 2 — NO DIRECT ENDPOINT REACHABLE. ***
Thomas suggested skipping the proxy and hitting the local model's OpenAI endpoint
directly. Scanned 1234, 11434, 8000, 8080, 5000, 5001, 9222, 9224, 8081, 3000 on the
server: nothing answered /v1/models. It is either on a non-standard port, bound to
localhost on that host, or proxy-only. Not currently an option from the agent host.

*** ADDRESS CORRECTION — bs-dox's RECORDED TAILNET ADDRESS IS STALE. ***
bs-dox notes say the tailscale address is 100.69.94.72. The working one is
  http://100.66.185.49:9223
Confirmed 2026-08-01 while Thomas was away from the LAN, which is also why an
earlier round of tests silently reached nothing: 192.168.0.48 does not route from
outside the house. The probes read FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL, so this is an env
override, not a code change. TREAT BOTH ADDRESSES AS VOLATILE and never hardcode.

STILL THE BINDING TECHNICAL PROBLEM — MIXED LINES. Two offsets runs failed in
OPPOSITE directions on the same hostile email: run 1 leaked 2 lyric lines, run 2
leaked 0 but destroyed a prose line, because line-granularity ranges cannot express
"the second half of line 7 is a lyric". Proposed minimal fix, which keeps the
structural no-hallucination guarantee: add OPTIONAL character trims to the spec, on
BOUNDARY LINES ONLY —
  {"name":"Verse 1","start":7,"end":12,"start_col":71}
Everything stays sliceable, the model emits two extra integers rather than any lyric
text, and the deterministic validator can still reject nonsense. The alternative —
having Bonsai emit the file CONTENT so it can split the line itself — fixes mixed
lines but trades the structural guarantee for an after-the-fact substring check.
(That check did pass 42/42 when measured, so it is not unreasonable, just weaker.)

2026-08-01 (later) — DIRECT llama.cpp + THINKING OFF + CONSENSUS.
This is the formulation that works. 25x faster AND zero leakage.
================================================================

Thomas exposed the LLM host directly on port 8080, bypassing UniClaudeProxy.
Endpoint: http://100.66.185.49:8080  (tailnet; VOLATILE, keep it in
FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL / a new LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL, never hardcode)

WHAT THE HOST ACTUALLY IS — worth knowing, none of it was visible through the proxy:
  server : llama.cpp  (owned_by "llamacpp")
  model  : Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf
  size   : 3.79 GB for 26.9B params  => ~1.13 bits/param. A 1-BIT QUANT.
  context: n_ctx 65536 (trained 262144)
  /props : reasoning_format=none, reasoning_in_content=false,
           chat_template_caps.supports_preserve_reasoning=true

*** THE FIX: chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} ***
Trivial prompt "Reply with exactly: OK":
  baseline                                 106-122 tok, reasoning_content 376-445 chars
  reasoning_budget=0                       119-150 tok   (NO effect)
  reasoning_effort=none                    140-175 tok   (NO effect)
  thinking:{"type":"disabled"}             158-165 tok   (NO effect)
  chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=F     2 tok, reasoning_content 0   <== WORKS
On the real lyric-offsets task: 159.0s / 7111 tok  ->  6.3s / ~250 tok. ~25x both ways.

*** AND THE PROXY WAS HIDING TWO THINGS. ***
1. It DROPS chat_template_kwargs — the identical param through UniClaudeProxy had no
   effect (174 tok). That is why the earlier ten-knob sweep came back all-noise.
2. It DROPS reasoning_content. llama.cpp returns thinking in a SEPARATE field, which
   is why a truncated call through the proxy showed an EMPTY text block: the thinking
   never lands in `content`, so a call that never finished thinking has nothing in
   content at all. Direct, you can see both.
Worth reporting upstream; both are silent losses.

*** QUALITY: A SINGLE CALL IS NOT RELIABLE, IN EITHER MODE. ***
Three identical think-off calls on the same hostile email:
  run1 leak=6 lostprose=2 titles=['Way Maker']                    (missed song 2 entirely)
  run2 leak=4 lostprose=2 titles=['Way Maker','Revelation Song']
  run3 leak=0 lostprose=2 titles=['Way Maker','Revelation Song']  44/44 verbatim
And think-ON was not better — that run titled song 2 "Holy, Holy, Holy", a LYRIC LINE
rather than the title. Thinking buys nothing here; it only costs 25x.
Do not read any single run as evidence either way. Variance dominates.

*** THE ANSWER: CONSENSUS. Speed is the resource that buys reliability. ***
7 calls, 44.4s total (6.3s each), 6 produced a valid spec. Union the claimed line
sets and vote on titles:

  threshold      lines claimed   prose destroyed   LYRICS LEAKED
  K>=1 .. K>=4        45               3                0
  K>=5                42               2                2
  K>=6                38               0                4

  titles voted: Way Maker 6, Revelation Song 4, Worthy Is the Lamb 1, Holy Holy Holy 1
  -> majority vote gives BOTH correct titles, outvoting the two bad guesses.

Different runs miss DIFFERENT lines, so the union covers all of them. K>=1 through
K>=4 are identical, meaning the runs largely agree and disagreement is confined to
range boundaries — exactly where you want redundancy.

WHY THE UNION IS THE RIGHT BIAS, not a fudge: the two error directions are NOT
symmetric. Over-claiming destroys a prose line — visible to the minister in the
reply, correctable, costs one email. Under-claiming leaks a lyric — content filter
400, run dies, and the failure this whole epic exists to fix. Bias toward
over-claiming and surface the over-claim: "I moved these lines into the song
library; tell me if any were instructions."

THIS VALIDATES THOMAS'S TOOL FRAMING COMPLETELY. Not an agent: N one-shot calls,
no tools, no loop, ~45s total, with every byte of lyric handled by
lyric_offsets.py. The model contributes only line numbers and titles, and is
allowed to be individually unreliable because the aggregate is not.

REMAINING, IN PRIORITY ORDER
1. The tool must take a THREAD_ID, never lyric text, and be called INSTEAD OF
   get_thread — see the constraint recorded in the previous section. Ordering is
   what makes this real rather than decorative.
2. Mixed prose/lyric lines still cost prose (the 3 destroyed lines). Optional
   character trims on BOUNDARY LINES ONLY would fix it; see previous section.
3. *** TRY A BETTER QUANT. *** Q1_0 is about as aggressive as quantisation gets.
   Much of the observed variance may simply be the quant, not the model. If the box
   can hold Q4 or Q5, re-run the consensus experiment — the required N may drop to
   1-2 and the mixed-line judgement may improve. Cheapest available win by far.
4. Tune N and K against a REAL minister email once a 7/26 fixture exists. N=7 was
   arbitrary; the data suggests N=5/K=1 would already be safe here.
5. Still no reproduction of the original 7/26 filter trip, so "zero leaked lines"
   cannot yet be scored against the failure it is meant to prevent.

title: UniClaudeProxy: any request with tools 400s on the OpenAI path (gpt-5.6-terra); Anthropic aliases 401
description:
EXTERNAL DEFECT — lives in UniClaudeProxy (http://192.168.0.48:9223), not in this
repo. BLOCKS bs-e4m completely: the Agent SDK's entire loop is tool calls, so a
model that cannot accept a tool definition cannot run the agent at all.

SYMPTOM: for the OpenAI-backed alias gpt-5.6-terra, ANY request carrying `tools`
fails upstream with an OpenAI 400, which the proxy surfaces as its own 502/api_error.
Requests WITHOUT tools work perfectly.

VERIFIED 2026-07-30 from the agent host. Isolated by bisection:

  plain text, no tools ............................ 200 OK ("OK", 4 output tokens)
  + system prompt, no tools ....................... 200 OK
  + one trivial tool, non-streaming ............... 400 upstream
  + one trivial tool, STREAMING ................... 400 upstream
      (message_start and ping arrive, then event: error)

Then four tool-schema variants, all 400:
  1. {"text":"string"}, required:["text"]
  2. same + additionalProperties:false + all-required (OpenAI strict-mode safe)
  3. {"type":"object","properties":{}}  <- trivially valid, nothing to reject
  4. tool omitting `description`

Because even an EMPTY-properties schema fails, this is NOT the JSON Schema content.
It is the tool ENVELOPE.

LIKELY CAUSE: the Anthropic tool shape is being passed through without conversion.
Anthropic sends
    {"name":..., "description":..., "input_schema":{...}}
OpenAI chat completions requires
    {"type":"function","function":{"name":..., "description":..., "parameters":{...}}}
So a missing "type":"function" wrapper, or `input_schema` left in place of
`parameters`, produces exactly this: unconditional 400 regardless of schema body.

NOTE THIS IS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM bs-qku. bs-qku is the RESPONSE direction
(OpenAI tool arguments -> Anthropic tool_use.input, lost on the non-streaming path).
This is the REQUEST direction (Anthropic tools -> OpenAI tools). They are separate
code paths and separate bugs; fixing one does not fix the other.

*** SECOND FINDING — THE ANTHROPIC ALIASES ARE NOW BROKEN TOO ***
claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5 now forward to https://api.anthropic.com and come
back 401 Unauthorized — the proxy has no valid Anthropic credential configured.
This is a REGRESSION against bs-dox's notes, which recorded claude-sonnet-5 as
mapped and working, and recorded claude-opus-5 as routing to Bonsai. The mapping has
evidently been reconfigured to pass through to Anthropic instead of to a local model.
Two consequences:
  - bs-dox's "GREEN, end-to-end SDK run PASSES" evidence is no longer reproducible
    as written; whatever claude-sonnet-5 pointed at then, it does not point there now.
  - Pass-through-to-Anthropic aliases are useless for our purpose even if the 401 is
    fixed: the whole point is to reach a NON-Anthropic provider, and Anthropic
    traffic is what the content filter applies to.
  - `bonsai` returns "All connection attempts failed" (expected — Thomas had not
    started it yet at time of test).

DIAGNOSTIC GAP WORTH FIXING FIRST — it would have answered this in one request:
the proxy DISCARDS the upstream error body. It reports only OpenAI's status line
("Client error '400 Bad Request' for url ...") and drops the JSON body, which is
where OpenAI states exactly which field it rejected. Surfacing the upstream
error body in the proxy's error envelope is a small change with a large payoff for
every future debugging session.

ACCEPTANCE CHECK once fixed (run from the agent host):

  curl -s -X POST http://192.168.0.48:9223/v1/messages \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra","max_tokens":300,
         "tools":[{"name":"echo_text","description":"Echo text back.",
           "input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{
             "text":{"type":"string"}},"required":["text"]}}],
         "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Use echo_text with text=banana"}]}'

Expect a tool_use block with input == {"text":"banana"} (per bs-qku, the
non-streaming path may still return {} — in that case re-run with "stream":true and
assert the input_json_delta fragments concatenate to {"text":"banana"}). Then
re-run agent/../scratchpad/probe_filter.py --backend proxy --model gpt-5.6-terra
and expect Read, Read, Write and a written output file.
acceptance_criteria: A POST to /v1/messages for gpt-5.6-terra carrying a tool definition returns a tool_use block with populated input (streaming acceptable per bs-qku), and probe_filter.py --backend proxy --model gpt-5.6-terra completes with Read/Read/Write and a written output file.
