title: beads DB silently reverts edits: false 'empty database' triggers a JSONL re-import on every command
description:
The Dolt `bs` database is in a degraded state that SILENTLY REVERTS EDITS. Hit
repeatedly on 2026-07-29 while updating bs-dox / bs-1x4 / bs-a1f: bd reports
"Updated issue" and exits 0, and the change is gone by the next command.

WHAT HAPPENED FIRST (the recovery, now done):
The dolt sql-server had no `bs` database at all — `bd dolt start` had initialised
.beads/dolt/ as a database ITSELF (.dolt/ at the top level, repo_state.json with
empty branches) instead of as a server data-dir CONTAINING a bs/ database. Every bd
command failed with 'database "bs" not found'. `bd bootstrap` could not fix it
("nothing to commit"). Recovered by stopping the server, moving the bogus top-level
.dolt/ and .doltcfg/ aside, and promoting the intact repo from
.beads/embeddeddolt/bs (a real beads DB with full history) to .beads/dolt/bs.
bd doctor then went from 3 errors to 0. A full pre-recovery snapshot of .beads/
was taken to the session scratchpad.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG (this issue):
Every single bd invocation prints
    auto-importing N bytes from .beads/issues.jsonl into empty database...
    auto-imported 51 issues
even though the database demonstrably is NOT empty — `dolt sql -q "select count(*)
from issues"` in .beads/dolt/bs returns 51, and `dolt log` shows the bd write
commits. The emptiness check is a false positive, and the import that follows it
UPSERTS the JSONL over the DB, so any edit made since the last export is reverted.

CONSEQUENCES, all observed:
  - `bd update` on a PRE-EXISTING issue succeeds, then is reverted by the next
    command's import. Verified twice on bs-dox (title + 4kb of notes) and once on
    bs-1x4.
  - Newly CREATED issues survive, because they are absent from the JSONL and the
    upsert has nothing to overwrite them with.
  - Auto-flush does NOT rescue this: after a successful update, waiting out the 5s
    debounce left issues.jsonl still holding the old record.
  - `bd export` with no -o writes to STDOUT, so the obvious "just export first"
    reflex does not refresh the file. Needs `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`.
  - Dependency EDGES are import-add-only. Removing one with `bd dep remove` sticks
    only if no import intervenes; a patched JSONL will not delete an edge.

WORKAROUNDS USED (do not mistake these for a fix):
  - `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` immediately after each mutation, so the next
    import is a no-op.
  - For stubborn records, patching .beads/issues.jsonl directly (it is bd's own
    format) and bumping updated_at.
  - `no-auto-import: true` in .beads/config.yaml DOES NOT WORK — nor do
    BD_NO_AUTO_IMPORT / BEADS_NO_AUTO_IMPORT. The "empty database" path appears to
    ignore the setting entirely. Reverted after testing; do not re-add expecting it
    to help.

WHY IT MATTERS: this project keeps its entire planning record in beads, and the
failure mode is silent — no error, exit 0, work quietly lost. Several long,
hard-won notes fields (bs-dox at 11kb, bs-a1f at 7kb, bs-tiz.6's gap analysis) are
exactly the kind of thing that vanishes without anyone noticing.

NEXT STEPS
1. Find what bd's "is the database empty" check actually reads. It is probably a
   metadata/marker table that the promoted embeddeddolt repo lacks — likely
   candidates in that DB: local_metadata, metadata, repo_mtimes, issue_counter.
   Compare against a healthy beads DB.
2. If it is a missing marker row, write it and confirm the auto-import line stops.
3. Consider `bd doctor --fix` and the two warnings it still reports (5 runtime
   files tracked by git under .beads/backup/, and outdated .beads/.gitignore).
4. No git remote is configured for Dolt (`bd doctor`: "No remotes configured", and
   `git ls-remote origin` shows no refs/dolt/data), so the ONLY durable copy of the
   issue history is .beads/issues.jsonl in git plus the local .beads/backup archive.
   Worth fixing independently — it is why the JSONL being stale was so dangerous.
acceptance_criteria: bd commands no longer print the "auto-importing ... into empty database" line, and an edit to a pre-existing issue survives the next several bd invocations without needing a manual export. Verified by updating a notes field, running bd list/show/ready, and confirming the change is still there.

title: Spike: does a non-Anthropic frontier model via UniClaudeProxy clear the content filter?
description:
SPIKE — measure before building. Nothing here ships; the deliverable is an answer
written back into this issue and into bs-dox.

THE QUESTION: does routing the agent through UniClaudeProxy to a NON-ANTHROPIC
FRONTIER model get past the content filter, and can that model drive the whole
loop?

WHY THIS FIRST, BEFORE THE LOCAL 27B (bs-dox's current plan). bs-dox conflates two
independent variables:
  1. PROVIDER — the content filter is Anthropic-side policy, not a property of
     "running locally". Any non-Anthropic model should bypass it.
  2. CAPABILITY — can the model drive Gmail MCP -> gen_service -> deck JSON ->
     build-deck.js -> publish -> reply?
The local 27B changes BOTH at once, and (2) is the doubtful half. A frontier model
through the same proxy changes only (1) and leaves capability near-certain. So it
isolates the variable that actually matters and is the cheaper experiment.

If this passes, the whole epic gets much better:
  - bs-dox stops being "fall back to a LOCAL model" and becomes "fall back to a
    different PROVIDER", with the endpoint and model as config.
  - The homelab 27B leaves the critical path (see the availability risk on bs-hc).
  - bs-fsx (caesura eval) becomes reachable for copyrighted songs.

METHOD
1. Thomas adds a model redirect in UniClaudeProxy config mapping an alias to a
   non-Anthropic frontier model. Record the exact alias here — the proxy rejects
   anything not in its "config models mapping" (see bs-dox notes for that trap).
2. Run the REAL harness against it. Do NOT write fallback logic for this spike;
   point the existing harness at the proxy and let it run start to finish.
3. Target the KNOWN-BAD 7/26 material — the run that failed 6/6 on the cloud with
   the copyrighted set (The Lord Will Provide / Goodness of God / All Hail King
   Jesus), threads 19f95387567d275e and 19f9e5592103ca17. A patriotic/public-domain
   thread proves nothing; it passed on the cloud already.
4. Record: (a) any content-filter 400 at all? (b) did the run reach send_reply?
   (c) is the OUTPUT actually correct — songs/*.md populated with the right lyrics,
   deck JSON valid against schemas/deck.schema.json, build-deck.js clean, published
   URL resolves with backgrounds?

TWO ENVIRONMENT TRAPS — both will cost an hour each if not handled up front:

  a) CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN IS INHERITED BY THE CLI SUBPROCESS. config.py:136
     assert_subscription_auth() REQUIRES it to be non-empty in the parent process,
     and subprocess_cli merges the parent env into the child. So the token reaches
     the CLI unless ClaudeAgentOptions.env explicitly blanks it, and the CLI may
     then prefer subscription auth over the proxy. The verified probe in bs-dox
     ran as a standalone script that probably had no token set, so its env block
     may NOT reproduce inside the real harness. Set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN to ""
     in options.env alongside the other three.

  b) assert_subscription_auth() also RAISES if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in the
     parent. Exporting it empty ("") reads as falsy and passes the guard, so that
     is the way through — do not delete the guard.

Because of (a), the spike needs a throwaway patch adding env={...} to the
ClaudeAgentOptions at harness.py:139. That is ~4 lines and it is the SAME seam the
real implementation uses, so it is not wasted work. Do not merge it.

ALSO MEASURE while you are here — these are on bs-dox's untested list and this run
exercises them for free:
  - Multi-turn tool_result round trip (request-direction translation).
  - The real agent's large multi-tool payload plus the full SYSTEM_PROMPT.
  - Context headroom: the 7/26 transcript was ~175KB of JSONL before it died.
  - Whether the model is verbose enough to need generous max_tokens (Bonsai spent
    102 output tokens to say "OK").
acceptance_criteria: A documented run of the known-bad 7/26 material through a non-Anthropic frontier model on the proxy, with a yes/no on each of: content-filter 400 encountered; run reached send_reply; deck output correct (lyrics verbatim from the email, deck JSON valid, published URL resolves with backgrounds). A clean failure is a passing outcome for this spike PROVIDED it identifies which of filter / capability / transport broke. Result written back into bs-dox.
notes:
================================================================
2026-07-30 — FIRST ATTEMPT. Two real findings, then BLOCKED on the proxy.
================================================================

Probe script kept at scratchpad/probe_filter.py (session
bcf03f92-bf35-4444-9c87-beed3c9dcadb). It runs the same task on either arm:
reproduce two COPYRIGHTED contemporary songs' lyrics verbatim from songs/*.md into
a new file — licensed lyrics in context AND in the output path, which is the shape
that blocked 6/6 on 7/26. No email is sent; nothing writes into the repo.

*** FINDING 1 — THE MINIMAL REPRO DOES NOT TRIP THE FILTER. This is important. ***
  ARM: cloud, claude-sonnet-5, normal subscription auth.
  RESULT: PASSED in 15.6s. Read, Read, Write. is_error=False. 1318 bytes,
  53 non-blank lines, both songs present, verbatim. NO content-filter 400.

So "copyrighted lyrics in context and in output" is NOT sufficient to trip it. The
trigger is narrower than bs-a1f's refined theory states. What is different about the
real 7/26 failure, and therefore what the trigger probably needs:
  - the lyrics arrived as PASTED TEXT IN AN EMAIL, not as a repo file the agent read;
  - the run carried the full SYSTEM_PROMPT, the Gmail + deck MCP servers, and ~40
    tool calls across a ~175KB transcript;
  - the songs were specifically The Lord Will Provide / Goodness of God /
    All Hail King Jesus, none of which are in songs/ (that run died before saving
    them, so we cannot reconstruct the exact input).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS SPIKE AND FOR bs-dox: any claim that a fallback "fixes" the
filter MUST be demonstrated on the real thread or a faithful fixture of it. A green
run on a synthetic lyric-copy task proves nothing — this arm just proved that. It
also means we currently have NO reliable local reproduction of the failure, which
should be fixed before trusting any fix. Consider building a 0726 eval fixture from
the real thread if the email is still in the mailbox.

*** FINDING 2 — bs-zzq CONFIRMED IN THE WILD (unplanned bonus). ***
The proxy arm failed and the SDK exception was literally
    Exception: Claude Code returned an error result: success
while the real reason sat in the assistant's last text block. Exactly the defect
bs-zzq describes, observed live. Evidence added to bs-zzq.

*** BLOCKED — the proxy cannot accept tool definitions for the OpenAI path. ***
  ARM: proxy, gpt-5.6-terra.
  RESULT: FAILED in 190s, zero tool calls, no output file.
    API Error: 502 Provider error: Client error '400 Bad Request'
    for url 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'

Bisected with curl: plain text OK, system prompt OK, ANY request with `tools` -> 400,
streaming or not, for every schema variant including an empty-properties one. The
bug is the tool ENVELOPE, not the schema. Filed as its own issue (see the
UniClaudeProxy OpenAI tool-translation bug), which now blocks this one.

ALSO: claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5 now pass through to api.anthropic.com and
return 401 — a regression against bs-dox's recorded mapping, and useless for our
purpose regardless since Anthropic traffic is exactly what the filter applies to.
`bonsai` was not yet started ("All connection attempts failed"); Thomas will bring
it up so bs-fxj can be attempted separately.

ENV SEAM CONFIRMED WORKING, for what it is worth: options.env reached the CLI and
redirected it to the proxy — the failure is upstream of us, at the proxy's
translation, not in the harness patch. The CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="" override
behaved as predicted and the CLI logged only the harmless
"claude.ai connectors are disabled" warning.

NEXT, in order:
1. Fix the proxy's OpenAI request-direction tool translation (blocking issue), and
   while in there surface the upstream error body — it would have answered this in
   one request instead of six.
2. Re-run probe_filter.py --backend proxy --model gpt-5.6-terra. Expect Read, Read,
   Write and a written file.
3. Only then run the capability arm: the real eval suite against gpt-5.6-terra
   through the proxy. tests/eval/eval_harness.py is the right vehicle — fresh
   workspace, seeded song library, and send_reply is a stand-in that records the
   body, so NO mail reaches the minister. Patch its ClaudeAgentOptions
   (eval_harness.py:224) with the same env block probe_filter.py uses.
4. Build a faithful 7/26 reproduction, because per Finding 1 we do not have one.

================================================================
2026-07-30 (later) — SPIKE ANSWERED. The premise is FALSIFIED.
Provider-swapping does NOT solve this. Recommend abandoning bs-dox
Approach A and building deterministic extraction instead.
================================================================

Thomas fixed the proxy (bs-c2e). Re-verified before re-running: gpt-5.6-terra now
accepts tools on BOTH paths — non-streaming returns a populated
input {"text":"banana"}, and the streaming input_json_delta fragments concatenate
correctly. Transport is fully green.

RESULT 1 — TRANSPORT AND TOOL USE: PASS.
The real SDK harness drove gpt-5.6-terra through the proxy and it issued correct
tool calls with correct arguments (Bash, Read x3). The options.env seam, the
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="" override, and the whole plumbing work. Nothing left to
prove here.

RESULT 2 — THE MODEL REFUSES. DETERMINISTICALLY. 2/2 runs.
    "Sorry, I can't reproduce or compile the complete lyrics of these
     copyrighted songs."
This is a MODEL-LEVEL REFUSAL, not an API content filter. It arrives with
is_error=False and no error status — the run looks superficially successful and
simply produces nothing. The prompt explicitly stated the church's CCLI license and
that these are our own licensed copies; it did not help.

RESULT 3 — THE PREMISE IS INVERTED. Cloud Sonnet PASSED the identical task
(15.6s, Read/Read/Write, 53 lines, verbatim, no 400). So on this task Anthropic was
MORE permissive than the OpenAI-backed model.

=> The whole "reach a non-Anthropic provider and the problem goes away" thesis that
bs-dox and this spike were built on is WRONG. Copyright-reproduction guardrails are
an industry norm, not an Anthropic policy quirk. Swapping providers trades an
Anthropic 400 for an OpenAI refusal. bs-dox Approach A should not be built.

RESULT 4 — THE FIX IS TO STOP ASKING A MODEL TO REPRODUCE LYRICS AT ALL.
Copying text is not a language task. Probe scratchpad/probe_copy.py gives the model
the same job but forbids it from emitting any lyric text, telling it to move the
bytes with shell instead. Both providers then succeed:

  gpt-5.6-terra : 1 Bash call, 6.4s, no refusal, correct file, NO lyrics in model text
  claude-sonnet-5: 2 Bash calls, 12.9s, no refusal, correct file, NO lyrics in model text

Same task the model refused outright when asked to retype it. This is the design.

RESULT 5 — BUT MODEL-AUTHORED SHELL IS NOT "DETERMINISTIC". IMPORTANT CAVEAT.
gpt-5.6-terra's one-liner was subtly WRONG: it duplicated stanza headings
(## Chorus, ## Verse 2 and ## Bridge each emitted twice; 16 headings instead of 10).
The lyric BYTES were exact — no hallucination — but the structure was mangled, and a
mangled stanza structure is a broken deck. Sonnet got it right, but only because it
ran an inspection pass (grep -n for frontmatter and heading offsets) before building
the command; it earned correctness rather than being guaranteed it.

CONCLUSION: the extraction must be a FIXED, TESTED TOOL — not shell the model writes
on the fly. That is exactly this repo's existing rule for build-deck.js
(CLAUDE.md: "the model emits data, not slide markup — if a slide is wrong, fix
build-deck.js, not the HTML"), and it should apply here identically. The model's job
is to identify WHICH text is which song and WHERE it starts and ends; a pinned
script does the copying.

STILL UNRESOLVED, AND IT MATTERS: this addresses the OUTPUT half only. bs-a1f's
attempt 3 blocked on the first assistant turn after get_thread having written
nothing at all, which means lyrics merely being IN CONTEXT was enough that time. So
the design needs BOTH halves: get_thread must redact/stash lyric blocks so they
never enter the model's context, AND a pinned tool must do the copying so they never
enter its output. Building only the copy half would leave the 7/26 failure mode
intact.

ALSO STILL TRUE FROM THE EARLIER SESSION: we have NO faithful local reproduction of
the original 7/26 filter trip — the minimal repro passes on cloud. Any claim that
this design fixes the real failure must be demonstrated against the real thread or a
fixture built from it.

VERDICT ON THIS SPIKE: answered. Do not proceed to bs-dox Approach A. The follow-up
work is the deterministic redact-and-extract design, filed separately.
close_reason: Spike answered 2026-07-30. Premise falsified: gpt-5.6-terra refuses copyrighted lyric reproduction deterministically (2/2) while cloud Sonnet does not, so provider-swapping does not clear the problem. Transport/tool use proven green. Follow-up is bs-8qs (redact + pinned extraction tool); bs-dox Approach A should not be built.

title: Fall back to a different provider when the API returns a content-filter 400
description:
Approach A (whole-run fallback), chosen 2026-07-27 over narrowing the model's output path. Rationale: per bs-a1f, lyrics merely being IN CONTEXT is enough to trip the filter, so no amount of output-shaping fixes it, and the roadmap (bs-fsx caesura placement, verse amendments from the minister, reasoning over stanza order) all inherently require lyric text in context AND in output. Fix it once at the transport layer instead of chasing it feature by feature.

MECHANISM (verified against the installed SDK, not from memory):
- claude_agent_sdk types.py:1819-1827 exposes ClaudeAgentOptions.model and .fallback_model.
- fallback_model is NOT usable here: it swaps models within Anthropic's API, and the content filter is not model-specific. Do not reach for it.
- The real seam is ClaudeAgentOptions.env, merged into the CLI subprocess at _internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py:486-521, where explicit options.env always wins over inherited env.
- The bundled CLI honors ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS and ANTHROPIC_MODEL (confirmed by string-scanning _bundled/claude).

TRIGGER: harness.py already re-raises AgentError carrying 'API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy'. Match on that and re-run against the local endpoint.

RETRY POLICY: a content-filter 400 is not transient (6/6 on 7/26). Attempt 1 goes to the cloud; on a filter block go STRAIGHT to local rather than burning the remaining cloud attempts. Today that wastes ~8 minutes before the minister hears anything.

TARGET: a 27B (PrismML Bonsai) served by LM Studio elsewhere on the network. URL TBD.

OPEN QUESTION — blocking implementation: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL expects Anthropic's /v1/messages. LM Studio's server is OpenAI-shaped (/v1/chat/completions). Confirm whether current LM Studio can serve an Anthropic-compatible endpoint; if not, put LiteLLM proxy in front of it. Verify before writing code.

RISK to measure once running: the fallback re-runs the WHOLE agentic loop cold (Gmail MCP, gen_service, deck JSON, build-deck.js, publish, reply) — not just the blocked step. Multi-step tool use is the weakest area for a local model. If it thrashes, the follow-up is approach B: keep the cloud model orchestrating and route only lyric-touching work to the local one. Do not build B pre-emptively; measure A first.

ALSO CHECK: the 7/26 transcript was ~175KB of JSONL before it died. Confirm the local model's context window and its behaviour near the top of it.
acceptance_criteria: A run that hits 'Output blocked by content filtering policy' automatically re-runs against the local endpoint and completes the deck + reply, with no lyric-shaped work removed from the model. The thread is pinned to the backend that served it (bs-1x4). A filter block does not consume the remaining cloud retry attempts.
notes:
================================================================
2026-07-28 — ENDPOINT VERIFIED FROM THE AGENT HOST. Open question RESOLVED.
================================================================

NO LiteLLM NEEDED. Thomas runs **UniClaudeProxy** in front of the LLM; it accepts
Anthropic-shaped /v1/messages and forwards to the appropriate OpenAI-compatible
endpoint. The earlier concern about LM Studio's OpenAI-only surface is moot.

ENDPOINT (current homelab address — TREAT AS VOLATILE, Thomas says it may change):
  http://192.168.0.48:9223

REACHABILITY — verified from this agent host (192.168.0.236/24, same /24):
  TCP 192.168.0.48:9223 -> OPEN
  GET  /            -> 200  {"status":"ok","provider":"UniClaudeProxy"}
  GET  /health      -> 200  {"status":"ok"}
  GET  /v1/messages -> 405  (route exists, POST-only — this is the good answer)
  GET  /messages    -> 404
  GET  /v1/models   -> 404  (no model listing; you cannot enumerate the mapping)

=> ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must be exactly "http://192.168.0.48:9223" (no path).
   The CLI appends /v1/messages itself. Do NOT append /v1 or /messages yourself.

NOTE the host also has a tailscale address (100.69.94.72). If the 192.168.0.x lease
moves, a tailnet name is the more stable way to address the proxy. Either way the
URL MUST be config/env-driven — never hardcode it. Suggested: LOCAL_API_BASE_URL
in config.py alongside agent_model, defaulting empty and disabling fallback when unset.

AUTH: none required. The probe POSTs above carried no x-api-key and no Authorization
header and were served. The bundled CLI may still insist on ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
being non-empty — if so, any dummy string will do. Verify; do not assume.

*** MODEL ALIAS TRAP — this WILL bite a naive implementation ***
The proxy resolves models through an internal "config models mapping" and rejects
anything else with:
  {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error",
    "message":"Model 'X' not found in config models mapping"}}
Tested: claude-opus-5 -> WORKS. claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-5, bonsai,
default -> all rejected.

The harness sends config.agent_model, which is "claude-sonnet-5"
(agent/src/email_agent/config.py:93, AGENT_MODEL env, chosen to keep API cost down).
**That alias is NOT mapped by the proxy.** So swapping only ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL fails
instantly on model resolution. The fallback MUST also override the model — either
via ClaudeAgentOptions.model or the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var — to an alias the proxy
maps (currently "claude-opus-5", which the proxy routes to PrismML Bonsai 27B).
Make that alias configurable too; it is the proxy's key, not a real Anthropic model.

WIRE FORMAT CONFIRMED GOOD (plain generation):
  POST /v1/messages {"model":"claude-opus-5","max_tokens":128,
                     "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: OK"}]}
  -> {"id":"msg_...","type":"message","role":"assistant",
      "content":[{"type":"text","text":"OK"}],"stop_reason":"end_turn",
      "usage":{"input_tokens":15,"output_tokens":102,
               "cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":0}}
Correct Anthropic envelope, correct stop_reason, usage fields present. Errors also
come back in the proper Anthropic error envelope, so SDK error handling should work.

*** BLOCKED: tool arguments are dropped in translation — see bs-qku (P0) ***
tool_use blocks come back with the right NAME and stop_reason but input is ALWAYS {},
reproducibly, even with forced tool_choice. Since every SDK capability (Read, Write,
Edit, Bash, mcp__gmail__get_thread) is a tool call, the fallback agent would be able
to do nothing at all. Do not write harness code against this endpoint until bs-qku
is fixed and its acceptance check passes — otherwise you will build against an
endpoint that returns plausible-looking turns which accomplish nothing.

STILL UNTESTED (do these once bs-qku lands):
  - Request-direction translation: does the proxy accept Anthropic tool_result
    blocks on the way IN? Only the response direction has been exercised.
  - Streaming (the SDK streams; only non-streaming POSTs were probed).
  - System prompts, and the large multi-tool payload the real agent sends.
  - Context headroom: the 7/26 transcript was ~175KB of JSONL before it died.
  - Whether Bonsai can actually drive the loop end to end (the bs-dox risk note).

REVISED SEQUENCING: bs-1x4 (backend column) is still the right first task and is
unblocked. bs-qku now gates the actual fallback wiring.

================================================================
2026-07-28 (later) — GREEN. End-to-end SDK run against the proxy PASSES.
================================================================
Thomas mapped Sonnet in the proxy config and tweaked tool translation. Re-probed:

1. MODEL ALIAS FIXED. claude-sonnet-5 now resolves, so config.agent_model
   ("claude-sonnet-5", config.py:93) works as-is. The fallback still SHOULD pin
   the model explicitly rather than rely on the proxy's mapping staying in sync
   with whatever AGENT_MODEL happens to be — but it is no longer a hard blocker.

2. THE TOOL-ARGUMENT SCARE WAS A NON-STREAMING-ONLY BUG (bs-qku, now P3).
   The SDK streams, and the streaming path carries arguments correctly.
   bs-qku has been removed as a dependency of this issue.

3. VERIFIED END TO END with the real SDK (scratchpad probe_sdk.py):
     ClaudeAgentOptions(
         model="claude-sonnet-5",
         allowed_tools=["Write","Read"],
         permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
         env={"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://192.168.0.48:9223",
              "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "unused-but-set",
              "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": ""},
     )
   Prompt: write probe.txt containing "banana".
   Result:
     TOOL Write input={'file_path': './probe.txt', 'content': 'banana'}
     file created: True, contents: 'banana'
     ResultMessage.is_error: False
   The local model planned, called a tool with correct arguments, wrote the file,
   and closed the turn cleanly. The options.env seam works exactly as designed.

4. AUTH: setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<any string> is
   sufficient. The CLI prints "claude.ai connectors are disabled because
   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or another auth source is set" — HARMLESS for us: the Gmail
   and deck tools are in-process SDK MCP servers passed via mcp_servers= at
   harness.py:143, not claude.ai org connectors. Nothing is lost.

WHAT THIS MEANS: the transport seam is proven. The remaining risk is purely
CAPABILITY — whether Bonsai can drive the full loop (Gmail MCP, gen_service,
deck JSON, build-deck.js, publish, reply), not whether the plumbing works.
Implementation can proceed as soon as bs-1x4 lands.

STILL UNTESTED before trusting it on a Sunday:
  - Multi-turn tool_result round trip (request-direction translation).
  - The real agent's large multi-tool payload + system prompt.
  - Context headroom: the 7/26 transcript was ~175KB before it died.
  - A full dry run against a real thread with the filter deliberately tripped.

MINOR OBSERVATION: the model is verbose before answering — 102 output tokens to
reply "OK", and max_tokens=64 returned empty text with stop_reason=max_tokens.
Give max_tokens generous headroom on the fallback path.
================================================================
2026-07-29 — REFRAMED. The fallback target is a PROVIDER, not "local".
Retitled. Two blockers added, one dependency removed.
================================================================

THE FRAMING WAS TOO NARROW. This issue was written as "fall back to a LOCAL
model", which quietly binds two independent choices together:

  PROVIDER  — the content filter is Anthropic-side POLICY. Anything non-Anthropic
              should clear it. "Local" is one way to be non-Anthropic; it is not
              the only way and not obviously the best one.
  CAPABILITY — can the target actually drive Gmail MCP -> gen_service -> deck JSON
              -> build-deck.js -> publish -> reply?

The 27B changes both at once, and CAPABILITY is the doubtful half — this issue
already concedes that ("the remaining risk is purely CAPABILITY"). A non-Anthropic
FRONTIER model reached through the same UniClaudeProxy changes only PROVIDER and
leaves capability near-certain. Thomas can accommodate that with a different model
redirect in the proxy config; no new infrastructure.

So the implementation must be provider-agnostic: endpoint AND model alias both
config-driven, with the local 27B as one configurable target rather than THE
target. Suggested keys stay as sketched above (LOCAL_API_BASE_URL -> rename to
something neutral like FALLBACK_API_BASE_URL / FALLBACK_MODEL), defaulting empty
and disabling the fallback when unset.

MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING — this is now enforced by dependency, not just advice:
  bs-e4m (P1)  frontier model via the proxy. Blocks this issue.
  bs-fxj (P1)  the 27B, only if bs-e4m is not the answer. Blocked by bs-e4m.
Both run the REAL harness against the known-bad 7/26 material (the copyrighted set
that failed 6/6), not a fresh synthetic case. Whichever wins, this issue then wires
the winner in. If bs-fxj shows the 27B cannot drive the loop, Approach A is dead
and this issue gets REWRITTEN as Approach B (cloud orchestrates, only lyric-touching
work routes out), not patched.

THE TRIGGER AS SPECIFIED DOES NOT FIRE RELIABLY — see bs-zzq (P1), now blocking.
This issue says "harness.py already re-raises AgentError carrying 'API Error: 400
Output blocked by content filtering policy'. Match on that." That holds ONLY when
the SDK itself raises. When the CLI reports failure via ResultMessage.is_error,
harness.py:198 raises an AgentError whose message is the bare result subtype
(the useless "success" of bs-zwj), and the enrichment branch at :217 declines to
touch it precisely BECAUSE it is already an AgentError. last_text is holding the
real reason and it is thrown away. Both paths occur in the wild. Fix bs-zzq first
or the fallback silently never fires on that path.

ENV TRAP THE VERIFIED PROBE DID NOT COVER: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
config.py:136 assert_subscription_auth() REQUIRES it non-empty in the parent
process, and subprocess_cli merges the parent env into the child — so it reaches
the CLI and may win over the proxy. The green probe in the notes above ran as a
standalone scratchpad script that likely had no token set, so its four-key env
block may NOT reproduce inside the real harness. Blank it explicitly in
options.env. (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is fine: the guard raises only if it is truthy, so
exporting it empty passes.)

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, unanswered here and needed before implementation:
ON FALLBACK, DOES THE RE-RUN RESUME THE SAME session_id?
  - Resume: the fallback model inherits a transcript written by another model and
    ending in a filter abort.
  - Fresh: it redoes the work cold, which is what the "re-runs the WHOLE agentic
    loop" risk note above is about, and loses whatever the first attempt achieved.
Neither is obviously right. Decide it explicitly rather than letting resume=
default into one of them.

bs-1x4 DEPENDENCY REMOVED. Fallback happens INSIDE one run_agent call, so a thread
resumed on the wrong backend costs latency (it re-trips the filter and falls back
again), not attempts — the bs-9ed 3-attempt bound is unaffected. bs-1x4 is a
coherence fix worth doing, not a prerequisite, and blocking on it delayed the only
work that helps on a Sunday.

================================================================
2026-07-30 — DO NOT BUILD THIS AS SPECIFIED. bs-e4m falsified the premise.
================================================================

This issue rests on "the content filter is Anthropic-side policy, so reach a
different provider and it goes away". MEASURED, AND IT IS FALSE.

  gpt-5.6-terra via the proxy, asked to reproduce copyrighted lyrics into a file:
    "Sorry, I can't reproduce or compile the complete lyrics of these copyrighted
     songs."  — deterministic, 2/2 runs, is_error=False so it LOOKS like success.
  cloud claude-sonnet-5, identical task: PASSED, 53 lines, verbatim, no 400.

So on this task Anthropic was the MORE permissive provider. Copyright-reproduction
guardrails are an industry norm, not an Anthropic quirk — there is no provider to
escape to. A fallback would trade an Anthropic 400 for an OpenAI refusal, and the
refusal is arguably worse operationally because it returns is_error=False and simply
produces nothing.

The transport work this issue specified is nonetheless PROVEN GOOD and should not be
thrown away if it is ever needed: options.env reaches the CLI, the
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN="" override behaves as predicted, and after bs-c2e the proxy
drives a real multi-tool SDK run correctly. The plumbing was never the problem.

SUPERSEDED BY bs-8qs — keep lyrics out of the model entirely: redact them in
get_thread so they never enter context, and copy them with a pinned, golden-tested
tool so they never enter output. That removes the failure mode by construction
instead of routing around it, keeps everything on subscription-billed Sonnet, and
drops the proxy, the homelab availability risk and the backend-pinning work with it.

Leaving this issue OPEN rather than closing it, because if bs-8qs's redaction half
turns out to be infeasible we may still need a fallback — but it must not be built
on the "another provider will just do it" assumption, which is now disproven.
close_reason:
Done, but not as specified — shipped as always-on routing rather than a 400-triggered fallback.

This issue described re-running against another provider ON a content-filter 400. What shipped (5520919) is simpler: AGENT_BASE_URL points the agent's CLI subprocess at any Anthropic-compatible endpoint for EVERY run; unset means the subscription. No 400 detection, no retry path, no mixed-provenance transcript — which is why the bs-zzq and bs-1x4 blocking edges were removed rather than satisfied.

The mechanism this issue identified was correct and is what shipped: ClaudeAgentOptions.env, merged over the inherited environment. Ruling out fallback_model here was also correct.

The local-model half was overtaken twice: bs-qku (the LAN proxy returns empty tool_use.input) killed the proxy route, and Moonshot speaks Anthropic's /v1/messages natively, so no proxy is needed at all.

Security detail worth keeping: agent_env() BLANKS CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rather than omitting them. The overlay is merged, so an omitted key inherits the real subscription token and would post it to a third party. Covered by agent/tests/test_backend_routing.py.

title: gen_service: lyrics must come from songs/, never from the model's memory (drop PD rung)
description:
Follow-on to bs-8yd, which removed rung 3 (draft copyrighted lyrics from memory) in batch mode. This removes rung 2 as well -- writing out a public-domain hymn from memory -- and applies the rule in BOTH modes: lyrics must already be in songs/, or the song is title_only and we ask.

Motivation: a persistent Anthropic API content-policy block on a real sample flowchart (How Great Thou Art / A Mighty Fortress / The Lily of the Valley / Days of Elijah / Before the Throne of God Above / Revelation Song / My Jesus I Love Thee). Zero of those songs are in songs/, so a single batch run asked the model to produce five songs' worth of lyrics back to back -- three of them via rung 2, which is the skill working AS DESIGNED, not a guardrail failure.

Key insight: the copyright classifier reacts to the SHAPE of the output (a long verbatim lyric block), not to the legal status of the work. "Public domain" is a fact about the hymn; it is not a property the filter can see. So rung 2 is not the safe path the ladder assumed.

Why this costs less than it looks: batch mode already forced verified:false on looked-up hymns, so a human had to read those slides before Sunday anyway. The labor is relocated (minister pastes lyrics into a reply) rather than added, and it lands somewhere with a better failure mode.

Architecture note: the deck JSON contains no lyric text -- build-deck.js pulls it from songs/*.md and the model emits only slugs and section names. So once a song is in the library the model never handles lyric text at all. Exposure is confined to the cold-start path and decays as the library fills. This is NOT a scaling risk.

Not in scope, tracked separately: a deterministic hymnary.org importer (plain HTTP fetch + parse, no model in the loop) to restore the PD automation without classifier exposure; and OCR recovery of the existing JPEG decks in passages/2026-06-*, 2026-07-12 to seed the library from the church's real repertoire.
acceptance_criteria: gen_service.md's Resolving-a-song ladder has exactly two outcomes in both modes: in the library -> reference by slug; not in the library -> title_only plus an explicit request for the text. No rung instructs the model to write lyrics it is recalling. Batch mode's "Lyrics you don't have" section agrees with the ladder rather than describing a different one. The WebFetch caveat no longer implies the model should supply lyric text itself.
close_reason:
Done in 89f65c8. gen_service.md's ladder is now two outcomes in both modes: in the library, or title_only plus a request for the text. Batch mode's section no longer describes a separate ladder, the WebFetch caveat is scoped to confirming identity only, and specs/email-agent.md records the reasoning.

Also fixed the batch-mode eval, which asserted the behavior just removed -- it required that a public-domain hymn NOT be title_only. It now asserts the hymn is asked for AND that the ask reaches both report.missing and the reply, so the non-blocking property stays pinned.

NOT yet proven live. Tests pass (17 node, 86 pytest) but those do not exercise the model; the eval that does needs a real run against the sample flowchart. The hypothesis that lyric generation caused the content-filter block remains unconfirmed -- this change is also the experiment that tests it.

title: harness: capture the bundled CLI's stderr into our logs (opaque agent failures)
description: An unattended run on the homelab box failed 2026-07-18 with 'Claude Code returned an error result: success' and NO further detail. Root cause of the opacity: harness.py builds ClaudeAgentOptions without a stderr callback. The SDK's subprocess transport (subprocess_cli.py:532) pipes the CLI's stderr ONLY when options.stderr is set; otherwise stderr is left as None and the child inherits the parent's. Under systemd that SHOULD reach the journal, but on the box the journal carried nothing — so the real error was lost either way. When the CLI exits non-zero with is_error=true and an empty error body, the SDK falls back to the result subtype ('success'), which is the useless message we got. Add an stderr callback that logs each CLI stderr line tagged with the thread/message id, so the next opaque failure is legible at the point of failure instead of reconstructed from timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: ClaudeAgentOptions gets an stderr callback; each CLI stderr line is logged (WARNING) with thread/msg context. A run that fails leaves the CLI's own stderr in email_agent logs, not only (maybe) the journal. Existing 81 agent tests still pass; a test covers that the callback forwards lines to the logger.
close_reason: harness now registers ClaudeAgentOptions.stderr. Each CLI stderr line is captured into a bounded tail (STDERR_TAIL_LINES=50) and mirrored to DEBUG; on ANY run failure (including timeout cancellation) the tail is dumped at ERROR with thread/msg context, so the next opaque CLI failure is legible at the point of failure. Verified: thomas confirmed the journal caught nothing by inheritance on the 2026-07-18 failure, which is exactly why an explicit callback was needed. 3 tests added (capture+skip-blanks, tail-logged-on-failure, no-cry-wolf-on-clean-run); 84 agent tests pass.

title: No retry bound: a failing message retries every tick for 7 days — quota burn + silence to the minister
description:
VERIFIED BY READING THE CODE 2026-07-16, not theorised. There is NO attempt counter anywhere in the system. store.py's SCHEMA has three tables (threads, processed_messages, agent_sent_messages) and not one has an attempts/retry column; mark_failed() sets status=FAILED and updates a timestamp, incrementing nothing. dispatcher._dispatch_one() catches BaseException -> mark_failed() -> the message is deliberately NOT added to the ledger 'so the next pass retries it'. Nothing ever stops that retry.

CONSEQUENCE FOR UNATTENDED OPERATION. A message that fails persistently (content filtering per bs-a1f, a malformed attachment, a Node/build-deck.js failure, a bad deck) is retried on EVERY heartbeat for as long as it stays in the gate's window — AGENT_LOOKBACK_DAYS defaults to 7. Each retry is a full Sonnet run on the subscription. The per-thread claim serialises retries (so the true cadence is one-per-run-duration, not one-per-60s), but a fast-failing run still retries every minute or two, for a week. That is thousands of agent runs against the five-hour subscription quota, which would take out the agent's ability to serve any OTHER request too — including the real one on Saturday night.

AND THE MINISTER GETS SILENCE THE WHOLE TIME. The dispatcher's failure path releases the claim and retries; it never composes an 'I hit an error' reply. bs-a1f's acceptance criteria asserts that path ends in such a reply — IT DOES NOT EXIST. bs-a1f calls the retry 'unbounded-ish' and asks to 'confirm a filtered thread cannot retry forever'. Confirmed: it can, and it does. Filing separately because this is not specific to content filtering — it is the generic failure path for ANY persistent error, and it is a deployment blocker in a way a nondeterministic 12% filter trip is not.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BITTEN: every run so far has been operator-attended, where a human notices and kills it. Unattended on the homelab box, nobody is watching.

FIX SKETCH: add an attempts column keyed by msg_id (survives the process, unlike anything in memory); mark_failed increments it; the dispatcher skips a message past N attempts and, on crossing N, sends the 'I hit an error' reply ONCE and marks it processed so it leaves the retry pool. Note the reply-send itself can fail, so 'give up' must be terminal even if the apology does not send. Backoff is a weaker alternative — it slows the burn but the thread still never terminates and the minister still never hears.
acceptance_criteria: A message that fails N times stops being retried. Crossing the bound sends exactly one 'I hit an error' reply to the thread and marks the message processed so it leaves the retry pool. A poison message cannot consume unbounded subscription quota. Regression test: a run_agent that always raises results in a bounded number of calls, one apology reply, and no further attempts on subsequent passes.
notes: Found during the pre-deployment review for bs-tiz.6 (2026-07-16). Blocks unattended operation: this is the failure mode where the agent quietly eats the subscription and the minister hears nothing back.
close_reason: Retry bound landed. New message_attempts table (a new table, not a column: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS threads is a silent no-op against an existing state.db, so a column there would never materialize on the unattended box — absent row == zero attempts). Attempts counted BEFORE the run, so wedged/reaped runs that never reach except: are bounded too. Give-up holds the claim (one apology, not one per overlapping heartbeat) and mark_processed is in a finally, so a failed apology-send cannot rebuild the same infinite loop against Gmail. Apology routes through store=self.store so mark_agent_sent records authorship and the gate does not hand it back as a fresh request. Default 3 attempts via AGENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS. 7 new tests, mutation-checked; 81 pass.

title: healthcheck's 7-day token age is measured from a file that is rewritten hourly — the check can never fire
description:
healthcheck.py's _token_age_days() stats token.json's MTIME and calls it "days since the refresh token was issued". It is not. gmail_client.py:44 REWRITES token.json every time the access token is refreshed, which google-auth does whenever creds.valid is False — i.e. roughly HOURLY, since access tokens live ~1 hour. In a live agent polling every 60s the file is rewritten every hour forever, so the reported age never exceeds ~1 hour.

The 7-day branch is therefore DEAD CODE. It can never fire, so healthcheck can never deliver the one verdict it was written to deliver.
design:
MEASURED 2026-07-16, not theorised. bs-xy9 records consent on 2026-07-11 (~5 days ago). healthcheck today prints "WARN gmail: refresh token is only 0.0 days old". token.json's mtime is 10:09 today and its `expiry` field is 15:09Z — exactly one hour later — because the healthcheck's own gmail_service() call refreshed the access token and rewrote the file before _token_age_days() ever stat'd it. The check resets the clock it is trying to read.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: bs-xy9 is the issue that keeps the unattended agent from silently dying every 7 days (Google expires refresh tokens while an OAuth app is in "Testing"). Its recorded verification plan is: "RE-CHECK AFTER 2026-07-18: run healthcheck. If it still says OK, publishing genuinely took and this can be closed." That plan CANNOT SUCCEED — the check will report ~0.0 days on 07-18 and every day after. xy9 would sit open forever, or worse, be closed on a misreading.

THE DATA ISN'T IN THE FILE. token.json carries no issued-at for the refresh token — fields are account, client_id, client_secret, expiry, refresh_token, scopes, token, token_uri, universe_domain, and `expiry` is the ACCESS token's hourly expiry, not the refresh token's. So no amount of reading token.json can answer this; the consent time has to be recorded when consent happens.

FIX: have authorize.py durably record the consent timestamp — the SQLite store (already there, already the home for agent state) or a sidecar next to token.json — and have healthcheck compare against THAT. Two constraints worth respecting: (1) the record must survive a token refresh, which is the whole point; (2) it must NOT survive a re-consent, or a re-authorized token inherits the old token's age and the cliff looks cleared when it was just reset. authorize.py overwriting the record on every consent gets both.

ALTERNATIVE WORTH CONSIDERING: the real question is not "how old is the token" but "is the OAuth app published". That is directly readable — the token's age is only a PROXY for it, and a proxy chosen because the direct answer seemed unavailable. If the Cloud Console publishing status can be queried via API with the credentials we already have, that is a better check: no clock, no waiting until day 8, unambiguous.
acceptance_criteria: healthcheck reports the age of the REFRESH token (time since consent), not time since the last access-token refresh. With a token consented N days ago it reports ~N, and the >=7-day 'cliff cleared' verdict can actually fire. Re-consenting resets the reported age. bs-xy9's re-check plan works as written.
close_reason: Dead check DELETED rather than fixed (decided by thomas 2026-07-17). Its only consumer was bs-xy9's verification plan, and bs-xy9 was settled directly by reading the Cloud Console — the token age was always just a proxy for 'is the app published'. No signal lost: healthcheck's live getProfile call already fails loudly with invalid_grant the moment a token dies, for any reason. Module docstring rewritten; the 7-day Testing-cliff story is now history.

title: Set Gmail OAuth app to 'In production' — 7-day refresh-token expiry
description: The pre-existing token.json was dead with invalid_grant. Root cause: while an OAuth app's publishing status is 'Testing' in Google Cloud Console, Google expires refresh tokens after 7 DAYS. An unattended agent will therefore silently stop working every week — a miserable failure to debug on a Saturday night before a Sunday service. Set the app to 'In production' so refresh tokens are long-lived.
acceptance_criteria: OAuth app publishing status is 'In production'; the agent's token survives longer than 7 days without re-consent.
notes:
OAuth app PUBLISHED by user 2026-07-11; token deleted and re-consented. Refresh verified live (rotates correctly, gmail.modify present). BUT publishing cannot be confirmed from the token — a Testing-status refresh token and a published one are indistinguishable for the first 7 days, and the failure is silent. Added agent/src/email_agent/healthcheck.py: it reports the refresh token's age and only declares the cliff cleared once the token is >=7 days old AND still valid. RE-CHECK AFTER 2026-07-18: run 'uv run python -m email_agent.healthcheck'. If it still says OK, publishing genuinely took and this can be closed.

*** THAT RE-CHECK PLAN DOES NOT WORK — see bs-qka (2026-07-16). *** healthcheck measures token.json's MTIME, and gmail_client.py:44 rewrites that file on every access-token refresh (~hourly). So the reported age is "time since the last hourly refresh", never the refresh token's real age. Measured today: consent was 5 days ago, healthcheck prints "0.0 days old". On 2026-07-18 it will print ~0.0 too, and every day after. Do NOT close this issue on a healthcheck reading until bs-qka is fixed — and do not read a low number as evidence of anything.

The underlying question (is the OAuth app actually 'In production'?) is still open and still matters: it is what stops the unattended agent dying silently every 7 days. bs-qka's design notes a better angle — query the publishing status directly rather than inferring it from a clock.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

RESOLVED 2026-07-17 BY DIRECT OBSERVATION. thomas read the Google Cloud Console and confirmed the OAuth app's publishing status is "In production", not "Testing". That is the authoritative answer to this issue's actual question, and it closes it.

WHY THIS DOES NOT NEED bs-qka AFTER ALL. This issue was blocked on bs-qka because the planned verification was a healthcheck token-age reading — but the token's age was only ever a PROXY for "is the app published", chosen back when the direct answer seemed unavailable. bs-qka's own design notes called this out: "the real question is not 'how old is the token' but 'is the OAuth app published'. That is directly readable." It was. Reading the console settled in seconds what the proxy could not have settled before 2026-07-18, and could not have settled at all while the proxy was broken. The dependency on bs-qka is therefore removed rather than satisfied.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, honestly assessed: "publishing status is 'In production'" — CONFIRMED directly. "the agent's token survives longer than 7 days without re-consent" — not yet observed (consent was 2026-07-11; day 7 is 2026-07-18). Closing anyway: that criterion was written as a way to INFER the publishing status, and we now have the status itself from the source of truth. Waiting two days to corroborate a fact we can already read would be superstition.

ONGOING PROTECTION, so this is not a silent cliff again: healthcheck already makes a LIVE Gmail getProfile call, which fails loudly with invalid_grant the moment a refresh token dies for any reason — reverted publishing status, revoked consent, anything. Run on a schedule, that is what makes it fail on a Tuesday instead of Saturday night. It does not depend on the token-age check at all. See bs-qka for the fate of that check.
close_reason: OAuth app publishing status confirmed 'In production' by direct reading of the Google Cloud Console (thomas, 2026-07-17). The token-age proxy was never needed; the direct answer settled it. Ongoing token death is caught by healthcheck's live getProfile call, independent of the broken age check (bs-qka).

title: Agent harness (Python Claude Agent SDK) with per-thread session resume
description: The broad 'handle-an-email' agent entry point, built on the Python Claude Agent SDK (Python chosen to match the Gmail tooling and attachment-conversion story). Launched by the dispatcher with a threadId + session_id: new session for an initiating email, resume for a reply so full prior context (including what it told the minister and his corrections) is restored. Deliberately NOT narrowed to gen_service — it is given the Gmail tools plus access to its skills and instructed to discover intent from the message and dispatch to the right skill. For this POC the one skill it drives is gen_service (invoked via its non-interactive batch contract). Architected broad so future skills slot in without rework.
design: Build on Python 'claude-agent-sdk' (Claude Code as a library). Confirmed-from-docs primitives (proven hands-on by bs-tiz.7): resume via ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id), session_id captured from the init SystemMessage; gen_service auto-loads from .claude/ (setting_sources) so NO skill-invocation bridge is needed — the harness gives the model the Gmail tools + its skills and lets it dispatch. Prior art: Anthropic's official email-assistant example, github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-demos — read before building. Note AskUserQuestion is a built-in SDK tool but does NOT apply here (no interactive user) — reinforces the non-interactive/report design in bs-ixn/bs-tiz.5.
acceptance_criteria: Agent starts from a threadId+session_id; an initiating email creates a session and a reply resumes the same session with prior context intact; the agent reads the message, retrieves attachments as needed, infers intent, and invokes gen_service via the batch contract; adding a second skill later requires no change to the harness.
notes:
DONE AND LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-12 (agent/src/email_agent/harness.py). Held open only by its dependency on bs-ixn — do NOT rebuild it. Proven end-to-end: a real 'AI:' email was read, handled on Sonnet, and answered with a correct in-thread reply; session_id persisted and resumed on the next tick.

Design points that must not be regressed:
- Broad 'handle-an-email' system prompt, NOT a gen_service wrapper — adding a second skill must not require touching this file.
- setting_sources=['project'] makes .claude/ skills visible. Omit it and the agent silently has NOTHING to dispatch to — no error, it just can't see the skills.
- permission_mode='bypassPermissions' — headless, nobody can approve a tool prompt.
- A run must end in send_reply OR skip_reply (TERMINAL_TOOLS). Deciding NOTHING is the error, because the dispatcher's commit boundary would drop the request silently. (An earlier version demanded a reply; that is what made the agent answer its own mail — see bs-c8y. Do not reintroduce it.)
close_reason: Unblocked by bs-ixn and closed. Both were DONE and live-verified on 2026-07-11/12 and were only held open by their dependency on bs-ixn (batch mode), which is now complete. No further work was needed on either.

title: Deterministic Gmail tools: getMessage, listAttachments, getAttachmentBinary, sendReply
description: The narrow, deterministic tool surface the agent uses to interact with Gmail (reusing existing OAuth creds). Four tools: getMessage(msgId) → headers + body; listAttachments(msgId) → attachment metadata (filename, extension, size, mimeType); getAttachmentBinary(msgId, attachmentId) → raw bytes; sendReply(threadId, body, attachments?) → replies IN-THREAD via In-Reply-To/References so the conversation stays one thread. Deliberately does NOT convert attachments — the agent handles conversion itself (it can pip install and turn a PDF/Word doc into text/markdown as needed). Tools stop at binary + metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Agent can retrieve a message's body and headers; can list attachment metadata and fetch raw bytes for each; sendReply lands as a reply within the original thread (correct In-Reply-To/References); no format conversion happens inside the tools.
notes: CREDENTIAL FINDING (blocks live verification): the pre-existing token.json (dated Mar 2025) is DEAD — refresh fails with 'invalid_grant'. Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days while an OAuth app's publishing status is still 'Testing'. The requested scope in the file is gmail.modify (read+send), which IS sufficient for sendReply, so the design holds — but the token must be regenerated. One-time consent script written at agent/src/email_agent/authorize.py (uv run python -m email_agent.authorize). To survive unattended, the OAuth app must be set to 'In production' in Google Cloud Console, or the 7-day expiry will keep killing the agent.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested (40 tests green). Live Gmail verification pending credential refresh — tracked separately.

title: Dispatcher + SQLite state store (idempotency, in-flight lock, thread→session map)
description: The component the ideation implies but doesn't name. Consumes the gate's {threadId, msgId} list and owns all cross-run state in a small SQLite DB: threadId → {session_id, last_processed_msgId, status, updated_at}. For each actionable thread it (a) skips messages already acted on, (b) skips threads currently in-flight via a transactional 'claim', and (c) maps the thread to a Claude Agent SDK session_id (new for an initial message, resume for a reply). SQLite over a JSON file specifically because the heartbeat overlaps itself — slide generation can take minutes and a JSON read/write race would double-process a thread; SQLite gives a transactional claim for free. This table is the single source of truth for 'have we handled this' and 'which session belongs to this thread'.
design: SCOPE NARROWED by Agent SDK: the SDK persists the full conversation transcript as JSONL on our filesystem, so this store does NOT hold conversation history — only the mapping/bookkeeping: threadId -> {session_id, last_processed_msgId, status, updated_at}. session_id is the Agent SDK session captured from the init SystemMessage (new session for an initial email; ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id) for a reply). SQLite still warranted for the transactional in-flight claim (overlapping heartbeats + minutes-long slide generation).
acceptance_criteria: A schema exists for threadId→{session_id,last_processed_msgId,status,updated_at}; re-running the heartbeat while a thread is in-flight does NOT launch a second agent for it; a reply resolves to the same session_id as its initiating message; an already-processed message is not reprocessed.
notes:
DONE AND LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-11 (store.py, dispatcher.py, heartbeat.py). Held open only by its dependency on bs-tiz.4 -> bs-ixn — do NOT rebuild it. Transactional claim is mutation-tested (swap it for read-then-write and the concurrency tests fail). Stale-claim reaping, thread→session mapping, and idempotency all proven; re-running the heartbeat on an answered thread processes 0 and sends nothing.

Two tables, both needed: processed_messages (idempotency ledger — last_processed_msg_id alone cannot prevent a duplicate reply when the gate re-emits an older message) and agent_sent_messages (authorship; surfaced to the agent as a HINT by get_thread, and a cheap dispatcher fast-path). 'We wrote it' and 'we handled it' are deliberately separate facts.
close_reason: Unblocked by bs-ixn and closed. Both were DONE and live-verified on 2026-07-11/12 and were only held open by their dependency on bs-ixn (batch mode), which is now complete. No further work was needed on either.

title: Email gate: CRON poll + subject-regex intent filter
description: Deterministic entry point for the email agent (no LLM). A heartbeat (~60s CRON for POC; later a Lambda+EventBridge timer) polls the shared Gmail inbox using existing OAuth creds and identifies ONLY messages the agent should act on. Applies a configurable subject-line regex (e.g. 'AI:', 'Calvary AI', 'media AI') and deterministically classifies initial-message vs reply (e.g. Re: / References header). Fetches metadata only, not content — its sole job is to emit a list of {threadId, msgId} for the dispatcher. Everything downstream (reading bodies, attachments, deciding intent) is left to the agent. Rationale: since the inbox is a shared personal Gmail during POC, we need a deterministic gate so the agent never 'wakes up and reads whatever is there' — it only ever acts on messages explicitly addressed to it.
acceptance_criteria: Subject pattern and poll interval are configurable; a matching new email and a matching reply are both detected and correctly classified; non-matching mail is ignored; output is a list of {threadId, msgId} with no message bodies fetched; no LLM call in this component.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested (40 tests green). Live Gmail verification pending credential refresh — tracked separately.

title: Deterministic build script: model emits structured data, script renders HTML
description: Today the model hand-writes slide markup and manually splices it into the template (replace the <!-- SLIDES --> line) — a large exact-syntax surface a cheap model gets subtly wrong (unclosed divs, dropped scrim, mis-padded Slide numbers). Move HTML out of the model: define a structured intermediate (JSON list of segments/slides with type + text fields) and a small deterministic build script that renders templates/service-slides-template.html from it. The model's only job becomes producing well-formed data. Foundational: also absorbs the stanza-split and slide-numbering risks.
acceptance_criteria: A documented JSON schema for the deck; a build script that renders the preview HTML from JSON deterministically; gen_service updated to emit JSON rather than raw HTML; example (2026-06-28) reproducible via the script.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested (40 tests green). Live Gmail verification pending credential refresh — tracked separately.

title: gen_service: library-first lyrics, no drafting-from-memory in batch mode
description: Current rule tells the model to draft copyrighted lyrics from memory and self-assess when it doesn't know — exactly the calibrated self-knowledge a small model is worst at, and the VERIFY flag is preview-only so nobody catches a hallucination in an unattended pipeline. For batch mode: project lyrics ONLY if already in songs/ or clearly public-domain-fetchable; everything else gets a title slide only and a 'needs lyrics' line in the report. Removes the fabrication surface entirely.
acceptance_criteria: In batch mode the model never invents lyrics; a song not in the library and not PD-fetchable yields a title-only slide + report entry; interactive mode may retain the drafted-with-VERIFY behavior if desired.
notes:
Why this matters more than it looks: the agent runs unattended on Sonnet with NOBODY in the loop to catch an invented verse before it reaches the sanctuary screen. gen_service.md today still permits drafting lyrics from memory for copyrighted songs (resolution rule 3: 'draft the best-known lyrics, save with verified: false'). That is defensible with a human reviewing; it is not defensible in batch mode.

Related, already handled deterministically: scripts/build-deck.js (bs-c16) now refuses placeholder/unknown sections and reports them as 'missing' rather than rendering them. See bs-1nn for the live near-miss — songs/his-name-is-jesus.md contained a literal '(paste lyrics here — song identity unconfirmed)' inside a Verse 1 section, which the old all-sections default would have projected.

Batch mode should: use the library or say 'I don't have these lyrics, send them' in the report. Never draft from memory.
close_reason: Done as part of batch mode. gen_service.md rule 3 (draft best-known lyrics from memory) is now marked INTERACTIVE ONLY; batch mode's ladder is library -> PD lookup (saved verified:false) -> title_only + ask. EVAL-PROVEN, not just documented: tests/eval/test_batch_mode.py runs the real model and asserts it. In the 7/12 run the agent wrote songs/forever-yahweh.md and songs/jesus.md with NO lyrics at all — frontmatter, a VERIFY comment, title_only in the deck, and a 'need lyrics' line in the report. It even identified Forever YHWH as Elevation Worship and recorded the copyright rather than reaching for the text.

title: gen_service: non-interactive batch mode
description: gen_service is currently built entirely around a human in the loop (ask one segment at a time, echo the running order for correction, 'ask if unsure'). The email agent has no interactive user. Add a non-interactive mode: the entire order of service arrives as one input (the emailed 'flowchart'); the model resolves everything in a single pass and NEVER blocks on a question. Anything it would have asked becomes a line in a structured report returned with the deck link (verify-these / missing-these). Biggest structural gap for the email agent and independent of model size.
acceptance_criteria: Skill documents an explicit non-interactive mode; running with a full order-of-service input produces a deck plus a report with zero blocking questions; ambiguities/missing items surface in the report, not as prompts.
notes:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-07-12 from examples/flowcharts.md + user answers. Read that file before touching this.

REFRAME — 'zero blocking questions' in the original acceptance criteria is MISLEADING. The agent asks questions constantly; it asks them BY EMAIL. The real invariant: never block the PROCESS waiting for an answer. Every question becomes an outbound reply; the thread is the loop; session resume (bs-tiz.4) is the mechanism. Both worked examples run 3-4 rounds of refinement.

1. THE FLOWCHART IS ELLIPTICAL. It lists ONLY the music. Preshow / Welcome / video-to-sermon transition / closing prayer / ending slide are IMPLIED and must be assumed. Batch mode needs an explicit DEFAULT SERVICE SKELETON that the flowchart's music is slotted into. This is the single biggest inference the skill has to make and it is currently undocumented.

2. FLOWCHART VOCABULARY (from the two examples):
   - 'Prelude: <title> (<performer>)' -> prelude segment w/ performer
   - 'Hymns' header -> the bare titles under it are congregational (type=song)
   - 'Choir: <title>' -> special_music
   - 'Quartet' (bare) -> special_music; performer is USUALLY 'The Lovette Quartet' but NOT a given
   - 'Tehillah: <title>' + bare titles under it -> CONGREGATIONAL praise (type=song). Tehillah is the praise TEAM, not a performer. (This closed bs-fdn.)
   - 'Invitation: <title>' -> type=song, role=invitation
   - 'Video' -> video segment (black slide)
   - '<title> Nx' -> N is the NUMBER OF VERSES to sing (user-confirmed): 'America the beautiful 2x' -> sections Verse 1, Verse 2.

3. TWO TIERS OF GAP — they get DIFFERENT treatment (user-confirmed 'hold and ask first'):
   - BLOCKING (a slide cannot be sensibly made — e.g. 'Quartet' with no song title): DO NOT GENERATE. Reply asking. Generate once the answer arrives. May SUGGEST the likely answer ('The Lovette Quartet') but must not assume it.
   - NON-BLOCKING (missing lyrics for a song we cannot look up): DO generate — title_only slide — and ask for the lyrics in the same reply. One unresolved song must never cost the operator his whole deck.
   If both are present, blocking wins: hold.

4. LYRIC RESOLUTION in batch mode (this IS bs-8yd): library -> public-domain hymn lookup (store to songs/) -> otherwise title_only + ask. NEVER draft from memory. gen_service.md rule 3 (draft best-known lyrics, verified:false) must be REMOVED for batch mode. Newly looked-up lyrics are stored verified:false so they render amber and land in report.unverified[] — which IS the 'we looked these up, check them carefully' list the minister wants.

5. THE DECK IS A LIVING ARTIFACT. passages/<date>/service.deck.json is durable state. Replies amend it — observed asks: supply missing lyrics; REORDER a segment ('Star-Spangled Banner should come before the Welcome'); add a verse that was missed; add lyric slides to a choir/quartet special (use special_music's inline 'lyrics' field — do NOT pollute songs/ with performed numbers; user has no preference, inline is cleaner). Re-read the deck JSON and amend it; do NOT rebuild from the original email.

6. SERVICE DATE: the flowchart may not state it. Derive from the email (subject/body), else the next Sunday after the email date, and STATE the assumption in the reply — it drives both the output path and the season.
close_reason:
Done. gen_service.md now has an explicit Batch mode section; tests/eval/test_batch_mode.py (8 evals, all passing) exercises it against the two real flowcharts.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THIS LATER: the original acceptance criterion 'zero blocking questions' was a misleading way to put it, and the implementation deliberately does NOT satisfy it literally. The agent asks questions constantly — it asks them by EMAIL. The invariant is that the PROCESS never blocks. Two tiers: a gap that makes a slide impossible (special music with no song title) HOLDS the deck and asks first; a gap that merely thins it (missing lyrics) ships a title_only slide and asks alongside. Both are proven by eval.

Also landed here: the implied service skeleton (the flowchart lists only music), the flowchart vocabulary incl. the Tehillah rule (bs-fdn), 'Nx' = N verses, and a new sermon_transition segment type — the black slide every deck needs and the reference deck was missing.

title: Email Agent: hostable slide-deck agent driven by order-of-service email
description: A small, cheaply-hostable agent that lets the minister of music email an order of service ('flowchart') and get back a link to the generated slide deck. Runs on a cheaper model (e.g. Sonnet) to control API cost. This epic collects the work to make gen_service robust enough to run unattended on a small model, plus the agent/hosting/email plumbing itself (to be fleshed out next session).
design:
HARNESS DECIDED: Claude Agent SDK (Python 'claude-agent-sdk') — Claude Code as a library, distinct from the API Tool Runner and from Managed Agents. Runs the agent loop in our own process, works on files on our infrastructure, session state as JSONL on our filesystem — matches the co-located-with-Express design (see bs-tiz.6). Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview.

CONFIRMED FROM DOCS (bs-tiz.7 to confirm hands-on): (1) Session resume is native — capture session_id from the init SystemMessage, resume via ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id); fork_session=True branches. (2) Headless auth via 'claude setup-token' -> CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (~1yr). (3) Skills/commands auto-load from .claude/ and ~/.claude/ (setting_sources) — gen_service loads natively (see bs-tiz.9 to move it to SKILL.md). Reference: official email-assistant example, github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-demos.

AUTH/ToS DECISION: run the POC on the Claude Pro subscription via OAuth token. Rationale: this is a personal-assistant agent doing a task emailed TO the operator (the volunteer PowerPoint maker), not a product offered to end users — a defensible personal use of subscription credit. WATCH: Anthropic's Agent SDK terms restrict using claude.ai login to power products for others; revisit and move to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (pay-per-token) if this is ever rolled out to serve others directly.
notes:
STATE AS OF 2026-07-12 (read this before starting anything).

THE EMAIL PLUMBING IS BUILT AND PROVEN LIVE END-TO-END. A real 'AI:' email was read from Gmail, handled by Sonnet, and answered with a correct in-thread reply; idempotent on re-run; the agent correctly DECLINES to reply when nothing is warranted. 45 tests pass (cd agent && uv run pytest). Do not rebuild any of this.

Built: agent/ (uv Python project) — gate.py, store.py, dispatcher.py, heartbeat.py, tools.py, harness.py, healthcheck.py, authorize.py. Plus scripts/build-deck.js + schemas/deck.schema.json (deterministic deck rendering).

bs-tiz.2 and bs-tiz.4 are COMPLETE but held open by their dependency on bs-ixn. Don't redo them.

WHAT'S LEFT is the SKILL side, not the plumbing: bs-ixn (non-interactive batch mode — THE critical path) -> bs-tiz.5 (reply/report composition) -> bs-tiz.6 (deployment host). bs-8yd runs parallel.

HARD-WON FACTS (all verified, don't re-derive):
1. total_cost_usd is NOT a billing signal — Claude Code reports a cost estimate regardless of which account pays. RateLimitEvent.rate_limit_type=='five_hour' is the real proof of SUBSCRIPTION billing. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY silently outranks CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; config.assert_subscription_auth() hard-fails on it.
2. setting_sources=['project'] is REQUIRED for the SDK to see .claude/ skills, and fails SILENTLY if omitted.
3. Session resume works across separate OS processes and keeps the SAME session_id.
4. AskUserQuestion must never be exposed — no interactive user, so it hangs the run.
5. THE REPLY LOOP: the agent's own reply keeps the thread subject ('Re: AI: ...') and so matches the gate regex. Neither sender nor SENT label can distinguish it (the operator tests by emailing himself — every message carries both SENT and INBOX). Fixed on TWO levels: a deterministic authorship record (store.mark_agent_sent) AND, more importantly, agent judgment — get_thread gives the whole conversation, skip_reply makes 'no reply needed' a first-class outcome. Verified with state.db DELETED: the agent still declined, reasoning from the text alone. Do not make the agent's correctness depend on the store again.
See specs/email-agent.md and agent/spike/FINDINGS.md.

title: beads: configure sync so multiple machines stop diverging
description:
Recurring pain: sessions on different machines each keep their own Dolt DB, and the only thing carrying issues between them is .beads/issues.jsonl as an ordinary tracked file.

WHAT HAPPENED 2026-08-02 (the concrete instance): the local DB held 44 issues while the tracked JSONL held 58 — bs-255, bs-2pn, bs-752, bs-7sb, bs-8qs, bs-c2e, bs-d0f, bs-e4m, bs-fxj, bs-kyp, bs-om5, bs-tr6, bs-vhp, bs-zzq existed only in the file. Any mutation would have exported the 44-issue DB over the JSONL and silently dropped the other 14. Recovered with: bd init --force --prefix bs --from-jsonl --destroy-token DESTROY-bs (JSONL was verified a strict superset first, in both directions, and .beads/ was tarballed).

WHY AUTO-IMPORT DID NOT SAVE US: no-auto-import defaults to false, i.e. import-when-JSONL-is-newer is enabled — but it did not fire. Touching issues.jsonl and restarting the Dolt server both failed to trigger it, so it is not keyed off file mtime. Worth understanding before trusting it.

THE ACTUAL FIX — neither sync mechanism is configured:
  - sync.git-remote is unset, and there are NO refs/dolt/* on the GitHub remote, so the mechanism CLAUDE.md documents has never been active.
  - sync.branch is unset.
  - bd dolt remote list is empty.

PREFERRED: set sync.git-remote so Dolt data rides in refs/dolt/data on the existing GitHub remote — no new hosting, travels with the repo, and bd bootstrap can then clone it on a fresh machine. Alternative is a native Dolt remote (bd dolt remote add + bd dolt push), which means DoltHub or an S3/GCS bucket.

Do this against a known-good DB and verify the round trip from a second machine before relying on it.

ALSO STILL LIVE, unrelated to sync: running almost any bd command can delete the repo-root config.json (the scroller's {passagesDir, port}) and drop a stray root metadata.json containing {"database": ""}. Seen again this session from a read-only-looking bd doctor/bd status, with bd fully initialized. bd doctor surfaces it under 'Git Working Tree'. Check git status after running bd.
