title: Investigate Pi (pi.dev) as a multi-provider replacement for the Claude Agent SDK harness
description:
INVESTIGATION, not a commitment. Tabled 2026-07-30 to be picked up after bs-e4m
reports; filed so the option is not lost.

THE QUESTION: should the email agent's orchestration move off the Claude Agent SDK
onto Pi (https://pi.dev, MIT, github.com/badlogic/pi-mono), which supports many
providers natively, instead of keeping the SDK and reaching other models through
UniClaudeProxy?

WHAT PI IS (from pi.dev, 2026-07-30 — verify before relying on any of it):
  - "A minimal agent harness", MIT licensed, TypeScript/Node (Bun for standalone
    binaries). Monorepo packages: pi-ai (unified LLM API), pi-agent-core (runtime),
    pi-coding-agent (CLI).
  - Providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure, Bedrock, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras,
    xAI, Hugging Face, Kimi, MiniMax, NVIDIA, OpenRouter, Ollama, and more.
  - Four modes: interactive, print/JSON, RPC, and SDK.
  - Has a SKILLS concept ("capability packages with instructions and tools, loaded
    on-demand") plus extensions, prompt templates, themes. Mid-session model
    switching via /model.

WHY IT IS ATTRACTIVE: multi-provider routing becomes a first-class config concern
instead of the options.env + ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + model-alias-mapping hack bs-dox
is built on, and we stop depending on a translation shim whose fidelity we have
already been bitten by (bs-qku: non-streaming tool_use.input silently dropped to {}).
Its print/JSON and RPC modes are the same subprocess seam the Agent SDK already
uses, so the Python dispatcher/gate/store could plausibly stay and only the
harness subprocess would change — a smaller blast radius than a rewrite.

*** THE DECISIVE POINT, DO NOT LOSE IT: A FRAMEWORK SWAP DOES NOT FIX THE FILTER. ***
The content filter is Anthropic-side policy on Anthropic API traffic. Define the
agent in Pi and still call Claude and you still get the 400. What clears the filter
is calling a DIFFERENT PROVIDER, which is equally reachable from where we already
are. So Pi buys CLEANLINESS of the multi-provider path, not access to it, and is
only worth its cost if multi-provider turns out to be the permanent architecture.
bs-e4m is what tells us that. Do not start this before bs-e4m reports.

WHAT WE WOULD BE GIVING UP — all load-bearing, all verified in harness.py:
  1. setting_sources=["project"] (harness.py:147) is the delivery mechanism for the
     repo's .claude/ skills, i.e. for gen_service, which is the core IP of the
     slide builder. Pi has its own skills format; the port is not free and
     gen_service's non-interactive BATCH mode would need re-proving.
  2. The built-in tool suite (harness.py:151): Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash,
     WebSearch, WebFetch. Bash is how build-deck.js gets run. Edit's exact-match
     semantics are relied on. Confirm Pi's equivalents exist and behave.
  3. Session resume (harness.py:154). threads.session_id is a pointer into the
     CLI's own session store. If Pi does not persist resumable sessions
     equivalently we inherit full transcript persistence in state.db, which makes
     bs-1x4 much larger than a side table.
  4. *** SUBSCRIPTION BILLING — weigh this heaviest. *** config.py:93 chose Sonnet
     because it "keeps API cost down — the point of the epic", and
     assert_subscription_auth() (config.py:136) exists solely to stop
     ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from silently switching us to per-token billing. Pi talks to
     provider APIs, which normally means per-token. UNVERIFIED and worth checking
     first: does Pi support Anthropic subscription OAuth (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN)
     as an auth source? If not, migrating trades the epic's economics away
     permanently to fix a defect that bites on some Sundays.
  5. MCP servers. The Gmail and deck tools are IN-PROCESS SDK MCP servers passed via
     mcp_servers= (harness.py:143) and built with create_sdk_mcp_server. pi.dev's
     landing page did not mention MCP; confirm support, because without it those
     tools need reimplementing in TypeScript or exposing over a transport.
  6. Language boundary. agent/ is Python (dispatcher, gate, store, tools, publish).
     Pi is TypeScript. Even via RPC that is a second runtime to install, version,
     and keep alive on the bs-tiz.6 deployment box.

ALSO WEIGH: the current system works every week EXCEPT on copyrighted-lyric
services. Replacing the orchestration layer is a large blast radius for a narrow
defect, on a system with a hard Sunday deadline and a non-technical minister
waiting on the other end.

THE ALTERNATIVE THIS SHOULD BE COMPARED AGAINST — not bs-dox's Approach A:
Narrow the model swap to a TOOL instead of the transport or the framework. Per
bs-a1f's forensics the run blocked on the first assistant turn after get_thread
having written nothing, so the problem is that the ORCHESTRATOR SEES THE LYRICS AT
ALL. Have get_thread redact lyric-shaped blocks and stash them, and give a narrow
tool the job of moving stashed text into songs/*.md by reference. The orchestrator
never has lyrics in context; skills, built-in tools, subscription billing and
session resume all stay exactly as they are; the multi-provider concern collapses
into one small testable component. That also reframes the homelab 27B from a poor
orchestrator (bs-fxj's risk) into a plausible EXTRACTOR — one bounded task, no
multi-turn tool use, no session resume, indifferent to proxy translation fidelity.
File that as its own issue if bs-e4m makes it the front-runner.

DELIVERABLE FOR THIS ISSUE: a written recommendation with the six items above
answered yes/no, not a migration.
acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation answering, with evidence: (1) can Pi skills carry gen_service including batch mode; (2) does it have Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash equivalents; (3) does it persist resumable sessions; (4) does it support Anthropic subscription OAuth or is it per-token only; (5) does it support MCP servers for the existing Gmail/deck tools; (6) what the Python/TypeScript boundary costs on the deployment box. Plus a go/no-go compared against the redact-and-extract alternative. NOT a migration.

title: healthcheck: probe the fallback endpoint and model alias, not just AWS
description:
Once bs-dox lands, the agent's ability to answer the minister at all on a
copyrighted-song week depends on a box that nothing monitors.

The rescue path runs through UniClaudeProxy (currently http://192.168.0.48:9223)
and, if the local model is the chosen target, a 27B served behind it. If either is
down when the filter trips on a Saturday night, every attempt burns its three
tries and the minister gets the bs-9ed apology — with no signal anywhere that the
cause was a dead homelab box rather than a real agent failure.

healthcheck.py today checks only AWS (check_aws at :55, credentials plus the deck
bucket). Add a fallback-endpoint check alongside it so a dead proxy is discovered
on a weekday, not at 11pm Saturday.

WHAT TO CHECK (all verified working in bs-dox's probe, so all are fair assertions):
  - GET / returns 200 with provider "UniClaudeProxy".
  - GET /health returns 200.
  - The configured fallback MODEL ALIAS actually resolves. This is the one that
    matters most and the one a naive ping misses: the proxy rejects unmapped models
    with "Model 'X' not found in config models mapping", and the mapping has already
    changed once under us (claude-sonnet-5 was unmapped, then Thomas mapped it).
    A reachable proxy with a stale alias is still a dead fallback. Cheapest real
    assertion is a tiny POST /v1/messages with max_tokens small and a trivial
    prompt — but note the model is verbose, and max_tokens=64 came back EMPTY with
    stop_reason=max_tokens, so give it room or you will alarm on nothing.

SKIP IF NOT CONFIGURED: when the fallback URL is unset the feature is off, and this
check must report "not configured" rather than fail. Otherwise every dev machine
without homelab access shows red.

Depends on bs-dox only for the config keys (the endpoint and alias must be
config-driven, not hardcoded — bs-dox notes are explicit that the address is
volatile and that a tailnet name may replace the 192.168.0.x lease).
acceptance_criteria: healthcheck reports the fallback proxy reachable AND the configured model alias resolving, fails loudly when the proxy is up but the alias is unmapped, and reports "not configured" (not failure) when the fallback URL is unset.

title: harness: is_error path discards the content-filter reason, breaking bs-dox's fallback trigger
description:
The content-filter reason is DISCARDED on one of the two paths a failed run can
take. bs-dox plans to trigger the fallback by matching on that reason, so on that
path the fallback would silently never fire.

THE DEFECT (harness.py):

  :197  if result is not None and getattr(result, "is_error", False):
  :198      raise AgentError(f"agent run errored: {result.result!r}")
  :199  except BaseException as exc:
  :216      if (isinstance(exc, Exception)
  :217          and not isinstance(exc, AgentError)      <-- False here
  :218          and last_text and last_text.startswith("API Error")):
  :222          raise AgentError(f"agent run aborted by an API error: {last_text}")
  :225      raise

The raise at :198 is INSIDE the try, so it lands in the except at :199. The
enrichment guard at :217 requires the exception NOT to be an AgentError — but we
just made it one. So it falls through to the bare re-raise at :225 and propagates
the original message. Per bs-zwj, result.result on this path degrades to the
literal, useless word "success".

Meanwhile last_text (captured at :179-192) is sitting right there holding
"API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy". It is populated on
BOTH paths, because it comes from the assistant's TextBlocks, not from the
exception.

WHY IT MATTERS TWICE OVER:
  1. bs-dox's trigger. Its notes assert "harness.py already re-raises AgentError
     carrying 'API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy'. Match on
     that." True only when the SDK itself raises. When the CLI reports failure via
     ResultMessage.is_error instead, the string never reaches the message and a
     substring match fails to fire. Both paths happen in practice — the exception
     path is what bs-a1f observed on 7/26, and the is_error path is the entire
     reason bs-zwj exists.
  2. Journal legibility, independent of any fallback. This is the same class of
     opacity bs-zwj was filed to fix; it fixed the stderr half and left this half.

FIX: key the detection off last_text rather than off the exception's message.
Simplest shape is to make the :198 raise carry last_text when it has one, e.g.
raise AgentError with both the result subtype AND last_text, so a single downstream
predicate works whichever path fired. Keep the existing :216-224 branch for the
case where the SDK raises before any ResultMessage arrives.

Do NOT paper over this by matching on more strings downstream. The reason is
already captured; the bug is that one path throws it away.
acceptance_criteria: A run that fails via ResultMessage.is_error surfaces the model's last API Error text in the AgentError message, not the bare result subtype. A single downstream predicate detects a content-filter block regardless of which of the two failure paths fired. Covered by a test in tests/test_harness_terminal.py exercising BOTH paths.
notes:
================================================================
2026-07-30 — CONFIRMED IN THE WILD. Not a theoretical path.
================================================================

Observed unprompted while running the bs-e4m proxy arm (scratchpad/probe_filter.py).
The run failed upstream at the proxy, and the SDK exception the harness would have
received was literally:

    Exception: Claude Code returned an error result: success

while the assistant's last text block was holding the entire real reason:

    API Error: 502 Provider error: Client error '400 Bad Request' for url
    'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'

That is precisely the defect described above: the failure arrived via
ResultMessage.is_error, harness.py:198 wrapped it in an AgentError whose message is
the useless result subtype, and the enrichment branch at :217 declined to touch it
because it was already an AgentError. The reason was available in last_text and was
thrown away.

Two things this settles:
  1. The is_error path is not hypothetical — it is what a PROXY/UPSTREAM failure
     takes, which is exactly the class of failure the fallback introduces. So the
     fallback would be running in the regime where its own trigger is blindest.
  2. The "success" degradation bs-zwj documented is still live and still actively
     misleading. In this instance the journal would have said a run failed with
     "success" while an OpenAI 400 was the truth.

Worth noting for the fix: in this run the probe recovered the reason ONLY because it
independently accumulated assistant TextBlocks and printed last_text itself. Nothing
in harness.py surfaces it on this path. Any predicate written against the exception
message alone — which is what bs-dox's plan proposed — would have seen the word
"success" and concluded nothing was wrong with the provider.

title: Keep the server song library and the repo songs/ in sync
description: Songs the minister emails land in the library ON THE SERVER (that is where the agent runs), so the repo songs/ and the server songs/ can drift. Decide the source of truth and a sync path (e.g. commit server-added songs back to the repo, or have the server pull songs/ from git) so evals and production render from the same lyrics. Raised 2026-07-24 while shipping the 75px + background-cover fixes.

Raise .lyric-slide .lyric to 75px (from 60px) and shift FONT_LADDER up so the width-fit fallback stays proportional. title: Third batch-mode eval fixture: an all-in-library flowchart that exercises rendering
description:
The two batch-mode eval fixtures now both test the ASKING path, and nothing exercises a clean end-to-end build.

7/12 pins non-blocking (build anyway, ask alongside). 7/5 pins blocking (hold the deck, ask first). Before bs-1mf, 7/12 also happened to cover rendering: the agent looked up two public-domain hymns, saved them with real lyrics, and those produced actual lyric slides -- so the run incidentally exercised line measurement, the font ladder, caesura breaks and stanza splitting. Under bs-1mf both resolve to title_only and render nothing. Only the two songs seed_library keeps still produce lyric slides.

So no test was deleted, but the eval suite lost most of its coverage of the typography path as a side effect of the lyrics policy.

This is NOT an unprotected regression: tests/build-deck.test.js pins the reference deck's HTML and report byte-for-byte, which is the stronger check for rendering. The gap is specifically that an EVAL -- the thing that tells us the model plus the renderer work together -- no longer says anything about slides.

Proposed: a third fixture whose songs are ALL in the library, so the agent's only job is deck assembly and the run goes end to end through rendering. Give seed_library a keep set covering every song in the flowchart. holy-holy-holy is the useful one to include: it carries a caesura, so it exercises the preferred break-at-the-caesura branch rather than the shrink branch.

Assertions worth making: no segment is title_only; report.missing has no lyrics entries; lyric slides were actually generated (report.slides well above the segment count); report.typography is populated; and the agent's own deck rebuilds via the rebuild() helper.

Cost note: each eval fixture is a real agent run, currently ~9 minutes and real tokens for the pair. A third adds to that, so it may be worth marking it separately if the suite gets slow enough to discourage running.
acceptance_criteria: A third batch-mode eval fixture exists whose flowchart resolves entirely from the library. It asserts no title_only segments, no missing-lyrics entries, that lyric slides were generated, that report.typography is populated, and that the agent's deck rebuilds. Running the eval suite exercises the renderer with real lyrics again, not only the asking path.

title: Seed songs/ by OCRing the existing JPEG service exports
description:
passages/2026-06-07, 2026-06-14, 2026-06-21 and 2026-07-12 hold full JPEG exports of real services. The lyrics on those slides are already proofread, already the arrangement this congregation sings, and already the church's own verse selections and repeat structure -- which is more than hymnary can give us. They are just trapped in images.

Run them through OCR (tesseract, or macOS Vision via a Shortcut) and split the output into songs/*.md. Deterministic, no model in the loop, so it carries none of the bs-1mf exposure.

Highest value per unit of effort of the three library-seeding options: it recovers the actual repertoire rather than a generic hymnal, and proofreading OCR against a slide we already trust is far lighter than typing from scratch.

Set verified:false until a human confirms -- OCR misreads, especially on the script/display faces used for song titles.

Caesuras will not survive this and should not be added up front. build-deck.js reports `shrunk` and names the offending line the first time a song is actually used, so they get added reactively.

title: Deterministic hymnary.org importer (no model in the loop)
description:
bs-1mf removed the model's ability to write out a public-domain hymn, which was the one automated path for hymns not yet in songs/. Restore it deterministically instead: a Node script that fetches a hymnary.org page over plain HTTP, parses the text, and writes songs/<slug>.md with frontmatter (source URL, hymnal, number, author, public_domain) and the sections.

The distinction that makes this safe: gen_service.md warns that WebFetch refuses to return lyric text, but that is WebFetch's model-backed summarizer. A curl-plus-parser has no model in the loop, so there is no output for a copyright classifier to act on -- the same reason build-deck.js can read lyrics out of songs/*.md all day.

It is also better engineering than the model doing it: reproducible, cacheable, cites its source, identical output every run.

Two caveats. Hymnary indexes plenty of non-public-domain texts, so the importer must read their PD field rather than infer it from age. And it should cache and rate-limit to be a decent citizen.

Write imported songs verified:false -- a script is not a human either.

title: songs/: replace the four memory-drafted lyric files with checked text
description:
Four songs in songs/ predate bs-1mf and contain lyrics the model wrote from memory: waymaker.md and worthy-of-worship.md say so explicitly in a VERIFY comment; his-name-is-jesus.md and o-what-a-savior.md are also verified:false. Under the new rule these are exactly the text we no longer allow -- they just happen to already be on disk, where the policy does not reach them.

Not urgent and not silent: all four are verified:false, so build-deck.js flags every slide amber and lists them under `unverified`. The risk is that this is a preview-only signal, and the library is about to start growing from minister-supplied replies, at which point these four become the only entries nobody ever checked.

Fix: ask the minister for the real text (or pull from the church's CCLI copy) and overwrite, setting verified:true. Cheapest to fold into the next service that actually uses one of them rather than doing all four up front.
notes:
SHARPER THAN FILED (2026-07-18): his-name-is-jesus.md was not merely unchecked, it was a build-stopper. It carried a single section whose only content was a placeholder string. build-deck.js correctly refuses placeholder text (bs-c16) -- but refusing is a hard DeckError, and omitting `sections` defaults to every section in file order, so ANY non-title_only reference to that song killed the whole build. "His name is Jesus" is in the real repertoire (it appears in the 7/5 flowchart in examples/flowcharts.md), so the next deck naming it would have stopped dead.

FIXED in this session: the placeholder section is gone, leaving frontmatter only. The song now takes the graceful path -- title slide plus a `missing` line asking for lyrics -- which is the same shape every unknown song takes under bs-1mf, so it stops being a special case. The HTML comment now explains WHY it has no sections, so nobody helpfully re-adds a placeholder.

Report output is unchanged: build-deck.js phrases the gap as "no projectable sections (empty or placeholder text)", which covers both shapes identically. That is why the golden test still passes byte-for-byte.

STILL OPEN, and the point of this issue: the four files still need real text. waymaker.md and worthy-of-worship.md have 4 sections each of memory-drafted lyrics and DO render (amber). o-what-a-savior.md has 0 sections and is the choir special, which is title-only by design -- it likely needs nothing. his-name-is-jesus.md now needs both an identity confirmation and the text.

Per the verified semantics added to gen_service.md this session: when he sends the text, overwrite the sections AND set verified: true in the same edit. verified:false is now reserved for machine-sourced text only.

title: Convert slide backgrounds to JPEG — the half of bs-9x5 that actually hits the weight target
description:
Follow-up to bs-9x5, which landed the downscale half (188MB -> 108MB on disk; the examples/2026-06-28 deck 71.0MB -> 41.9MB first load). That is only a 1.7x win and MISSES bs-9x5's own acceptance criterion of 'a few MB'. Deferred by thomas 2026-07-17 to think about the format trade-off; nothing blocks on it (bs-tiz.6 does not depend on this).

WHY DOWNSCALE ALONE CANNOT GET THERE. PNG is lossless and these backgrounds are photographs, so FORMAT DOMINATES WIDTH. Measured on the deck's real 12 backgrounds (downscale-only, no upscaling of already-small files; the 2912/PNG row reproduces the 41.9MB actually on disk, which validates the method):

  2912 PNG      41.9 MB   <- what shipped
  1456 PNG      18.4 MB
  2912 JPEG q90  8.2 MB
  1456 JPEG q90  3.9 MB
  1456 JPEG q85  3.7 MB

No PNG width reaches 'a few MB'. Only a JPEG conversion does.

DECISION STILL OPEN — 1456 (3.9MB) vs 2912 (8.2MB). The input that should settle it: EXPORT QUALITY IS IDENTICAL EITHER WAY. templates/service-slides-template.html exports via html2canvas at scale:1 into the 1456x816 slide box and encodes JPEG q0.95, so the ProPresenter slide is a 1456-wide JPEG regardless of source width. Width only affects how the PREVIEW looks: 1456 is soft only when viewed full-screen on a large HiDPI monitor, and the minister previews on a PHONE, where 1456 is already heavily oversampled. That argues for 1456 unless the operator's desktop preview matters more than the parking-lot download.

WHAT THE WORK IS (this is why it was split, per bs-9x5's own notes): NOT purely an asset change. build-deck.js resolves backgrounds by NAME — SCRIM_BACKGROUNDS is a Set of .png filenames, and validation checks fs.existsSync against templates/service/. So it touches renderer constants + the golden tests (tests/build-deck.test.js, 17 tests). Do NOT keep a .png extension on a JPEG body: browsers sniff it and it renders, but it is a lie on the wire that will confuse someone later.

GROUNDWORK ALREADY DONE by bs-9x5, reuse it: masters preserved at templates/service-masters/ (git mv, so zero new repo weight); scripts/optimize-templates.sh + npm run optimize-templates, idempotent, sips-based (ImageMagick is NOT installed on this box), copies rather than upscales files already under the cap; TEMPLATE_MAX_WIDTH is a one-line knob. sips CANNOT write WebP — that would need a new dependency, so WebP is a bigger decision than it looks.
acceptance_criteria: A published deck's first-load weight is a few MB, not 41.9MB. Exported JPEGs remain visually indistinguishable from today's at 1456x816. Masters under templates/service-masters/ remain untouched. build-deck.js and its 17 goldens pass with the new filenames.
notes: Measured 2026-07-17 during the bs-tiz.6 pre-deployment review. The 2912+PNG combination that shipped was MY (the assistant's) bad call: bs-9x5's '17MB -> 2.5MB, 7x, zero renderer changes' figure was measured at 1456, and I pinned it to 2912 — combining the two size-INCREASING choices. Each rationale was defensible alone; together they land at 41.9MB. The subagent implemented as directed, measured, and correctly pushed back rather than silently shipping a miss. Recording it so the next session does not repeat the reasoning error.

title: healthcheck: assert AWS identity is cbc-wilm-agent + probe Put/Get
description:
healthcheck.py covers Claude + Gmail but NOT AWS. AWS creds joined the silently-failing-on-a-delay class when bs-tiz.10 landed, which is exactly the class healthcheck exists for: a publish failure surfaces at the worst possible moment (Saturday night, mid-run, after the deck is built).

Now urgent because the key EXISTS as of 2026-07-17 (bs-crp closed). The foot-gun is the AWS SDK credential chain: environment variables beat ~/.aws/credentials, so a stray AWS_PROFILE or AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID in the host/service environment silently publishes to the WRONG ACCOUNT — or fails at publish time with the deck already built. Same family as the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY foot-gun that config.assert_subscription_auth() already guards.

Add to healthcheck.py:
1. sts:GetCallerIdentity and ASSERT the Arn ends in ':user/cbc-wilm-agent'. Any other identity (root, a personal profile) is a FAIL, not a pass — publishing as root works, which is precisely why it hides the misconfiguration.
2. A scoped Put + Get probe against config.deck_bucket to prove the key actually carries the publisher policy. Use a fixed throwaway key (e.g. _policy-probe/healthcheck.txt). NOTE: the agent CANNOT DeleteObject by design (verified on bs-crp), so the probe object cannot clean itself up — either overwrite the same fixed key every run (overwrite is allowed and proven) or accept one lingering object. Do NOT add DeleteObject to the policy to make cleanup tidy; the no-Delete scoping is deliberate.

Do NOT probe Delete expecting failure — that is bs-crp's job and it is already verified; a healthcheck should test what must WORK.
acceptance_criteria: healthcheck reports OK/FAIL for AWS. Running it with AWS_PROFILE pointed at a different identity (or root) FAILS with a message naming the expected vs actual Arn. Running it with the agent's key passes, proving Put and Get. Exit code is non-zero on any AWS failure, consistent with the existing Claude/Gmail checks.
notes: Split out of bs-tiz.6's gap analysis 2026-07-17 when bs-crp closed. Rationale for living in healthcheck rather than the systemd unit (bs-crp's notes suggested the unit): healthcheck is the thing already built for credentials that fail silently and on a delay, it already runs on the host where the key lives, and it is runnable on demand on a Tuesday. A unit-level assertion only fires at start, which misses a key revoked while the service is up.
close_reason: healthcheck now asserts sts:GetCallerIdentity ends in :user/cbc-wilm-agent and probes Put+Get against the real bucket at a fixed overwritten key (no Delete — the agent cannot, by design). Verified live BOTH ways: with AWS_PROFILE unset it correctly FAILS on arn:...:root (the identity that would publish successfully and hide the misconfiguration); with AWS_PROFILE=cbc-wilm-agent it passes and proves Put+Get under the real IAM policy. 11 new tests, fully mocked.

title: Slide templates are ~28x larger than they need to be: 71MB first load on the minister's phone
description:
The service backgrounds are stored at ~4496x2475 as PNG despite being photographic. The slide box is 1456x816. A single real deck (examples/2026-06-28) references 12 unique templates totalling 71MB of first-load page weight — on a link whose entire purpose is a minister opening it on a phone, possibly on mobile data, in a church parking lot. templates/service/ is 188MB across 23 PNGs.

Found while building bs-tiz.10; deliberately scoped out of bs-tiz.11 (which syncs what is on disk today) so it did not grow into an image-pipeline task.
design:
THE OVERSAMPLING BUYS NOTHING — this is the fact that makes it safe. templates/service-slides-template.html:224-240 exports with html2canvas at scale:1 and encodes toBlob('image/jpeg', 0.95). So the browser ALREADY downsamples the 4496px source to the 1456x816 slide box and JPEG-encodes it. The ProPresenter slide is a 1456x816 JPEG regardless of what we upload; the extra resolution is discarded at export, not preserved.

MEASURED, not estimated: welcome-text-summer.png 17MB -> 613KB at 1456px wide, JPEG q90 (~28x). The 71MB deck becomes roughly 2-3MB. Corroboration from the repo's own assets: hymn-1.png is already 1300x720 and weighs 0.3MB — it is the model the others should follow. The outliers are the seasonal welcome cards (4 seasons x 3 styles) plus choir.png (14MB) and scripture-emphasis.png (11MB).

CAVEAT ON 1456: that width is sized for EXPORT, which is what feeds ProPresenter. A preview viewed full-screen on a large monitor CSS-scales the slide up, and a 1456px source would look slightly soft there. 2x (2912x1632) is immune to that and still ~4x smaller than today. Pick deliberately.

KEEP THE MASTERS. Do not re-encode templates/service/*.png in place — archive or keep the high-res originals and generate derived copies. Re-encoding source assets is destructive and the originals are what an operator edits.

FORMAT COUPLING: build-deck.js resolves backgrounds by NAME (e.g. hymn-1.png, SCRIM_BACKGROUNDS is a Set of .png filenames). Switching to .jpg/.webp is therefore NOT purely an asset change — it touches the renderer's filename constants and the golden tests. Keeping the .png extension on a JPEG-encoded body would render (browsers sniff) but is a lie on the wire and will confuse someone later. Decide: rename properly and update build-deck.js, or downscale-only as PNG (2.5MB for the 17MB file measured above — a 7x win with zero renderer changes, and a strictly cheaper first step).
acceptance_criteria: A published deck's first-load weight is a few MB, not 71MB. Exported JPEGs are visually indistinguishable from today's at 1456x816 (the export path re-encodes anyway). High-res masters are preserved somewhere, not destroyed. build-deck.js and its goldens still pass if filenames change.
notes:
DOWNSCALE HALF SHIPPED 2026-07-17; FORMAT HALF DEFERRED to bs-sft by thomas.

Delivered: masters moved to templates/service-masters/ via git mv (23 files; a rename reuses existing blobs, so preserving the originals cost ZERO new repo weight). templates/service/ is now derived, committed output — which is why build-deck.js (validates against that dir) and sync-templates.sh (SRC points there) needed no rewiring. New scripts/optimize-templates.sh + npm run optimize-templates: idempotent via mtime, --dry-run/--force, sips-based (ImageMagick is NOT installed), and files at/under the cap are COPIED not resampled, so hymn-1.png (1300x720) is never upscaled. Operator loop: edit master -> npm run optimize-templates -> npm test -> npm run sync-templates. npm test 17/17; build-deck.js untouched.

RESULT IS ONLY 1.7x AND DOES NOT MEET THIS ISSUE'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: templates/service/ 188.3MB -> 108.5MB; the examples/2026-06-28 deck 71.0MB -> 41.9MB first load. 'A few MB' is unmet, so this issue stays OPEN pending bs-sft.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS, recorded so it is not repeated: the assistant instructed 2912px + PNG, combining the two size-INCREASING choices. This issue's own '7x win with zero renderer changes' figure was measured at 1456, not 2912. PNG is lossless and these are photographs, so format dominates width. Measured on the deck's real 12 backgrounds, downscale-only (the 2912/PNG row reproduces the 41.9MB on disk, validating the method):
  2912 PNG 41.9MB | 1456 PNG 18.4MB | 2912 JPEG q90 8.2MB | 1456 JPEG q90 3.9MB
The subagent implemented as directed, measured, and pushed back rather than silently shipping a miss — the right call.

The 1.7x is banked and harmless; bs-sft carries the format conversion and the build-deck.js/golden work it requires.

title: Deck bucket has no CORS config; html2canvas export can taint the canvas cross-origin
description: bs-tiz.10 acceptance criteria explicitly requires the bucket (or CDN front) to return Access-Control-Allow-Origin on template-image responses, because cross-origin template images taint the html2canvas canvas and make canvas.toBlob() throw SecurityError — the Export button fails while the deck still LOOKS correct on screen. infra/ (bs-crp) ships no aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration, so that criterion is currently unmet.
design: NUANCE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ADDING IT: when the deck HTML is served from the bucket itself (decks/<date>/index.html) and templates live at templates/service/*.png in the SAME bucket, the images are SAME-ORIGIN and no CORS is needed — the tainting scenario does not arise on the happy path. It bites on the DEV/PREVIEW path: a locally rendered service-preview.html (file:// or localhost) built with --asset-base pointing at S3 pulls those images cross-origin and taints the canvas. So this is not a production blocker but it will bite whoever tests export locally, confusingly, because the slides render fine. Fix: aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration allowing GET, and crossorigin=anonymous on the img tags in build-deck.js templates (CORS headers alone do not untaint — the element must opt in). Both halves are required.
acceptance_criteria: JPEG export via the Export button is verified from the hosted S3 URL AND from a locally rendered preview pointed at the S3 asset base, without SecurityError.
notes: BUCKET HALF DONE (bs-crp / infra/s3.tf): aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration allows GET+HEAD from any origin. allowed_origins=* is deliberate — every object is already anonymously readable via the bucket policy, so a narrower list would imply a confidentiality this bucket does not have. VERIFIED ON THE WIRE 2026-07-16: ACAO * returned on a cross-origin GET of a template PNG. CODE HALF DONE (commit 32a9aeb): build-deck.js emits crossorigin="anonymous" on bg ONLY when the asset base is absolute/cross-origin (regex on scheme:// or //); same-origin default unaffected so goldens are byte-identical. Unit-tested (both modes). HOSTED EXPORT CONFIRMED 2026-07-16 (thomas, real browser): the deck at https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/decks/2026-06-28/index.html renders all backgrounds AND the Export button produces a JPEG with no SecurityError. Half the criterion. WHY THAT IS ONLY HALF, AND THE HALF THAT MATTERS LESS. DECK_BASE_URL is now the bucket's own REST origin, so a deck served FROM the bucket loads its templates SAME-ORIGIN. The crossorigin="anonymous" attribute is present (the asset base is absolute) but the browser never needs it — same-origin passes before any CORS check. So the hosted pass proves crossorigin does not BREAK the same-origin case; it does NOT exercise the tainting this issue exists for. The real test is the DEV/PREVIEW path: a locally rendered service-preview.html (file:// or localhost) built with --asset-base pointing at S3, which pulls those images genuinely cross-origin. REMAINING: export from that local preview. Built for the test at /tmp/local-preview-s3/service-preview.html (37 crossorigin attrs, absolute S3 srcs) via: node scripts/build-deck.js examples/2026-06-28.deck.json --out --asset-base https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/templates/service Open it and click Export. If it throws SecurityError about a tainted canvas, one of the two halves is not doing its job. This is the case that will bite whoever tests export locally, confusingly, because the slides render fine either way.
close_reason: ACCEPTANCE FULLY MET 2026-07-16 (thomas verified BOTH cases in a real browser). Commits: bucket CORS in bs-crp/infra/s3.tf, crossorigin emission in 32a9aeb. - JPEG export from the HOSTED S3 URL: no SecurityError. - JPEG export from a LOCALLY rendered preview pointed at the S3 asset base (/tmp/local-preview-s3/service-preview.html, built with --asset-base https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/templates/service): no SecurityError. THIS is the case the issue exists for — a file:// page pulling images genuinely cross-origin — and it passing is what actually proves both halves work together: S3 returns ACAO (verified on the wire: ACAO * on a cross-origin GET) AND the elements opt in with crossorigin="anonymous", so the canvas is never tainted. WHY BOTH CASES WERE NEEDED, worth keeping. The hosted pass alone proves almost nothing about tainting: DECK_BASE_URL is the bucket's own origin, so a deck served from the bucket loads its templates SAME-ORIGIN and the browser never consults CORS at all — same-origin passes first. The hosted test only shows crossorigin="anonymous" does not BREAK the same-origin path. The local-preview test is the one that exercises the actual mechanism. Anyone re-verifying this after a change must run the local case; a green hosted export is not evidence. BOTH HALVES REMAIN REQUIRED. CORS response headers alone do not untaint a canvas — without crossorigin="anonymous" the browser never sends Origin and S3's ACAO goes unused. And the attribute alone does nothing without the bucket returning ACAO. Removing either one reintroduces the bug, and it fails CONFUSINGLY: the slides still render correctly and only Export throws.

title: Deck URLs are HTTP-only: S3 website endpoint can't serve the https link bs-tiz.10 promises
description: infra/ (bs-crp) configures cbc-wilm-agent-public via aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration, whose endpoint is http://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com. S3 static website endpoints DO NOT SUPPORT HTTPS — that is a hard AWS limitation, not a config gap. But bs-tiz.10 notes specify DECK_BASE_URL as 'https://<bucket> or a CloudFront domain' and the whole point of the S3 pivot is the minister opening the link on his phone over the public internet. An emailed http:// link gets a 'Not secure' interstitial on mobile Safari/Chrome, which is a bad look for a link we tell a minister to trust.
design: THREE OPTIONS. (1) Use the REST endpoint instead: https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/decks/<date>/index.html. HTTPS works today, public via the existing bucket policy, no new infra. The website config's index_document suffix buys us NOTHING here because bs-tiz.10 already uploads an explicit .../index.html path — the suffix only matters for bare-directory URLs we never emit. Cheapest correct fix; drop the website configuration entirely. (2) CloudFront in front of the bucket: HTTPS + the custom-domain future bs-tiz.10 design already anticipates ('a future CloudFront+custom-domain front keep old links working'), plus it makes the permanent-URL goal real. More moving parts, ~free at this volume. (3) Keep http:// and accept the browser warning — rejected. RECOMMEND (1) now, (2) when a custom domain is wanted; the date-keyed path scheme survives both.
acceptance_criteria: The URL emailed to the minister is https:// and opens clean on a phone with no security interstitial.
notes: DECISION REVERSED 2026-07-16 (thomas), on new evidence. The earlier decision was "accept plain http:// for now; not a blocker". That was made believing the only cost of http was a cosmetic browser interstitial. IT IS NOT COSMETIC — http breaks the deck outright, silently: THE ACTUAL FAILURE (hit by thomas in a real browser, not theory). bs-tiz.10 bakes DECK_BASE_URL into every AT RENDER TIME. With the website endpoint as the origin, those srcs are http. Open the deck over https and the browser BLOCKS every one of them as insecure mixed content. The HTML loads, text and layout are perfect, and all 37 backgrounds vanish with no error anywhere in the UI. Opening the SAME object via the http website endpoint rendered fine — which is exactly what made this look like a non-issue and is why it survived a round of "verification". WHY https IS STRICTLY BETTER, not just nicer: mixed-content blocking only applies to INSECURE subresources on a SECURE page, never the reverse. So https images work from BOTH endpoints (https page: same-scheme, fine; http page: secure subresource on an insecure page is allowed). http images work from exactly one. The http origin makes the two endpoints non-interchangeable and the divergence silent. FIXED 2026-07-16 (commit 8311cdb): DECK_BASE_URL default + .env.example -> https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (REST endpoint). Deck re-published; 0 insecure refs, 37 https img refs, all 12 unique backgrounds 200 over https. Website configuration KEPT in infra/ — harmless, and nothing depends on its index-document suffix since decks are always explicit .../index.html paths. So option (1) was taken WITHOUT needing to drop the website config, contrary to the original design note. ROOT CAUSE WORTH REMEMBERING: infra/outputs.tf literally described the website endpoint as "use as the media asset base for build-deck.js". The wrong thing was the documented thing. Now emits deck_rest_endpoint as the one to use (outputs-only change; needs a terraform apply to refresh). PINNED: agent/tests/test_publish.py asserts the default origin is https and is never an s3-website host, and that the asset base and deck link always share one origin. STILL OPEN: the acceptance criterion says "opens clean on a phone with no security interstitial". The scheme is now https and the wire is verified, but nobody has opened it on a phone, and the visual render has not been confirmed in ANY browser — no browser tooling was available. Needs a human eyeball before this closes.
close_reason: FIXED + VERIFIED 2026-07-16 (commit 8311cdb; thomas confirmed the render in a browser). DECK_BASE_URL is now the https REST endpoint https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com. The emailed link is https:// and opens clean — no interstitial is possible on https by construction, and the deck renders correctly. This closed for a much better reason than the one it was filed with. The original decision was "accept http, it is only a cosmetic interstitial". That was WRONG: http did not merely look bad, it BROKE the deck. The origin is baked into every at render time, so an http origin served over https had all 37 backgrounds blocked as insecure mixed content — perfect text and layout, zero images, no error. Found by thomas opening the real URL after curl-based checks had pronounced it fine. https turned out strictly better rather than merely nicer: mixed-content blocking only applies to insecure subresources on a SECURE page, never the reverse, so https images render from BOTH the REST and website endpoints, while http images render from only one. Option (1) was taken and the website configuration was KEPT — contrary to the original design note, dropping it was unnecessary, since nothing depends on its index-document suffix (decks are always explicit .../index.html paths). ROOT CAUSE: infra/outputs.tf described the website endpoint as "use as the media asset base for build-deck.js". The wrong thing was the documented thing. Now emits deck_rest_endpoint as the one to use (outputs-only; needs a terraform apply to refresh). PINNED: agent/tests/test_publish.py asserts the default origin is https and never an s3-website host, and that the asset base and deck link share one origin. FUTURE: a CloudFront + custom domain front (the original option 2) remains available whenever wanted. The date-keyed path scheme survives it, so links already emailed keep working.

title: Terraform: S3 deck bucket + agent IAM (infra/)
description: Stand up the public deck bucket that bs-tiz.10/11 publish into, as Terraform in infra/ with the S3 backend in cbc-wilm-agent-private. Creates: (1) aws_s3_bucket cbc-wilm-agent-public configured as a static website; (2) aws_iam_policy cbc-wilm-agent-publisher scoped to that one bucket (ListBucket + GetObject + PutObject, no DeleteObject); (3) aws_iam_user cbc-wilm-agent with that policy attached directly. Outputs: bucket name, website endpoint, policy ARN, user name. APPLIED 2026-07-16 by thomas. Documented in README (Infrastructure section).
design: PUBLIC READ IS A BUCKET POLICY, NOT AN ACL. The original draft used aws_s3_bucket_acl acl=public-read, which grants READ on the BUCKET (list objects) and NOT s3:GetObject on the objects — the website endpoint would have 403'd on every fetch. Replaced with object_ownership=BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled entirely) + a bucket policy granting anonymous s3:GetObject on arn/*. CONSEQUENCE FOR bs-tiz.10/11: uploads must NOT pass --acl public-read; it now hard-fails with AccessControlListNotSupported. Objects are public via the policy alone. Public access block accordingly relaxes ONLY block_public_policy + restrict_public_buckets; the two ACL flags stay true since ACLs cannot grant anything under BucketOwnerEnforced. Anonymous principals get GetObject only, never ListBucket, so the bucket is not a browsable archive (satisfies the bs-tiz.10 no-listing constraint). NO ROLE IN THE MIDDLE: the agent runs on a self-hosted always-on box (specs/email-agent.md 4.6), so there is no EC2 instance profile to source rotating creds from, and a user-assumes-role hop would add a trust policy without shrinking blast radius (long-lived keys sufficient to assume the role == long-lived keys sufficient to write the bucket). IAM Roles Anywhere would eliminate the standing secret but needs a private CA (~400/mo) — not proportionate here. The policy scoping is the actual control: worst case on a leak is read/write of slide media.
acceptance_criteria: terraform validate passes; apply creates the bucket, policy, and user. Bucket serves an uploaded object publicly over the website endpoint with no --acl flag on upload. Anonymous ListBucket is denied. Agent user can Put and Get but not Delete.
notes: ACCESS KEYS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN TERRAFORM. aws_iam_access_key would persist the secret into the state file (in cbc-wilm-agent-private) forever. Key is created by hand in the IAM console and lives ONLY in the agent host's environment (systemd EnvironmentFile, 0600, root-owned — not a .env in the repo). A plan showing a user with no key is CORRECT, not half-finished: Terraform does not track keys and will not report drift on one. Same family as the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY foot-gun on bs-tiz.6 — the AWS SDK has its own credential chain where env vars beat ~/.aws/credentials, so a startup sts:GetCallerIdentity assertion (expect cbc-wilm-agent) is worth baking into the service unit. .gitignore now excludes .terraform/, *.tfstate*, *.tfvars; .terraform.lock.hcl stays TRACKED on purpose (pins provider hashes). AWS_PROFILE must be exported rather than set via provider profile= — the S3 backend resolves credentials independently of the provider block and would otherwise reach for the default profile. VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-16 (during bs-tiz.10/.11), 3 of 4 acceptance criteria: - Bucket serves an uploaded object publicly over the website endpoint with NO --acl on upload: CONFIRMED. bs-tiz.10 publishes and bs-tiz.11 syncs 23 PNGs, both without any ACL argument; anonymous GET returns 200. The BucketOwnerEnforced + bucket-policy design works as designed. - Anonymous ListBucket DENIED: CONFIRMED. GET /?list-type=2 returns 403 AccessDenied. This also satisfies bs-tiz.10's "not a browsable archive" constraint. - CORS: ACAO * returned on a cross-origin GET of a template. STILL UNVERIFIED — "Agent user can Put and Get but not Delete". `aws iam list-access-keys --user-name cbc-wilm-agent` returns ZERO keys: the key does not exist yet, so the scoped policy has never been exercised by anything. Everything above ran as ACCOUNT ROOT (arn:aws:iam::867500253271:root), which can write regardless — a policy bug would NOT have shown up in any of it. This criterion is genuinely open and can only close on the agent host once the key is created by hand. SIDE-EVIDENCE FOR bs-a4a (measured 2026-07-16, not theory): the REST endpoint serves HTTPS TODAY with no new infra — https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ returns 200 for both a template PNG and the deck HTML. So a4a option (1) is a config change (DECK_BASE_URL) whenever wanted, costing nothing. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- LAST CRITERION NOW VERIFIED 2026-07-17 — "Agent user can Put and Get but not Delete" is CONFIRMED. thomas created the access key by hand (per the design above, still not in Terraform) and an AWS CLI profile "cbc-wilm-agent" for verification. Probed against the real bucket with that profile, no longer as root: - sts:GetCallerIdentity -> arn:aws:iam::867500253271:user/cbc-wilm-agent (NOT root — the probe genuinely exercised the scoped policy for the first time). - PutObject _policy-probe/bs-crp-verification.txt -> 200. - GetObject -> 200. - ListBucket (prefix _policy-probe/) -> 200. Note the agent CAN list; only ANONYMOUS list is denied. Both are intended. - DeleteObject -> AccessDenied: "not authorized to perform: s3:DeleteObject ... because no identity-based policy allows the s3:DeleteObject action". Object survived a subsequent head-object. The implicit deny works. - OVERWRITE of the same key -> 200, content replaced. This is the one that actually matters for production: re-publishing a corrected deck for the same date replaces the object at the same URL, and it does NOT need DeleteObject. The no-Delete scoping does not break the correction workflow (bs-tiz.10 / harness system prompt both rely on this). Probe object cleaned up afterwards as root (the agent, correctly, could not remove it). ALL FOUR ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ARE NOW MET. Closing. CARRIED FORWARD to bs-tiz.6: the credential-chain foot-gun this issue's notes warn about is NOT yet mitigated in code. The key exists now and lives in a local AWS profile; on the host it must go in a root-owned 0600 systemd EnvironmentFile, and healthcheck should assert sts:GetCallerIdentity == cbc-wilm-agent so a stray AWS_PROFILE / env var cannot silently publish to the wrong account. That work is tracked on bs-tiz.6, not here.
close_reason: All four acceptance criteria met. The last one — 'agent user can Put and Get but not Delete' — verified 2026-07-17 against the real bucket as arn:aws:iam::867500253271:user/cbc-wilm-agent (not root) now that the access key exists: Put/Get/List 200, Delete AccessDenied by implicit deny, and same-key overwrite works so the re-publish correction workflow does not need DeleteObject.

title: Template-sync script (operator-run): upload templates/service/*.png to the S3 asset root
description:
The slide backgrounds are a small SHARED set that changes only when the operator edits or adds a template. A user-run npm script uploads templates/service/*.png to the same S3 asset root the renderer's --asset-base points at. Run MANUALLY when a template changes, NOT per deck. This is the piece that keeps per-deck publishing down to a single HTML upload (bs-tiz.10).

CORRECTED 2026-07-16: the description said '~13 PNGs'. It is actually 23 PNGs / 188MB. The count is higher because the welcome backgrounds have seasonal variants (4 seasons x 3 styles); a given deck uses only one season's worth, but ANY date may be built, so all 23 sync.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script makes every templates/service/*.png reachable under the configured asset base; re-running is idempotent; documented as the operator step to run after changing a template.
notes:
The PNGs this script uploads are the images html2canvas rasterizes at export time. They must be served with Access-Control-Allow-Origin or JPEG export from a cross-origin preview fails with a tainted-canvas SecurityError. CORS OWNERSHIP CORRECTED 2026-07-16: the note originally said this was owned by bs-tiz.10. It is not — the bucket CORS config landed in bs-crp (infra/s3.tf) and the crossorigin="anonymous" half in bs-517. Both are DONE; nothing to do here beyond uploading.

DECISIONS 2026-07-16 (thomas), before implementation:
- IMPLEMENTATION: an npm script wrapping the "aws s3 sync" CLI, NOT scripts/sync-templates.js with @aws-sdk/client-s3. Rationale: the repo has zero AWS npm deps and would gain one; more importantly "aws s3 sync" gives idempotency (size+mtime), parallel upload of 188MB, and Content-Type detection FOR FREE. A hand-rolled PutObject defaults to binary/octet-stream unless ContentType is set explicitly — exactly the bug class that makes images silently not render.
- SIZE/OPTIMIZATION IS OUT OF SCOPE: sync what is on disk today. The 71MB-per-deck page-weight problem is filed as bs-9x5 with the measurements. Keeping it out stops .11 becoming an image-pipeline task and unblocks the bs-tiz.10 + bs-517 live verification now.
- GLOB *.png, NOT *: there is a .DS_Store in templates/service/.
- NO --delete: bs-crp deliberately grants the agent no DeleteObject. The operator may run this with admin creds so --delete would work for them, but the no-delete design is intentional; a renamed template orphaning its old object is harmless. "Idempotent" here means re-running is a no-op, not that it prunes.
- KEY PREFIX must be templates/service/ to match config.deck_asset_base() = ${DECK_BASE_URL}/templates/service (bs-tiz.10). If these drift, every background 404s.

IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-16 (commit 5e43bfa). scripts/sync-templates.sh + "npm run sync-templates" (-- --dry-run supported). Cache-Control public,max-age=86400: a day, NOT a year, because these filenames are NOT content-hashed — editing hymn-1.png reuses the same URL, so the max-age bounds how long a corrected template can keep looking uncorrected. Sync is size+mtime based, so a fresh clone (new mtimes) re-uploads once; harmless, and preferable to --size-only, which would MISS a same-size edit.

TWO BASH BUGS, both found by RUNNING it rather than reading it, both worth remembering:
(1) the DECK_BUCKET grep against .env exits 1 when the key is absent, and under "set -e" that killed the script SILENTLY before any output. Not an edge case — any .env predating bs-tiz.10 lacks the line, so this was the common path. Needs "|| true".
(2) macOS ships bash 3.2, where "set -u" treats expanding an EMPTY array as an unbound variable. Only the REAL sync tripped it; the dry run had an element in the array and passed. Needs the ${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"} idiom. Lesson: a dry-run passing does not mean the real path works.

EVIDENCE: 23 objects up, 0 .DS_Store, Content-Type image/png (the thing "aws s3 sync" bought us), Cache-Control honored, ACAO * returned on a cross-origin GET, re-run = 0 uploads in 0.5s vs 72s cold. All 12 unique backgrounds referenced by the live 2026-06-28 deck return 200.
close_reason:
Implemented + verified live (commit 5e43bfa). All acceptance criteria met: all 23 templates reachable under the configured asset base (the 12 backgrounds the live 2026-06-28 deck references all return 200), re-running is idempotent (0 uploads in 0.5s vs 72s cold), documented in README as the operator step after changing a template. Content-Type image/png and ACAO * confirmed on the wire.

--force JUSTIFIED: bd blocked this on bs-crp still being open. That dependency existed so the bucket would exist before anything synced to it — and it does; the sync ran against it successfully. bs-crp remains open only for an ORTHOGONAL criterion (agent IAM user can Put/Get but not Delete), which cannot be tested until the agent's access key is created by hand on the agent host — it currently has zero keys. Nothing about that gates .11's work, which is done.

title: Publish tool: upload a generated deck to S3 and return its public URL
description: A tool the agent runs when a deck is ready to share with the minister. It renders (or takes the already-rendered) service-preview.html with the asset base pointed at the S3 template root, uploads the HTML to a date-keyed path in the existing public bucket (e.g. s3://<bucket>/decks/<date>/index.html), and returns the public https URL for the email reply. Per-deck upload is EXACTLY ONE HTML object — templates are synced separately and rarely (see the template-sync issue), and there are no per-deck images and no data-URIs. Bucket, path prefix, and asset base are config (env), not code, because the external URL may change.
design: Content is not sensitive, but do not make it a browsable archive: disable bucket directory listing and use date-keyed, hard-to-enumerate paths. Emit absolute image URLs via the asset-base seam so the HTML renders from the bucket with no local server. Design paths as PERMANENT — an emailed link lives in the mailbox forever; a stable date-based scheme lets a future CloudFront+custom-domain front keep old links working.
acceptance_criteria: Running the tool for a deck uploads a single HTML object, prints the public URL, and that URL renders with correct backgrounds in a browser with no local server running. ALSO: the bucket (or its CDN front) returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin on template-image responses, and JPEG export via the Export button is VERIFIED from the hosted S3 URL — not just locally — because cross-origin template images can taint the html2canvas canvas and make canvas.toBlob() throw a SecurityError (export fails while the deck still looks correct on screen).
notes: ENV/INVOCATION design (2026-07-16, confirmed w/ thomas). Single origin var DECK_BASE_URL = public bucket/CDN origin (e.g. https://<bucket> or a CloudFront domain). The publish tool COMPOSES from it and passes --asset-base EXPLICITLY as a CLI arg to build-deck.js — never relies on .env bleeding into the Node subprocess (nothing loads .env into Node's process.env; the env-file plumbing is Python-side only): asset-base = ${DECK_BASE_URL}/templates/service ; deck link = ${DECK_BASE_URL}/decks/<date>/index.html . PUBLIC_BASE_URL is REMOVED/superseded by DECK_BASE_URL (update .env.example + agent config.py public_base_url->deck_base_url). DECK_ASSET_BASE (read by build-deck.js, bs-tiz.9) stays ONLY as a manual/dev script override, documented in .env.example as optional; the tool does not use it. The templates path (/templates/service) must match where bs-tiz.11 uploads.  ||  IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-16 (commit 2a03bed). agent/src/email_agent/publish.py: publish_deck(deck_json) -> {url,bucket,key,date}; SDK tool mcp__deck__publish_deck wired into harness via mcp_servers={'deck': ...}. DECK_BASE_URL/DECK_BUCKET/DECK_PREFIX in config + .env.example; PUBLIC_BASE_URL removed. 16 unit tests (S3 client + subprocess injected) incl. one that runs the REAL build-deck.js so a --asset-base rename cannot pass silently. KEY DESIGN: publish RE-RENDERS from deck JSON to a temp dir rather than uploading passages/<date>/service-preview.html — that local file is built with the default /templates/service asset base and would host with every background 404. Local preview left untouched. config deck_* fields use default_factory (a bare os.getenv default is evaluated once at IMPORT, so Config() would ignore env — same reason subject_pattern already did this).  ||  VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-16 (partial, per thomas's call to defer): example deck published to s3://cbc-wilm-agent-public/decks/2026-06-28/index.html; curl returns 200, Content-Type text/html; charset=utf-8, Cache-Control public max-age=300 (300s NOT immutable, deliberately — a corrected deck re-publishes to the SAME url and must not serve stale). HTML carries absolute bucket-origin img srcs, 37 crossorigin=anonymous, ZERO local /templates paths. STILL OUTSTANDING (both need bs-tiz.11 templates in the bucket): (1) backgrounds actually rendering, (2) JPEG Export from the hosted URL + from a local preview pointed at the S3 base — converges with bs-517's remaining criterion. CAVEAT: local smoke test ran as ACCOUNT ROOT (arn:aws:iam::867500253271:root), NOT the cbc-wilm-agent user, so it did NOT exercise the scoped IAM policy — root can write anything, so a policy bug would not have shown. Real credential check must happen on the agent host.
close_reason: ACCEPTANCE MET + VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER 2026-07-16 (thomas confirmed render AND Export). Commits 2a03bed (tool) + 8311cdb (https origin fix). Every criterion demonstrated live, not inferred: - Uploads EXACTLY ONE HTML object and prints the public URL: decks/2026-06-28/index.html, Content-Type text/html, Cache-Control max-age=300 (300s, deliberately not immutable — a corrected deck re-publishes to the SAME url and must not serve stale). - That URL renders with correct backgrounds in a browser with NO local server running: CONFIRMED after the https fix. All 12 unique backgrounds 200, 0 insecure refs. - Bucket returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin on template-image responses: CONFIRMED (ACAO * on a cross-origin GET). - JPEG export via the Export button VERIFIED FROM THE HOSTED S3 URL, not just locally: CONFIRMED, no SecurityError. (The local-preview-pointed-at-S3 case also passes — see bs-517.) - Not a browsable archive: anonymous ListBucket returns 403 AccessDenied; paths are date-keyed. THE ONE THAT NEARLY SHIPPED BROKEN — read before touching DECK_BASE_URL. The first published deck used the http website endpoint as its origin. This tool bakes that origin into every AT RENDER TIME, so opening the deck over https made the browser block all 37 backgrounds as insecure mixed content: perfect text, perfect layout, no images, NO ERROR ANYWHERE. It survived a full round of curl-based verification because every object returned 200 individually — and 200-per-object does not imply the page renders. Caught only when a human opened the URL. Fixed via bs-a4a (https REST endpoint) and pinned by tests asserting the origin is https and never an s3-website host. LESSON FOR RE-VERIFYING THIS: status codes are not evidence of rendering. This deck's failure signature IS "structurally correct with the images gone". STILL UNTESTED, and it belongs to bs-crp: every AWS call in this verification ran as account ROOT, not the cbc-wilm-agent IAM user, which still has ZERO access keys. The scoped publisher policy has never been exercised by anything — a policy bug would not have surfaced in any of the above. Must be checked on the agent host once the key is created by hand. --force JUSTIFIED: bd blocked on bs-crp being open. That dependency existed so the bucket would exist before publishing to it — it does, and publishing works. bs-crp stays open ONLY for the orthogonal IAM-user criterion above, which cannot be tested from here and does not gate this tool's work.

title: build-deck.js: configurable media asset base (decouple image paths from serving root)
description: The renderer hardcodes image src as /templates/service/ (the bg() helper at scripts/build-deck.js:463), which assumes the deck is served from the same origin/root as the template PNGs. To publish decks to object storage (S3) independently of where the agent runs, the renderer must emit media paths from a CONFIGURED base. Add a --asset-base CLI flag (and matching env, e.g. DECK_ASSET_BASE) that prefixes every media reference. When set to a full origin (e.g. https:///templates/service) the emitted become ABSOLUTE URLs, so the HTML renders correctly no matter where the file itself is opened (email client, bucket root, sub-path, local disk). This is the single seam that decouples the deck HTML from its serving location.
design: Change only bg() and thread the base through. Default MUST remain the literal '/templates/service' so existing local Express serving AND the golden tests (tests/build-deck.test.js + tests/golden/*) stay byte-for-byte identical when the flag is unset. Absolute-URL mode is opt-in via the flag/env.
acceptance_criteria: bg() reads from a configurable base; with the flag unset the golden output is reproduced byte-for-byte; with a full-URL base every is an absolute URL; a unit test pins both modes.
notes: Export interaction: once the asset base points at a cross-origin S3 URL, the background images become cross-origin. The Export button's html2canvas bakes those images into each JPEG, so the bucket MUST send Access-Control-Allow-Origin or canvas.toBlob() throws (tainted canvas). Same-origin '/templates/...' (the default) never hits this; it only appears once decks are hosted. CORS config + a hosted-export test live on bs-tiz.10.
close_reason: Implemented --asset-base + DECK_ASSET_BASE; default byte-identical (golden tests green), full-origin yields absolute URLs, trailing slash normalized; verified via npm test (16/16) and CLI e2e. Unblocks bs-tiz.10/.11.

title: Eval: prove the model adds a caesura when the report asks for one
description:
The caesura loop has two halves. The SCRIPT half is proven (tests/build-deck.test.js: an unmarked over-wide line shrinks the song and the report names the line + the fix). The MODEL half is NOT.

In the 7/12 eval the agent looked up two new hymns and both happened to fit at 60px, so report.typography was empty and it was never asked to mark anything. So we have not yet seen the model: (a) read a 'shrunk' typography entry, (b) place a '|' at the line's sense-break in songs/*.md, (c) rebuild and get back to 60px, (d) mention the split in its reply so the operator can move a badly-placed marker.

That loop is the whole reason the mechanism exists — the script measures, the model judges. Until it is exercised, 'the model proposes the caesura' is a design intention, not an observed behaviour.

HOW: add an eval fixture whose flowchart names a hymn with a genuinely long line that the agent must look up fresh (so it writes the song file itself). Assert the resulting song file contains a '|', the report's typography kind is 'caesura' not 'shrunk', and the size is 60px. Consider also asserting the break lands at a sense-break rather than the midpoint — probably by pinning the expected split for that one known hymn.
acceptance_criteria: An eval shows the agent placing a caesura in a song file it wrote, keeping the song at 60px, and mentioning the split in its reply.

title: Agent output can be blocked by content filtering (verbatim lyrics)
description:
An eval run of the 7/5 flowchart died mid-run with 'API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy'. The agent sent NO reply; the run simply ended.

TRIGGER (probable): the agent's core job is reproducing song lyrics verbatim into songs/*.md. The 7/5 flowchart is all patriotic hymns (Star-Spangled Banner, Battle Hymn of the Republic, America the Beautiful, My Country 'Tis of Thee). Long verbatim lyric output looks like copyrighted-material reproduction to an output filter. NONDETERMINISTIC — the same eval passed twice before this and 6/8 tests passed on the failing run.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the one failure mode that produces SILENCE. The minister emails on Saturday, the agent dies, and nothing comes back. The dispatcher's failure path (bs-tiz.2) should catch it — agent error -> thread out of in-flight -> 'I hit an error' reply — but that path has NOT been exercised against this specific failure, and if the error arrives as an assistant TextBlock rather than an exception, the harness may treat it as a normal (empty) completion instead of an error. VERIFY THAT.

MITIGATIONS TO CONSIDER:
1. Confirm harness.py raises AgentError on a filtered/errored run rather than completing silently. The run must reach the dispatcher's failure path.
2. Lyrics are written to songs/*.md with the Write tool — consider whether writing them via a tool call (rather than emitting them in prose) is less likely to trip the filter, and prefer that path.
3. The reply itself should never quote lyrics back; it should reference songs by title.
4. Retry once on a filtered run before giving up.

tests/eval/eval_harness.py:EvalRun.error now surfaces this so it stops masquerading as 'the agent chose not to reply'.
acceptance_criteria: A service whose songs are COPYRIGHTED (not public-domain) is processed end to end: the agent reads the thread, writes the lyrics into songs/*.md, builds and publishes a correct deck, and replies — without a content-filter 400 stopping it. Failing politely is already delivered by bs-9ed and is NOT what this issue is about.
notes:
SEVERITY REDUCED after checking the production path — it is NOT silence.

A content-filtered run ends without calling send_reply or skip_reply, which trips the 'if not terminal' guard at harness.py:151 -> AgentError -> the dispatcher's failure path (bs-tiz.2): thread marked failed, claim released, message retried on the next tick. This is exactly the case bs-tiz.4's design note anticipated ('Deciding NOTHING is the error, because the dispatcher's commit boundary would drop the request silently'). The guard earns its keep here.

So the real-world behaviour is: the run dies, and the next heartbeat retries it. Since the filter is nondeterministic, a retry will often succeed. Remaining work is therefore hardening, not rescue:
1. The retry is currently unbounded-ish — confirm a filtered thread cannot retry forever, and that a repeatedly-failing thread eventually emails 'I hit an error' rather than looping quietly.
2. Reduce the trigger: prefer writing lyrics via the Write tool over emitting them in prose, and never quote lyrics back in the reply body (reference songs by title).

Observed once in 8 eval runs (~12%), on the all-patriotic-hymns 7/5 flowchart.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

RETRY BOUND SPLIT OUT 2026-07-16 as bs-9ed (P1), which ANSWERS item 1 above. The answer is bad: verified by reading store.py + dispatcher.py during the bs-tiz.6 pre-deployment review, there is NO attempt counter in the schema at all, mark_failed() increments nothing, and the 'I hit an error' reply this issue's acceptance criteria assumes DOES NOT EXIST. A filtered thread CAN retry forever — for the full 7-day gate window, one full Sonnet run at a time.

That behaviour is generic to every persistent failure, not just content filtering, so it now lives on bs-9ed and is a bs-tiz.6 deployment blocker. Note this means THIS issue's acceptance criteria cannot be met until bs-9ed lands: the 'reaches the dispatcher's failure path' half is already true (verified), but the 'results in an I hit an error reply, never silence' half is bs-9ed's to deliver.

What REMAINS here is item 2, trigger reduction, which is genuinely a1f-specific: prefer writing lyrics via the Write tool over emitting them in prose, and never quote lyrics back in the reply body (reference songs by title).

================================================================
2026-07-26 PRODUCTION INCIDENT — two mitigations above are DISPROVEN
================================================================
Six 400s across two threads, both retired to the apology. Journal:
  11:21/11:23/11:28  thread 19f95387567d275e msg 19f9e252615fabcb -> GAVE UP
  12:15/12:18/12:19  thread 19f9e5592103ca17 msg 19f9e5592103ca17 -> GAVE UP

DISPROVEN #1 — "prefer the Write tool over emitting lyrics in prose."
Attempt 2 (session e87f1819) blocked ON a Write call:
  [38] Write one-day.md              -> OK  (public_domain: true)
  [40] Write how-firm-a-foundation.md -> OK  (public_domain: true)
  [42] API Error: Output blocked by content filtering policy
The tool-call path trips the filter exactly like prose. Item 2 of
"MITIGATIONS TO CONSIDER" is not a mitigation. Do not build on it.

DISPROVEN #2 — "NONDETERMINISTIC, a retry will often succeed."
True for the 7/5 patriotic-hymn case (1-in-8). NOT true here: 6/6
attempts failed. What correlates is the song's copyright status, not
luck — the two writes that succeeded were public_domain hymns; the
block landed on the copyrighted contemporary set (The Lord Will
Provide / Goodness of God / All Hail King Jesus).

REFINED TRIGGER — it is not verbatim *reproduction from memory*.
The minister PASTED the licensed lyrics into the email and it still
blocked. Stronger: attempt 3 (session 8cebe443, 17 rows) blocked on
the FIRST assistant turn after mcp__gmail__get_thread, having written
nothing at all. Lyrics merely being in context is enough to put the
next turn at risk, whatever that turn contains. Exact offending tokens
are unrecoverable (blocked output is not captured), so the mechanism
(input-conditioned vs output-caught-early) is not established — but
the observable pattern rules out output-shaping as a fix.

CONSEQUENCE — this kills the "keep lyrics out of the model's output
path" class of fix generally, including a deterministic transcriber:
the agent still has to READ the thread. It also means bs-fsx (caesura
eval) cannot pass on the cloud model for a copyrighted song, since
placing a '|' requires the lyric line in context AND in output.

STILL TRUE: bs-9ed landed and works. Three bounded attempts, then the
fixed apology went out both times. Not silence. Journal legibility
(bs-zwj follow-up) also holds — the real message now surfaces instead
of "error result: success".

COLLATERAL: the run died mid-sequence, leaving songs/ half-written
(one-day.md + how-firm-a-foundation.md populated, four still stubs)
and passages/2026-07-26/ stale at the 7/24 title-only deck.

Remaining a1f-specific work moves to the transport layer -> see the
local-model fallback issue this now depends on.
================================================================
2026-07-29 — SCOPE AUDIT. This issue has no work of its own left.
Acceptance criteria rewritten to match what is actually true.
================================================================

Everything this issue originally proposed is now either DONE or DISPROVEN BY ITS
OWN NOTES. Recording that explicitly so nobody re-reads the MITIGATIONS TO CONSIDER
list above and builds from it — it is a historical record now, not a plan.

  1. "Confirm harness raises AgentError rather than completing silently"
     -> DONE. Verified: the terminal guard at harness.py:237 fires and reaches the
        dispatcher's failure path.
  2. "Prefer writing lyrics via the Write tool over emitting them in prose"
     -> DISPROVEN on 7/26. The block landed ON a Write call. Not a mitigation.
  3. "Never quote lyrics back in the reply body"
     -> Still good hygiene, but NOT a fix: attempt 3 blocked on the first assistant
        turn after get_thread, having written nothing. Lyrics merely being IN
        CONTEXT is enough.
  4. "Retry once on a filtered run before giving up"
     -> DONE by bs-9ed (three bounded attempts, then the fixed apology). Confirmed
        working in production both times on 7/26.

The old acceptance criteria ("...results in an 'I hit an error' reply, never
silence") was therefore ALREADY MET by bs-9ed and no longer describes anything
outstanding. It has been rewritten to describe the actual end state we want: not
"fail politely" but "produce the right deck anyway".

WHY THIS STAYS OPEN rather than being closed as superseded: it is the umbrella
problem statement — the licensed lyrics our church is entitled to display cannot be
processed by the agent at all — and it holds the 7/26 forensics that every
downstream decision rests on. It closes when a filtered run actually produces a
correct deck and reply, which is bs-dox's job. The dependency on bs-dox already
encodes that.

WHAT TO WATCH: the trigger correlates with COPYRIGHT STATUS, not with luck. The two
writes that succeeded on 7/26 were public_domain hymns; the block landed on the
contemporary set. So a green run on a patriotic or public-domain service proves
NOTHING about this issue — any verification must use copyrighted material. That is
why bs-e4m and bs-fxj both pin themselves to the known-bad 7/26 threads.

COLLATERAL STILL OUTSTANDING from the 7/26 run, unless someone has since fixed it:
songs/ was left half-written (one-day.md and how-firm-a-foundation.md populated,
four still stubs) and passages/2026-07-26/ was left stale at the 7/24 title-only
deck. Check before reusing either as a fixture.
close_reason:
Resolved 2026-08-02 by routing runs at a non-Anthropic endpoint (AGENT_BASE_URL, currently Moonshot / kimi-k3[1m]).

The filter is a property of the ENDPOINT, not the model — lyrics merely being in context trips it, so no prompt or output shaping avoids it, and fallback_model cannot help (it swaps models within Anthropic's API). Fixed once at the transport layer. Shipped in 5520919, documented in 8f5e4ad.

Verified end to end on the exact workload that failed: thread 19fc3e070fa4459f on 8/2 (one attempt, ~4 min, deck published, reply sent) and a re-run of the full 7/26 thread. Same mixed public-domain/copyrighted song set that produced six failures across two threads on 7/26.

NOT closed by this: bs-vhp (service-report.json still leaks lyric text — a separate channel, and it survives any endpoint choice) and bs-zzq (the is_error path still reports the useless word 'success'; re-scoped to journal legibility now that no fallback trigger depends on it).

The cost of the fix, recorded so it is not forgotten: thread contents now leave for a third party on every run, and it is pay-per-token where the subscription was not.
