title: Deployment host: always-on local box for the agent (CRON gate + dispatcher + agent); deck delivery decoupled to S3
description: REVISED 2026-07-15 (see specs/deck-publishing.md). The agent still needs one small ALWAYS-ON host — the user's home server / Raspberry Pi — to run the CRON heartbeat gate, the dispatcher, and the agent against a shared filesystem. What changed: deck DELIVERY is no longer served off this host. The original plan co-located an Express server and wrote service-preview.html into a served passages/ tree, with the reply link = https://<host>/passages/<date>/... and explicitly 'no upload step', reached by the minister over a tailnet. That is reversed: decks now PUBLISH to a public S3 bucket (bs-tiz.10) and the minister opens them on his phone over the public internet, so (a) the host does NOT need to serve decks to anyone but the operator, and (b) the minister needs NO tailnet/VPN access at all. The host may still serve the Bible Scroller app itself for the operator, but that is now separable from deck delivery. There IS a deliberate upload step now (bs-tiz.10 + bs-tiz.11).
design:
DELIVERABLE REDEFINED 2026-07-17 by thomas: an IDEMPOTENT IN-REPO INSTALL SCRIPT, not a runbook. This issue previously specified an outcome ("an always-on host runs the gate/dispatcher/agent") and its gap analysis asked for a "runbook" — human-readable steps. Taken literally that would have produced agent/README.md plus a unit file to copy by hand. That is NOT the goal. The goal is:

  1. git clone the repo on the homelab server
  2. create the AWS profile by hand (access/secret key for cbc-wilm-agent)
  3. run ONE script that installs prerequisites, wires the service, and registers the timer

TARGET, decided 2026-07-17 (do not re-ask): Debian/Ubuntu on x86_64. systemd TIMER, not crontab. The script INSTALLS missing prerequisites (node, uv) rather than asserting and failing.

IDEMPOTENCY IS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT, NOT A NICE-TO-HAVE. thomas will re-run this whenever anything changes. It has to be designed in from the first line: every step is check-then-act, re-running is a series of no-ops, and it must never duplicate a timer, append a second env line, or clobber a credential that is already correct. This is the single most important property of the deliverable.

WHY systemd TIMER OVER CRON (decided): journald gives logs you can actually read after a Saturday-night failure; cron's default failure mode is mailing output into the void. Persistent=true survives reboots. And the unit file is the natural home for the env that the two known foot-guns live in. heartbeat.py is already shaped for either (one poll->dispatch pass, exits 0/1, --dry-run), so no code change is needed to adopt the timer.

ENV ON THE HOST — the unit is where this is won or lost:
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be UNSET. It silently outranks CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and bills pay-per-token instead of the subscription. config.assert_subscription_auth() hard-fails on it, but the unit should scrub it rather than rely on the process dying.
- CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token` (~1yr).
- AWS: thomas is using a PROFILE (step 2), not an EnvironmentFile. That is fine — the root-as-default-profile hazard that makes healthcheck FAIL on his laptop does not exist on a box whose only profile is cbc-wilm-agent — but it carries its own FOOT-GUN: systemd does NOT inherit HOME, so boto3 silently cannot find ~/.aws/credentials unless the unit sets HOME or AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE explicitly, plus AWS_PROFILE=cbc-wilm-agent. Works by hand, fails as a service. The install script must set these in the unit and then PROVE it by running healthcheck AS THE SERVICE USER, not as the invoking shell.

VERIFICATION IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE, not an afterthought: the script must finish by running `healthcheck` in the service's own environment. healthcheck already covers all three credential classes (Claude, Gmail, AWS identity+Put/Get as of bs-sjz). An install that "succeeds" without that proof is the exact failure this whole epic is trying to avoid — everything green until fifteen minutes before a service.

UNDOCUMENTED HOST DEP, easy to miss: NODE is required at RUNTIME. publish.py shells out to `node scripts/build-deck.js`. A Python-only box installs cleanly, passes every Python check, and then fails at publish time — after the deck is built, at the worst possible moment. The script must install and verify node, and ideally exercise build-deck.js once.

CANNOT BE TESTED FROM THE DEV LAPTOP: it is darwin; the target is Debian+systemd. The script will be UNVERIFIED until it runs on the box. Design accordingly: a --check/--dry-run mode that makes no changes, loud failure over silent partial success, and idempotency so a half-run is recoverable by re-running.
acceptance_criteria: An idempotent in-repo install script takes a freshly-cloned repo on a Debian/Ubuntu x86_64 box (with the cbc-wilm-agent AWS profile already created by hand) to a running agent in ONE invocation: prerequisites (node>=18, uv, python>=3.11) installed or skipped if already satisfactory, dependencies synced, systemd service + timer written and enabled, env wired (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrubbed, HOME/AWS_PROFILE set so boto3 resolves the profile under systemd). RE-RUNNING IT IS A SERIES OF NO-OPS: no duplicate timer, no appended env lines, no clobbered credentials, exit 0. The script finishes by running healthcheck IN THE SERVICE'S OWN ENVIRONMENT and fails loudly if it is not HEALTHY. A --check mode makes no changes. The gate, dispatcher, and agent then run unattended with subscription OAuth auth, and a generated deck reaches the minister via a public S3 URL, openable on a phone with no tailnet membership. Serving the scroller app to the operator remains optional and independent.
notes:
AUTH on the host: authenticate the Agent SDK with a subscription OAuth token from 'claude setup-token' set as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. FOOT-GUN: ensure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is UNSET in the host/service environment — if present it silently wins over the OAuth token and bills a pay-per-token API account instead of the subscription. Bake an env-scrub / assertion into the service unit. (Subscription-vs-API decision recorded on the epic bs-tiz.)  ||  PUBLIC_BASE_URL is superseded by DECK_BASE_URL, owned by bs-tiz.10 — DONE and verified 2026-07-16.

GAP ANALYSIS 2026-07-16 (asked by thomas: "what do we have planned for setup/run instructions on the homelab box?"). Honest answer: THE DELIVERY HALF OF THIS ISSUE IS DONE, THE HOST HALF HAS NO PLAN WRITTEN DOWN. This issue is currently a decision record about what changed (S3), not a runbook. Nothing here is blocked on design — it is unwritten, not undecided.

WHAT IS ALREADY HOST-READY (better than expected):
- heartbeat.py is CRON-SHAPED BY DESIGN: one poll->dispatch pass, exits 0/1, has --dry-run. It is a drop-in for a systemd timer or a cron line; it does not need a supervisor loop.
- dispatcher.py holds a SQLite claim/lock, so overlapping runs cannot double-process a thread. Timer overlap is safe.
- healthcheck.py is the preflight for credentials that fail silently and on a delay.
- authorize.py handles Gmail consent.
- README documents the EnvironmentFile approach for the AWS key.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST:
1. NO SERVICE DEFINITION AT ALL. No systemd unit, no timer, no Dockerfile — nothing to systemctl enable. Verified by find: zero *.service/*.timer/Dockerfile in the repo.
2. NO ENTRY POINTS. pyproject has no [project.scripts], so invocation is 'uv run python -m email_agent.heartbeat' — fine by hand, but a unit file needs an absolute uv path + WorkingDirectory. Adding console_scripts would make the unit trivial.
3. NO RUNBOOK. No agent/README.md, no host setup steps. UNDOCUMENTED HOST DEPS, found by reading the code: NODE is required at runtime — publish.py shells out to 'node scripts/build-deck.js' (so a Python-only box silently fails at publish time, at the worst moment); plus uv/Python >=3.11. The AWS CLI is NOT needed by the agent (boto3 covers publish); it is only needed for the operator-run 'npm run sync-templates', which can run from a laptop.
4. HEALTHCHECK DOES NOT CHECK AWS. It covers Claude + Gmail only. AWS creds joined the silently-failing-on-a-delay class on 2026-07-16 when bs-tiz.10 landed, which is exactly what healthcheck exists for. THIS IS ALSO THE RIGHT HOME FOR bs-crp's LAST UNTESTED CRITERION ("agent user can Put and Get but not Delete"): that can only be exercised where the agent's key actually lives, and healthcheck already runs there. An sts:GetCallerIdentity asserting cbc-wilm-agent (bs-crp's notes suggest the service unit; healthcheck is better — it is the thing already built for this) plus a scoped Put/Get probe would close bs-crp and catch the AWS-SDK credential-chain foot-gun (env vars beat ~/.aws/credentials, so a stray AWS_PROFILE publishes to the wrong account).

HARD BLOCKERS FOR ACTUALLY RUNNING UNATTENDED, in order:
- bs-xy9 (P1): if the OAuth app is not really 'In production', the agent dies silently every 7 days. And its verification method is itself broken — see bs-qka (filed 2026-07-16).
- bs-crp: the agent's IAM key does not exist yet (zero access keys). Publishing has ONLY ever been exercised as account root. The scoped policy is entirely unproven.
- bs-9x5: not a blocker, but the first thing the minister will notice — 71MB per deck.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PRE-DEPLOYMENT REVIEW 2026-07-16 (thomas asked: are we ready to install on the homelab box?). The gap analysis above was RE-VERIFIED against the code and the live environment rather than taken on trust. Every claim in it held. Quality gates green at review time: 63 agent tests, 17 node tests.

RE-CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not by re-reading the notes:
- No service definition, no Dockerfile, no [project.scripts], no agent/README.md. Still true.
- bs-qka: token.json's mtime is 10:09 today and its access-token "expiry" field is 15:09Z — exactly one hour later. mtime tracks the last hourly access-token refresh, never consent. The refresh token's issue time is genuinely absent from the file (fields: account, client_id, client_secret, expiry, refresh_token, scopes, token, token_uri, universe_domain).
- bs-crp: "aws sts get-caller-identity" returns arn:aws:iam::867500253271:root, and "aws iam list-access-keys --user-name cbc-wilm-agent" returns an empty AccessKeyMetadata list. The agent's key still does not exist; the scoped policy remains entirely unproven.
- publish.py DOES shell out to "node scripts/build-deck.js" (publish.py:68-78). Node is a hard, undocumented runtime dep on the host.

NEW BLOCKER FOUND, not previously known: bs-9ed (P1) — there is no retry bound anywhere. store.py's schema has no attempts column and mark_failed increments nothing, so a persistently-failing message retries every tick for the full 7-day gate window, burning subscription quota, while the minister hears nothing. This is the one defect on this list that is CREATED by unattended operation: attended, a human notices and kills it; unattended, nobody does. Now a dependency of this issue.

REVISED BLOCKER ORDER FOR AN UNATTENDED TEST: bs-9ed (retry bound) -> bs-crp (create the IAM key by hand, prove Put/Get/no-Delete) -> bs-qka (fix the age check) -> bs-xy9 (which cannot be closed until qka is fixed). The runbook/service unit is then the LAST step, not the first: it should document a system whose failure modes are bounded, rather than freezing the current ones into a systemd unit.

STILL WORTH DOING WHEN THE RUNBOOK IS WRITTEN (from the gap analysis, unchanged): teach healthcheck to check AWS (sts:GetCallerIdentity asserting cbc-wilm-agent + a scoped Put/Get probe) — that closes bs-crp's last criterion and catches the AWS credential-chain foot-gun; add [project.scripts] entry points so the unit file is trivial; document Node + uv + Python >=3.11 as host deps.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2026-07-17 — TWO OF THREE BLOCKERS CLEARED. bs-xy9 CLOSED (OAuth app confirmed "In production" by direct console reading — the token-age proxy was never needed). bs-crp CLOSED (access key created by hand; scoped policy exercised as the IAM user for the first time: Put/Get/List 200, Delete AccessDenied, and same-key OVERWRITE works, so the re-publish correction workflow does not need DeleteObject). Remaining blockers: bs-9ed (retry bound) and bs-sjz (AWS healthcheck).

AWS IDENTITY ON THE HOST — a real runbook item, found by running the new check live. healthcheck now asserts sts:GetCallerIdentity ends in :user/cbc-wilm-agent and FAILS on anything else (bs-sjz). Verified live both ways: with AWS_PROFILE unset it correctly FAILS reporting arn:aws:iam::867500253271:root; with AWS_PROFILE=cbc-wilm-agent it passes and proves Put+Get.

Read that result carefully — it is a LAPTOP artifact, not a host prediction. thomas's laptop has root as the DEFAULT profile and the agent as a named one, which is why the check fails there without AWS_PROFILE set. The host should NOT be set up that way. The host must carry the agent key ONLY, as AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in a root-owned 0600 systemd EnvironmentFile (per bs-crp's design: the key stays out of Terraform state and out of the repo). With no other credentials present there is no root to fall back to and no AWS_PROFILE needed. If the runbook instead tells the operator to copy ~/.aws/credentials to the host, it reintroduces exactly the ambiguity the assertion exists to catch. The assertion is what makes either setup verifiable, so run healthcheck on the host after install.

Note healthcheck's AWS probe leaves one object at s3://cbc-wilm-agent-public/_policy-probe/healthcheck.txt, overwritten each run. It cannot clean itself up (no DeleteObject, by design) and the bucket is public-read, so keep the probe body boring — it is a timestamp today.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

INSTALL SCRIPT IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-17. scripts/install-agent-host.sh (694 lines, +x), agent/README.md, and [project.scripts] in agent/pyproject.toml (email-agent-heartbeat / -healthcheck / -authorize; the first two return int so console_scripts propagate exit codes, which is what makes the systemd verification meaningful). Suites green: 81 agent, 17 node.

IDEMPOTENCY MECHANISM, reviewed and confirmed real rather than claimed: units are rendered to a temp file -> cmp -> `install` ONLY if different; daemon-reload fires only if a unit actually changed; enable/start gated on is-enabled/is-active; the timer is restarted only when unit content changed, so a no-op run cannot reset the schedule under a run in flight. NodeSource list is rendered->cmp->written, never appended. uv/node skipped entirely when already satisfactory. `uv sync --frozen` always runs because it IS the reconciliation and is a no-op when .venv matches the lock. THE SCRIPT NEVER WRITES A SECRET — it asserts and leaves .env byte-untouched (verified by grep: the only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN writes are instruction strings printed to the operator).

BEST IDEA IN IT: env_block() is ONE function shared by the heartbeat unit and a generated healthcheck unit, and verification is `systemctl start --wait` on that healthcheck unit. So the proof runs in provably the SAME environment as the real service, not one that resembles it. That is what makes the HOME/AWS_PROFILE foot-gun actually defended rather than merely commented.

BUG FOUND IN REVIEW AND FIXED (assistant, not the subagent): under `set -euo pipefail` the EXIT trap's final status REPLACES the script's exit code. cleanup() ended in `[ -n "$TMPDIR_SELF" ]`, which is a FAILURE when the temp dir was never created — so `--help` exited 1. It bit only --help today (by --check's converged exit the tmpdir exists and rm succeeds), but it is a latent trap on every success path: any failed rm would make a converged --check report drift, which is the one thing --check's contract promises. cleanup() now ends `return 0`. Verified: --help 0, wrong-host --check 1, bad flag 1, shellcheck still clean.

CORRECTION TO THE SUBAGENT'S REPORT — do not propagate it. It reported "one real bug: .env re-injects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after systemd scrubs it, silently outranking the OAuth token and billing pay-per-token." The silence half is WRONG, measured not argued: config.assert_subscription_auth() RAISES on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and it is called in harness._run() before every agent run AND in healthcheck. An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env therefore produces a LOUD hard failure, never silent billing. The installer's refusal to install while .env declares it is still worth keeping — failing at install beats failing at 3am — but it is early-warning, not a billing hole being plugged. (It checks the key's presence, not its value.)

DECISIONS THE SUBAGENT MADE THAT THE BEAD DID NOT SETTLE, all accepted:
- Secrets stay in .env (config.py already load_dotenv's it; a second env source would create two sources of truth). The unit carries ONLY what .env cannot express: the boto3 resolution vars + the scrub.
- OnCalendar=*:0/1 rather than OnUnitActiveSec=60 — because Persistent= only applies to CALENDAR timers and is silently ignored on monotonic ones. The bead asked for both ~60s and reboot survival; only calendar syntax delivers both. Good catch.
- ExecStart uses the venv binary directly, not `uv run` — no lockfile resolution at service-start.
- Refuses to run as root (--user required, defaults to $SUDO_USER / repo owner): all three credential stores live in a user home.
- No apt Python: Ubuntu 22.04 ships 3.10, below requires-python; uv fetches one instead of adding a PPA.

STILL UNVERIFIED, and this is expected, not a gap: the dev box is darwin and the target is Debian+systemd, so every apt/NodeSource path, runuser, uv python install, all systemd behaviour, and healthcheck's live Claude/Gmail/AWS calls under the unit's env are UNTESTED until the script runs on the homelab box. Verified locally: bash -n, shellcheck 0.11.0 rc=0 (re-run independently by the assistant via npx), uv sync --frozen, all three console scripts resolve, `node scripts/build-deck.js examples/2026-06-28.deck.json` rc=0, units render with correct interpolation, exit codes correct on the failure paths. Run `--check` FIRST on the box: it makes no changes and reports drift. A half-run is recoverable by re-running — that was the design constraint throughout.

In the worked example His Name Is Jesus was mislabeled 'Special Music' — a small model would copy that. Clarify the distinction and the resulting slide treatment/background for each.

notes:
CONCRETE EVIDENCE (2026-07-12, found while adding the build-deck golden test in bs-66k): the ambiguity is real and already live in the reference deck.

examples/2026-06-28.deck.json encodes 'His Name Is Jesus' as type=special_music. The script therefore renders slide 22 on choir.png (what gen_service.md documents for special_music). The HAND-BUILT passages/2026-06-28/service-preview.html renders that same slide on praise-2.png — the congregational-praise background.

RESOLVED by examples/flowcharts.md + user confirmation 2026-07-12.

title: Spike: can the local 27B (Bonsai) drive the full agent loop end to end?
description:
SPIKE — the second half of the measurement, and only worth running if the frontier
model (the sibling spike) is not the answer: it failed, it is too expensive, or
Thomas would rather not send the minister's mail off-network.

THE QUESTION: can PrismML Bonsai 27B, via UniClaudeProxy at the claude-opus-5
alias, actually DRIVE THE FULL AGENT LOOP — Gmail MCP -> gen_service -> deck JSON
-> build-deck.js -> publish -> reply — on a real thread?

This is the risk bs-dox names and defers: "the remaining risk is purely CAPABILITY
... not whether the plumbing works." The plumbing is proven (a real SDK run wrote
probe.txt with correct tool arguments and returned is_error=False). Nobody has
asked the 27B to do anything harder than that. Multi-step tool use over a long
context is exactly where a small model degrades, and the agent's job is ~40 tool
calls deep.

METHOD: identical to the frontier spike — same throwaway options.env patch, same
known-bad 7/26 threads (19f95387567d275e, 19f9e5592103ca17), same four things
recorded. Only AGENT_MODEL changes, to the proxy alias that routes to Bonsai
(currently claude-opus-5 — that alias is the PROXY's key, not a real Anthropic
model, and it is volatile; confirm before running).

WATCH FOR, specifically, the small-model failure modes:
  - Does it read the whole thread with mcp__gmail__get_thread, or answer from the
    newest message alone? (SYSTEM_PROMPT step 1 exists because this is hard.)
  - Does it invent lyrics it does not have? SYSTEM_PROMPT step 4 forbids this and
    it is the single worst outcome — wrong words on a sanctuary screen, sent
    without a human in the loop. A model that hallucinates a verse here disqualifies
    itself no matter how good the rest of the run looks. CHECK THE LYRICS WORD BY
    WORD against the minister's email, do not eyeball the deck.
  - Does it end on exactly one of send_reply / skip_reply, or wander until the
    harness:237 terminal guard fires?
  - Context headroom — the 7/26 transcript was ~175KB of JSONL. Where does Bonsai
    start degrading?

DECISION THIS FEEDS: if Bonsai cannot drive the loop, bs-dox's Approach A
(whole-run fallback) is dead as designed, and the fallback becomes Approach B —
cloud model orchestrates, only the lyric-touching work routes to the local model.
That is a materially different design and bs-dox should be rewritten, not patched.
Do not build Approach B pre-emptively; this spike is what tells you whether you
need it.
acceptance_criteria: A documented run of the known-bad 7/26 material through Bonsai on the proxy, recording: content-filter 400 encountered (expected: no); run reached exactly one of send_reply/skip_reply; lyrics in songs/*.md checked WORD BY WORD against the minister's email with zero invented text; deck JSON valid; published URL resolves. Plus a stated verdict on whether Approach A (whole-run fallback) is viable or bs-dox must be rewritten as Approach B.
notes:
================================================================
2026-07-30 — REFRAME. Do not run this as written; the question changed.
================================================================

This spike asks whether Bonsai can drive the FULL agent loop, as the rescue path for
a provider fallback. bs-e4m has since removed the reason to care: provider-swapping
does not clear copyright guardrails (gpt-5.6-terra refuses deterministically; cloud
Sonnet does not), so there is no fallback for Bonsai to be the target of. Running a
27B through a 40-tool-call loop to answer a question we no longer need answered is
not worth the Sunday risk it would take to trust.

WHAT BONSAI IS ACTUALLY WELL-SUITED FOR, per bs-8qs: the REDACTION CLASSIFIER.
Deciding which blocks of a minister's email are lyric text and which are prose or
instructions is one bounded call — no multi-turn tool use, no session resume, no
dependence on proxy translation fidelity for complex payloads, and a wrong answer is
caught by a test rather than emailed to a congregation. It is also the one place a
local model has a genuine advantage: the classifier necessarily sees the lyrics, and
a local model has no copyright guardrail to trip.

RESCOPE THIS ISSUE to that, or close it in favour of a task under bs-8qs. Do not run
the full-loop version. If it is rescoped, the useful measurements become: does it
segment a mixed prose/lyric email correctly, does it over- or under-redact, and how
does it behave on the messy real 7/26 email rather than a clean fixture.

Note also that Bonsai was still down at test time ("All connection attempts failed"),
so nothing here has actually been measured yet.

title: UniClaudeProxy: non-streaming tool_use.input is {} (streaming path is fine)
description:
EXTERNAL DEFECT — lives in UniClaudeProxy (http://192.168.0.48:9223), not in this repo. Blocks bs-dox: the local-model fallback cannot work until this is fixed, because the Agent SDK's entire loop is tool calls.

SYMPTOM: the proxy returns a structurally valid Anthropic tool_use block with the correct tool NAME and stop_reason 'tool_use', but `input` is ALWAYS an empty object.

REPRODUCTION (verified 2026-07-28 from the agent host, 3/3 runs empty):

  curl -s -X POST http://192.168.0.48:9223/v1/messages \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5","max_tokens":300,
         "tools":[{"name":"write_file","description":"Write text to a file.",
           "input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{
             "path":{"type":"string"},"content":{"type":"string"}},
             "required":["path","content"]}}],
         "tool_choice":{"type":"tool","name":"write_file"},
         "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write hello world to /tmp/a.txt using the write_file tool."}]}'

  -> {"content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_...","name":"write_file","input":{}}],
      "stop_reason":"tool_use", "usage":{"output_tokens":130,...}}

Both required params are missing. Forcing tool_choice does not help.

LIKELY CAUSE: OpenAI returns tool arguments as a JSON *string* —
  {"function":{"name":"write_file","arguments":"{\"path\":\"/tmp/a.txt\"}"}}
Anthropic expects `input` as a parsed *object*. If the proxy passes the arguments
string through without json.loads(), or reads the wrong field, the result is
exactly {}. Supporting evidence: output_tokens=130 for a call whose visible
payload is `{}` — the model plainly generated the arguments and they were
discarded in translation. Plain text generation round-trips fine, so this is
specific to the tool-call path.

NOT a model-capability problem, most likely: the model picked the right tool name
unprompted, which is the harder half of the task.

WHY P0: every capability the agent uses is a tool — Read, Write, Edit, Bash, and
mcp__gmail__get_thread. With empty inputs the fallback agent cannot read the
minister's email, cannot write songs/*.md, and cannot reply. It would fail worse
than the content filter it is meant to rescue us from, and would do so silently-ish
(valid-looking turns that accomplish nothing).

NEXT STEPS
1. Inspect UniClaudeProxy's OpenAI->Anthropic response mapper for the tool-call
   branch; confirm whether `arguments` is being json.loads()'d into `input`.
2. Re-run the curl above; assert input == {"path":"/tmp/a.txt","content":"hello world"}.
3. Then re-test a two-turn round trip: send a tool_result back and confirm the
   proxy accepts Anthropic-shaped tool_result blocks on the REQUEST side too.
   Request-direction translation is untested and could be broken independently.
acceptance_criteria: A POST to /v1/messages with a tool definition returns tool_use blocks whose input contains the populated arguments matching input_schema, and a follow-up request carrying an Anthropic tool_result block is accepted and answered.
notes:
================================================================
2026-07-28 (later) — NOT A BLOCKER. Scope is narrower than filed. P0 -> P3.
================================================================
After Thomas tweaked the tool translation settings, re-probed and isolated it:
the bug is confined to the NON-STREAMING response path.

STREAMING WORKS — the arguments are all there, as input_json_delta fragments:
  content_block_start -> {"type":"tool_use","name":"echo_text","input":{}}
  content_block_delta -> partial_json: "{"
  content_block_delta -> partial_json: "\"text\":\""
  content_block_delta -> partial_json: "banana"
  content_block_delta -> partial_json: "\""
  content_block_delta -> partial_json: "}"
  content_block_stop
Concatenated: {"text":"banana"} — exactly correct.

So the proxy streams the fragments correctly but does not ACCUMULATE them into
tool_use.input when assembling a non-streamed response. The bug is in the
non-streaming aggregation, not in the OpenAI->Anthropic argument translation as
originally guessed.

MODEL IS NOT AT FAULT: asked to emit the same JSON with no tools declared, it
returned {"path":"/tmp/a.txt","content":"hello world"} perfectly.

WHY THIS NO LONGER BLOCKS bs-dox: the Claude Agent SDK streams. Verified end to
end (see bs-dox notes) — a real SDK run against the proxy produced
Write(file_path='./probe.txt', content='banana'), wrote the file, and returned
is_error=False. The dependency from bs-dox has been removed.

Still worth fixing eventually: any non-streaming caller of this proxy gets silent
argument loss. Not our path, so demoted to P3.
close_reason:
No longer blocks anything — closing as won't-fix on our side.

This was an EXTERNAL defect in UniClaudeProxy (non-streaming tool_use.input always {}), filed because it blocked bs-dox's local-model route. That route is gone: Moonshot speaks Anthropic's /v1/messages natively, so there is no translating proxy in the path at all.

The finding is still worth keeping for whoever next reaches for an OpenAI-shaped backend: a proxy can look completely healthy on plain text and still fail on every tool call, which is the entire Agent SDK loop. That warning now lives in .env.example next to AGENT_BASE_URL.

Reopen if the LAN/local-model route is ever revived (see the SHELVED banner in specs/lyric-ingestion.md).

title: state.db: record which backend served a thread's session
description:
threads.session_id records the Claude Code session to resume, but not WHICH backend
produced it. Once a run can fall back from the Anthropic API to another provider, a
thread's transcript can have mixed provenance, and resuming it against the wrong
backend is at best a cold prompt cache and at worst incoherent.

Record the backend that served a thread's session, set it when a session is
created, and have the dispatcher pin a thread to that backend for its remaining
turns rather than silently bouncing between endpoints.

Touches: agent/src/email_agent/store.py (schema), dispatcher.py (pass the backend
through to run_agent), harness.py (select env by backend).

*** THE MIGRATION QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED — DO NOT ADD A COLUMN TO `threads`. ***
The original text of this issue said "check how store.py creates tables before
adding a column". The answer is written down in the file, at store.py:85-93, and it
is a hard NO:

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS threads (...)

against an existing DB is a SILENT NO-OP. A column added to that statement never
appears on any deployed state.db, and every read of it raises OperationalError on
the one box we cannot watch. bs-9ed hit exactly this and solved it with a new
TABLE instead — message_attempts — precisely because IF NOT EXISTS creates a new
table cleanly and leaves existing rows untouched. No ALTER TABLE, no version stamp,
no backfill.

Follow that precedent: a `thread_backend` side table keyed by thread_id, with an
absent row meaning 'anthropic' (the correct reading for every thread that predates
the fallback). That also makes the change reversible and keeps `threads` untouched.

state.db currently holds live thread state for 7 real threads; do not blow it away.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR THE FALLBACK — dependency from bs-dox removed 2026-07-29.
The fallback happens INSIDE a single run_agent call, so a thread resumed on the
wrong backend costs LATENCY (it re-trips the filter and falls back again), not
retry attempts — the bs-9ed 3-attempt bound is unaffected. This is a coherence and
prompt-cache fix worth doing on its own merits; it was blocking the only work that
actually helps on a Sunday, which was the wrong ordering.

RELATED OPEN QUESTION, owned by bs-dox: on fallback, does the re-run resume the
SAME session_id (inheriting a transcript written by another model and ending in a
filter abort) or start fresh (redoing the work cold)? Whichever bs-dox decides
determines what 'the backend that served this thread' even means for a mixed run,
so read that decision before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: The backend that served a session is recorded (in a side table, not a new threads column) and a thread resumes on the backend that served it. An existing state.db upgrades in place without losing thread rows — verified against a copy of the real 7-thread state.db, not a fresh one.

title: Harden gate against agent-authored mail (reply-loop defence-in-depth)
description:
The reply-loop bug (agent replying to its own replies) was fixed on 2026-07-11 at the DISPATCHER layer: tools.send_reply records the sent message id via store.mark_agent_sent(), so is_processed() rejects it. That is correct and is covered by a mutation-checked regression test (agent/tests/test_reply_loop.py).

But the guard is only in the dispatcher, which leaves two rough edges:
1. The gate still emits agent-authored messages as 'actionable' on every tick and the dispatcher discards them — correct but wasteful (observed: gate saw 3 actionable, dispatcher processed 0).
2. The guard is STATE-dependent. Wiping or losing state.db would make the agent's own past replies look like fresh requests again and re-trigger the loop on an existing thread. The state store is bookkeeping, so treating it as a safety mechanism is fragile.

Harden at the gate so the invariant holds without state: e.g. skip messages whose From is the authenticated user AND that carry the SENT label (safe in production, where the minister's mail is inbound-only), or track authored Message-IDs, or bound the query to messages newer than the thread's last agent reply. Note the self-email test case defeats naive From/label filtering — every message carries both SENT and INBOX.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting state.db and re-running the heartbeat against an already-answered thread does not send a duplicate reply.
notes:
LARGELY ADDRESSED 2026-07-12, but by steering rather than by a gate — which is the better fix. The original framing of this issue (harden the deterministic filter) accepted a flawed premise: the agent had no way to judge for itself, because (a) it was handed a single msg_id, never the thread, and (b) the system prompt COMPELLED a reply ('never finish silently'), so declining was structurally impossible. Authorship tracking was therefore load-bearing safety, which is too much weight for bookkeeping.

Now: get_thread gives the agent the whole conversation with authorship as an explicit HINT (documented as fallible), and skip_reply makes 'no reply is warranted' a first-class terminal outcome. The harness accepts send_reply OR skip_reply; only deciding NOTHING is an error.

VERIFIED LIVE with state.db DELETED (every authored_by_agent flag false): the agent read the thread, recognised its own prior replies from their content, and declined 3/3 times — explicitly reasoning 'replying again would just be me answering myself' and 'to avoid perpetuating the loop'. No mail sent. This is precisely the state-loss scenario this issue was filed for.

REMAINING (why this stays open, at lower priority): the gate still emits agent-authored messages every tick and the dispatcher discards them — correct but wasteful, and each one that reaches the agent costs a Sonnet call to decide 'no'. Worth a cheap gate-level filter as an efficiency measure, but it is no longer a SAFETY issue: correctness now rests on the agent's judgment, with the store as a cheap fast-path and a hint.

title: Vendor html2canvas locally (drop the cdnjs dependency in the slide template)
description: The service-slides template loads html2canvas from cdnjs (the export-to-image button). In the S3 + phone delivery model the CDN works fine (internet is guaranteed for the minister, and the export button is an operator tool run locally with internet), so this is NOT on the critical path — captured for completeness. Vendoring the one file removes the last external dependency, so a deck renders and exports with no internet at all (e.g. if ever served from an offline box).
